title: CI hardening follow-up: security-scanner install + CI-aware scan test + CodeQL continue-on-error
detail:
PR #35 (iterate-2026-05-18-fix-launch-blocker-tests) fixed the 17 launch-blocker test failures, but activating the CI workflows (launch Step 4) surfaced CI-environment issues the dormant workflows had masked.

CI run on PR #35 failed:
  1-3) plugins/shipwright-security tests/test_oss_backend_smoke.py (semgrep / gitleaks / trivy smoke tests) hard-fail in CI because ci.yml runs the security plugin's tests but never installs those scanners - only security.yml does. Per ADR-044 these tests fail-loud in CI by design.
  4) tests/test_run_scan_and_report.py::test_full_evidence_retains_raw_secret_fields fails: the scanner refuses --full-evidence when CI=true and the test does not handle that guard.

CodeQL run failed separately: 'Advanced Security must be enabled for this repository' - codeql.yml lacks the continue-on-error guard security.yml already carries for private repos without code scanning.

Fix scope: (a) ci.yml installs semgrep/gitleaks/trivy before the plugin-test loop (mirror security.yml), or skip the tool-dependent security tests in the basic CI job; (b) make test_full_evidence_retains_raw_secret_fields CI-aware; (c) add continue-on-error to codeql.yml's analyze/upload step, or enable GitHub code scanning in repo settings (resolves on going public). Decided as follow-up: user chose 'merge #35, rest as follow-up'.

title: write_decision_drop.py not worktree-aware — F3 decision-drops lost on worktree cleanup
detail: Since unconditional worktree isolation (ADR-049), iterate F3 writes the decision-drop into the WORKTREE's .shipwright/agent_docs/decision-drops/. That dir is gitignored by design (launch-prep plan: drops are 'Staging', aggregated into decision_log.md). But write_decision_drop.py uses project_root/.shipwright/... directly — NOT worktree-aware — so the drop lands in the worktree and is destroyed by 'git worktree remove' before /shipwright-changelog's aggregate_decisions.py can fold it into decision_log.md. Net effect: every iterate ADR since ADR-049 is silently lost from decision_log.md aggregation. Fix: make write_decision_drop.py resolve the MAIN repo via git-common-dir and write the drop there, mirroring record_event.py / resolve_events_path (ADR-050). The gitignore decision stays unchanged. Identified during iterate-2026-05-18-phase-quality-check-fixes (PR #37).

title: SBOM cluster: non-determinism + broken cleanup launch-payloads
detail: Two real bugs in SBOM subsystem (ADR-056) surfaced during 2026-05-22 bloat-cleanup follow-up. (1) Non-determinism: consecutive sbom.md regenerations produce structurally different output — 'Unique licenses: 3 (Apache-2.0, MIT, unknown)' vs 'Unique licenses: 2 (MIT, unknown)' for the same monorepo. License resolver appears to read venv state non-reproducibly. (2) Broken cleanup launch-payload: the auto-emitted hint 'cd plugins/<x> && uv sync && update_compliance' for trg-95fba1e3 (requests) and trg-db49aad2 (google-genai) does NOT clear the items — uv sync resolves dep graph but doesn't add license metadata that the SBOM resolver picks up; packages stay 'unknown'. Either the resolver is broken (should read PKG-INFO/METADATA from site-packages directly) or the launch payload is misleading. Fix needed analogous to d325fd6 (deterministic-render-timestamps): pin SBOM resolution to uv.lock or installed METADATA, NOT live venv probe. Two follow-up iterates needed: (A) SBOM determinism, (B) SBOM license-resolver actually reads PKG-INFO.

title: [P3.2] Code-Simplify Skill (standalone, behavior-preserving)
detail:
## Intent

P3.2 (OS1) from Spec/external-frameworks-integration.md. Standalone Code-Simplify Skill that runs behavior-preserving refactors. Five Osmani principles (Preserve Behavior, Follow Conventions, Clarity over Cleverness, Maintain Balance, Scope to What Changed) + Chesterton-Fence check + behavior-snapshot test (run full test suite before+after, reject if behavior diff).

## Files

Decision in iterate (choose ONE):
(a) Sub-skill: plugins/shipwright-iterate/skills/iterate/references/F-simplify.md (NEW) — triggers when iterate intent is 'simplify X' / 'clean up Y' / 'refactor Z'.
(b) Mini-plugin: plugins/shipwright-simplify/ (NEW directory with full plugin scaffolding) — exposed as /shipwright-simplify slash command.

Recommend (a) for speed; (b) only if /shipwright-simplify should be discoverable as its own command.

## Acceptance

title: finalize_iterate work_completed event lands uncommitted in main tree during worktree iterates (never enters the PR)
detail:
## Summary

During a **worktree-based iterate** (the default since `setup_iterate_worktree.py`),
the `work_completed` event that `finalize_iterate.py` (F5b) records into
`shipwright_events.jsonl` lands **only as an uncommitted line in the MAIN
tree's working copy**. It is in no commit, never enters the iterate PR, and
requires a separate manual `chore(events): record evt-... for iterate-...`
commit (F7) to persist. F7 is documented as "skip unless replaying", so it is
routinely skipped -> the canonical event log silently misses entries and
`shipwright_events.jsonl` shows as dirty (`M`) at the start of essentially
every session.

This is an audit-log / compliance-integrity bug: `traceability-matrix.md`,
`change-history.md`, and the build dashboard all derive from the event log,
so a missing `work_completed` event means the iterate is invisible to those
artifacts unless someone notices the dirty file and hand-commits it.

## Symptom

- `git status` in the consuming project's main tree perpetually shows
  `M shipwright_events.jsonl`.
- The latest iterate's `work_completed` event is present in the working copy
  but absent from `HEAD:shipwright_events.jsonl`.
- A recurring stream of `chore(events): record evt-XXXX for iterate-YYY`
  commits exists purely to backfill these (8+ in shipwright-webui history:
  68a8965, f88a4e8, 5ff5c3e, 2159acd, bb37b4f, 0d1702a, ...).

## Root cause (3-way file mismatch)

Reproduced in shipwright-webui iterate-2026-05-27-transcript-renderer-scroll.
Line counts of `shipwright_events.jsonl` across the lineage:

| Ref | lines | last event id | has the new evt? |
|-----|-------|---------------|------------------|
| iterate commit (in worktree) | 164 | evt-ecf57fd9 (stale base) | no |
| merge-of-main commit | 165 | evt-18779597 | no |
| HEAD (after PR merge) | 165 | evt-18779597 | no |
| MAIN-tree working copy | 166 | evt-126ed67f | YES (uncommitted) |

1. `finalize_iterate.py` records the event by **appending to the main tree's**
   `shipwright_events.jsonl`. The events-log path resolves to the git
   *common-dir* (main tree), NOT the worktree -- even when
   `SHIPWRIGHT_PROJECT_ROOT` is exported to the worktree absolute path (the
   env override is honored for decision-drops / changelog-drops / iterate
   entries, but the events append still hits the main tree).
2. The iterate's F6 commit happens **in the worktree**, whose
   `shipwright_events.jsonl` is a different (stale-from-branch-base) file, and
   the F6 explicit `git add` list never includes `shipwright_events.jsonl`.
   So the event cannot enter the PR.
3. Net: the canonical `work_completed` event exists only as an uncommitted
   line in the main tree. `git log -S <evt-id>` may falsely appear to find it
   in the iterate commit -- that match is the event id echoed in the staged
   `.shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/<run_id>.json` + `session_handoff.md`,
   NOT in `shipwright_events.jsonl`.

## Reproduction

1. Start any iterate (worktree is created by `setup_iterate_worktree.py`).
2. Run finalization through F5b (`finalize_iterate.py`).
3. `cd` to the MAIN tree, `git status` -> `M shipwright_events.jsonl`,
   `git diff shipwright_events.jsonl` shows the +work_completed line.
4. The iterate branch / PR contains no events.jsonl change.

## Proposed fixes (pick one; (a) preferred)

- **(a) Honor the worktree for the events append.** Make
  `finalize_iterate.py` write the `work_completed` event to the SAME project
  root used for the other artifacts (respect `SHIPWRIGHT_PROJECT_ROOT` /
  `--project-root` for the events log too, not the git common-dir). Then F6
  stages it like every other artifact and it ships in the PR. Cleanest;
  removes the F7 backfill entirely for worktree iterates.
- **(b) Stage events.jsonl in F6.** Have the iterate F6 commit step always
  `git add shipwright_events.jsonl` when dirty in the worktree. Only works if
  (a) is also done (the event must be in the worktree copy first).
- **(c) Make F7 mandatory.** Drop the "skip unless replaying" carve-out so the
  `chore(events)` commit always runs post-merge. Keeps the main-tree-append
  model but guarantees the commit. Least clean (extra commit per iterate,
  direct-to-main).

## Affected files (shipwright shared tooling)

- `shared/scripts/tools/finalize_iterate.py` (events-append path / root
  resolution) -- primary.
- `shared/scripts/tools/record_event.py` (F7 out-of-band recorder) -- if (c).
- The iterate SKILL F6/F7 reference docs (`shipwright-iterate` plugin:
  `references/F6.md`, `references/F7.md`) -- update the staging/commit rule.
- `check_iterate_isolation.py` -- consider asserting the events.jsonl entry is
  committed (not just present) at F11 to fail-closed on this class of drift.

## Acceptance criteria for the fix

- AC1: After a worktree iterate's F6 commit, `HEAD:shipwright_events.jsonl`
  in the merged result contains the `work_completed` event for that run_id.
- AC2: The main tree's `shipwright_events.jsonl` is clean (`git status` shows
  no `M`) after finalization -- no orphaned uncommitted lines.
- AC3: No separate `chore(events)` backfill commit is required for a normal
  worktree iterate.
- AC4: `verify_iterate_finalization.py` "events.jsonl has commit" check is
  tightened to assert the event is in a COMMIT, not just the working copy.

## Evidence

- Consuming project: shipwright-webui, run_id
  `iterate-2026-05-27-transcript-renderer-scroll`, event `evt-126ed67f`,
  commit `7573e84a00cd8984ecc53455bca42c32e6725be3` (PR #81, merged
  2026-05-29). The event is uncommitted in shipwright-webui's main tree at
  time of writing.
- Related, same mechanism: ADR decision-drops also resolve to the main tree
  (mitigated there because `decision-drops/` is gitignored + consumed on main
  at /shipwright-changelog time). The events.jsonl case is worse because the
  file is TRACKED, so the drift is a real uncommitted-diff, not a benign
  local-only artifact.

title: F-group / source=compliance triage items never auto-dismiss outside /shipwright-compliance
detail: GAP: audit_detector.run(emit_to_triage=True) is the ONLY path that runs mirror_findings_to_triage (the auto-dismiss-when-finding-cleared logic in plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/audit/audit_detector.py). That run() is invoked ONLY by the explicit /shipwright-compliance skill. No Stop hook, SessionStart hook, finalize_iterate, or update_compliance.py calls it. Consequence: any source=compliance triage item (F2/F4/F5/F6/F7, B-group, etc.) stays in status=triage until someone manually runs /shipwright-compliance, even after the underlying finding is fixed. EVIDENCE: in shipwright-webui, F4-F7 lingered ~24h after PR #55 cleared them (had to dismiss manually); an F2 item sat stale from 2026-05-14 for over a week. Every OTHER triage producer (phaseQuality via audit_phase_quality_on_stop, github via import_github_findings SessionStart, test-failure + sbom via update_compliance) has a frequent automatic trigger; the compliance-audit producer is the lone exception. NOT solved by PR #78/#79 — those fixed E1-E5 compliance-MD STALENESS false-positives via single-producer + snapshot-provenance, a different concern; they do not touch the F-group emit/dismiss path. RECOMMENDED FIX (Option A1 from the 2026-05-23 design discussion): add shared/scripts/hooks/audit_compliance_on_stop.py modeled on audit_phase_quality_on_stop.py (same Stop contract: never-block, idempotent per HEAD-sha+session, greenfield-safe, opt-out via SHIPWRIGHT_COMPLIANCE_AUDIT_ON_STOP=0). It calls audit_detector.run(emit_to_triage=True). Wire into plugins/shipwright-iterate + plugins/shipwright-changelog hooks.json Stop chains, ordered AFTER finalize + phase_quality and BEFORE aggregate_triage_on_stop. MUST run the FULL audit (groups A-G): mirror_findings_to_triage auto-dismiss is groupless, so running only group F would erroneously dismiss B7/B2/etc. (scoped auto-dismiss = a separate follow-up, Option A2). Do NOT touch the #78 snapshot-provenance E-staleness machinery. Worktree note: triage.jsonl is gitignored + per-worktree, so the hook only cleans the local tree it fires in; cross-worktree triage sync is out of scope (Option C, separate iterate). Priority is now MEDIUM not HIGH because #78 removed the loud recurring E-staleness noise; F-group items are rarer (only on real ADR/CLAUDE.md/architecture hygiene regressions).

reason: Fixed: events.jsonl is now a per-tree, PR-committed artifact (PR #111, iterate-2026-05-29-events-jsonl-worktree-commit). AC1-AC4 all met and verified on origin/main; evt committed in HEAD, main tree clean, no chore(events) backfill, verifier asserts committed.

title: Framework .gitignore artifact rules do not propagate to consuming projects (no canonical template; adopt/project only check coverage)
detail:
## Gap

Framework-added .gitignore rules for .shipwright/ artifacts do NOT propagate to consuming projects — neither existing nor newly-adopted ones.

Root cause:
- shared/templates/shipwright-gitignore.template is a 3-line orphan (loop.lock + runs/ only) and is applied by nobody.
- /shipwright-adopt only CHECKS coverage (gitignore_check.py majority_gitignored ratio + check_paths_against_gitignore report) and hard-enforces only .env.local (secrets). It does NOT write the canonical .shipwright artifact-ignore block (the !/.shipwright/agent_docs/ whitelist + decision-drops/visual/runtime/ re-excludes).
- /shipwright-project writes no .gitignore entries at all.
- Shipwright own .gitignore is hand-maintained; runtime/ was added by ADR-089 (2026-05-27) and is drift-guarded by test_runtime_dir_gitignored.py — but that test covers the FRAMEWORK repo only (REPO_ROOT=shipwright), not consuming projects or any template.

Symptom (found 2026-05-29): shipwright-webui missed /.shipwright/agent_docs/runtime/ → the 3 Stop-hook runtime files (build_dashboard/session_handoff/triage_inbox) showed as untracked clutter. Patched manually in webui (commit f6e34a6). That patch is a symptom-fix; this item is the systemic fix.

## Proposed fix
1. Flesh out shared/templates/shipwright-gitignore.template into the FULL canonical .shipwright artifact-ignore block (SSoT) incl. runtime/.
2. Make /shipwright-adopt AND /shipwright-project idempotently MERGE that block into the target .gitignore (add missing lines, no duplicates) — not just check coverage.
3. Drift-test: template <-> framework .gitignore artifact block stay congruent (a future ADR adding a gitignored dir must update the template -> auto-propagates).
4. Optional: adopt/iterate gitignore self-heal that back-fills missing canonical rules into EXISTING projects (would have caught webui runtime/).

## Affected
shared/templates/shipwright-gitignore.template, plugins/shipwright-adopt/scripts/lib/gitignore_check.py (+ a new writer), plugins/shipwright-project scaffolding, new drift-test under shared/tests/.

title: WebUI triage flip does not regenerate triage_inbox.md (Stop-hook-only trigger)
detail:
Gap: A WebUI triage status flip (dismiss/promote/snooze) appends a status event to <project>/.shipwright/triage.jsonl (so the live view via GET /api/triage/:id is correct), but does NOT regenerate the committed .shipwright/agent_docs/triage_inbox.md. That markdown is refreshed ONLY by the Stop hook aggregate_triage_on_stop.py (registered LAST in plugins/shipwright-iterate/hooks/hooks.json), which fires at Claude-session end -- never on a WebUI/browser action (no Claude session is involved). So between a WebUI triage action and the next Claude-session Stop in that project, the WebUI live view and triage_inbox.md diverge.

Evidence (shipwright-webui, observed 2026-05-30): triage_inbox.md header 'Auto-generated 2026-05-27T07:43'; latest triage.jsonl status event 2026-05-27T15:01; no regeneration since, despite later WebUI activity.

Why it matters: triage_inbox.md is git-tracked and is the anchor target for compliance RTM deep-links (FAIL -> [trg-XXX](../agent_docs/triage_inbox.md#trg-XXX), rtm_generator.py). A stale snapshot means RTM links point to cards already dismissed, or 404 the anchor for items appended after the last Stop.

Scope: framework (shipwright monorepo), NOT the webui repo -- the regeneration trigger + render logic live in shared/scripts/tools/aggregate_triage.py + shared/scripts/hooks/aggregate_triage_on_stop.py. The WebUI (read-mostly observer) has no path to invoke it.

Candidate fixes (decide during the run):
A) Instant sync -- expose aggregate_triage as a thin invokable the WebUI server calls (subprocess) after each status flip. Keeps Python as the single render source of truth. Cost: python-runtime dependency in the Hono server + Windows subprocess fragility + expanded webui write surface (triage_inbox.md becomes a webui-written file). REJECT a TS reimplementation of render_markdown (guaranteed drift vs the canonical Python renderer).
B) Framework-only -- leave regeneration at Stop time but make the staleness explicit/bounded: WebUI surfaces 'snapshot may lag; live view is authoritative', and/or add a standalone regenerate entrypoint (CLI / cron). Lower effort, no instant sync.

Recommendation: B is proportional -- the WebUI live view is already the authoritative inbox; triage_inbox.md is a derived cache. Choose A only if RTM deep-link freshness BETWEEN sessions is a hard requirement.

Do NOT 'remove the item from triage.jsonl' -- the log is append-only / event-sourced by design (audit trail of who dismissed what and why). The current dismiss behavior (append a status event, last-status-wins on read) is correct and must stay.

Filed from a shipwright-webui session on 2026-05-30 at user request (Sven).
launchPayload:
Framework change in the shipwright monorepo. Entry points:
- shared/scripts/tools/aggregate_triage.py (render_markdown)
- shared/scripts/hooks/aggregate_triage_on_stop.py (Stop-time trigger)
- plugins/shipwright-iterate/hooks/hooks.json (Stop chain)
Follow shared/prompts/writing-plugin.md. After editing plugins/shared, run:
  bash scripts/update-marketplace.sh && uv run scripts/check_plugin_cache_sync.py --strict

reason: By design: triage_inbox.md is a derived cache. The RTM (rtm_generator.py:_open_triage_by_fr) and the live WebUI view both read triage.jsonl directly (last-status-wins), so the cache lag is cosmetic and no RTM link breaks. Rejected option A (instant sync); option B regenerate CLI (aggregate_triage.py --project-root) already exists. Full rationale in Claude memory: triage-inbox-md-derived-cache (project_triage_inbox_md_derived_cache.md).

title: CI quick-wins: un-swallow integration-test failures + fix F821 Path import
detail: TWO verified-safe ci.yml/test fixes, bundle into ONE iterate (no debt-paydown needed). (1) .github/workflows/ci.yml line ~74: the integration-tests step ends in '|| true', so integration FAILURES are swallowed and CI stays green. Verified: integration-tests currently 136 passed / 0 failed, so removing '|| true' is risk-free and makes the layer actually gate. (2) shared/tests/test_events_log.py: 14x ruff F821 'Undefined name Path' — the file uses Path only in lazy annotations (has 'from __future__ import annotations') without importing it; add 'from pathlib import Path'. Not a runtime bug (file passes) but removes the F821 noise so lint enforcement (separate item) is cleaner. AC: '|| true' gone from integration step; ruff F821 count = 0; integration + test_events_log green.

title: Wire shared/ tests into CI (collection-collision + 4 stale shared tests)
detail: ROOT systemic gap: ci.yml plugin-test loop only iterates plugins/*/tests/ + integration-tests/, so shared/scripts/**/tests/ and shared/tests/ NEVER run in CI (this is why the 7 record_event tests fixed in iterate-2026-05-30-record-event-test-failures rotted unseen). Wiring is non-trivial in TWO ways. (a) Collection collision: 'pytest shared/tests shared/scripts/tests shared/scripts/tools/tests' together raises 11 ModuleNotFoundError (duplicate top-level 'tests' package between shared/tests/ and shared/scripts/tests/). Workaround: run each dir as a SEPARATE pytest invocation (like the per-plugin loop), or rename/namespace the packages. (b) Running per-dir reveals 4 MORE stale/red shared tests that must be fixed first, else the new CI step is born red: shared/scripts/tests/test_validate_env.py::TestValidateBuild::test_all_vars_present + ::test_partial_vars; shared/tests/test_architecture_md_reflects_arch_impact.py::test_every_arch_impact_drop_has_architecture_md_entry; shared/tests/test_artifact_path_canon.py::test_no_legacy_artifact_paths[compliance-migrated]. AC: those 4 root-caused+fixed (stale vs real?), shared dirs collect+pass per-dir, ci.yml runs them. Supersedes/enriches trg-f363b1ab.

title: Enforce ruff lint in CI (pay down 262 findings, then un-neuter)
detail: ci.yml line ~33: 'uv run ruff check . || true' AND 'continue-on-error: true' — lint is DOUBLE-neutralized, gates nothing, despite 'lint' being in the job name. Current state: ruff check . reports 262 findings (sample: 14x F821 undefined-name [all in test_events_log.py, see quick-wins item], 12x E741 ambiguous-var-name, E701/E401/F811/E731). 176 are --fix auto-fixable. PLAN: (1) decide rule set (ruff config in pyproject? currently none beyond defaults), (2) auto-fix the safe ones, manually resolve the rest (esp. confirm the F821 are all annotation-only / not real), (3) remove BOTH '|| true' and 'continue-on-error: true' so lint actually gates. Large debt-paydown — own iterate. AC: ruff check . exits 0; ci.yml lint step gates (no || true / continue-on-error).

title: Introduce Python type-checking in CI (the job name claims type but none exists)
detail: The ci.yml job is named 'Python (lint + type + test)' but there is NO type-checker configured ANYWHERE (no mypy/pyright/ty in pyproject.toml, no CI step). The 'type' claim is fiction. PLAN: pick a checker (recommend Astral 'ty' for uv-native speed, or pyright), add minimal config (start lenient: check shared/ + plugins/*/scripts/, ignore tests), pay down the surfaced errors incrementally (likely many on a large untyped codebase), then add a gating CI step. Large — own iterate, can be staged (e.g. type-check only changed files first). AC: a type-checker runs in CI and gates; the job name is truthful.

title: CI extension guard: assert all test dirs covered + no silent un-gating
detail: WHY THIS EXISTS: ci.yml was authored as 'dormant' (commit 4107a6b, early-access) with || true + continue-on-error baked in, then only PARTIALLY hardened (2671c69/d85210f added scanners+CI-aware-tests+CodeQL guard but left lint/integration/shared/type loose). No guard prevents this recurring. BUILD a meta-check (shared test or a tiny CI-lint script run in CI) that fails when: (a) any test directory under plugins/*/tests, shared/**/tests, integration-tests/ is NOT referenced by a CI pytest invocation (catches a new plugin/shared dir silently uncovered — the 'CI extension' guard you asked for); (b) any gating step (test/lint/type) carries '|| true' or 'continue-on-error: true' outside a documented allowlist (allow: codeql analyze + security SARIF-upload/scan steps, which are intentionally non-gating on private repos). ALSO fold in two known loose gates to verify/track: security.yml critical-gate reads 0 criticals when findings.json is ABSENT (scanner crash => silent green) — make missing-file fail or warn-loud; codeql.yml analyze has continue-on-error (documented, private-repo) that MUST be removed at public launch. AC: the guard fails on an injected || true and on an uncovered test dir; security missing-findings no longer passes silently; codeql launch-gate tracked.

reason: Won't-do (pragmatic, solo/small-team target): full static type-checking on a mature un-annotated scripts codebase is a perpetual annotation tax for marginal ROI. Tests + ruff F-rules (undefined-name, redefinition, unused) already cover the realistic bug surface. The only real issue — the misleading 'type' in the CI job name — is folded into the lint item (rename job to lint+test).
Re-scoped: enforcing the full ruff default set (262 findings, mostly style noise) is over-rigor for the target audience. Superseded by a pragmatic curated-ruleset item.

title: Enforce a pragmatic ruff ruleset in CI (bug-focused, not full default set)
detail: ci.yml line ~33 neuters lint twice ('ruff check . || true' + 'continue-on-error: true') so it gates nothing, despite 'lint' in the job name. PRAGMATIC plan for solo/small-team (NOT the full 262-finding default set): (1) add a ruff config in pyproject.toml selecting a BUG-FOCUSED ruleset — pyflakes F (F821 undefined-name, F811 redefinition, F401 unused-import, F-string issues) plus a light, high-signal slice of E/W; explicitly skip purely-cosmetic rules that just create churn. (2) 'ruff check --fix' the freebies (~176 auto-fixable), manually clear the rest of the SELECTED set. (3) remove BOTH '|| true' and 'continue-on-error: true' so lint gates. (4) While in this job: rename it from 'Python (lint + type + test)' to 'Python (lint + test)' since type-checking is a deliberate won't-do (see dismissed trg-84f204ba). AC: ruff check . exits 0 against the curated ruleset; lint step gates; job name no longer claims type.

title: plugin_sync_reminder_on_stop files its triage item in the worktree log (ephemeral), not the main repo -- does not survive iterate-worktree sessions
detail:
## Bug

`shared/scripts/hooks/plugin_sync_reminder_on_stop.py` (SP4 Stop hook) appends its `source=plugin-sync` / dedupKey `plugin-sync:cache-drift` triage item via `_emit_triage(project_root, ...)`, where `project_root = _resolve_project_root()` -> `lib.project_root.resolve_project_root()`. In an iterate-worktree session that resolves to the WORKTREE root (`.worktrees/<slug>`), so the item lands in `.worktrees/<slug>/.shipwright/triage.jsonl` -- a gitignored, per-tree, ephemeral log discarded on `git worktree remove` after PR merge. It never reaches the durable main-repo `.shipwright/triage.jsonl` that the WebUI / RTM read.

Result: the docstring promise ('a triage item has been filed so it survives the session') is FALSE for iterate-worktree sessions -- the durable follow-up handle is lost on worktree cleanup. The block-once Stop reminder banner still fires (the live nag works); only the audit/follow-up item evaporates.

## Evidence (2026-05-30, observed live)
- iterate-2026-05-30-gitignore-canon-propagation ran in `.worktrees/gitignore-canon-propagation`.
- Its reminder item landed there as trg-b860a99e; `grep -c plugin-sync` on the main-tree `.shipwright/triage.jsonl` = 0.
- Contrast: the gap item trg-afce5459 (source=manual) correctly lived in the main-tree log and survived for the user to ask about.

## Root cause
`_resolve_project_root()` returns the active SDLC project context (the worktree) -- correct for the reminder banner + once-per-session sentinel, but WRONG for the durable triage append. Triage items are an append-only audit trail and must live in the MAIN repo log.

## Proposed fix
Resolve the MAIN repo root for the `_emit_triage` append only -- mirror the decision-drop pattern (`shared/scripts/lib/events_log.resolve_main_repo_root`, git-common-dir) that already writes decision-drops to the main tree from inside a worktree. Keep `_resolve_project_root()` (worktree) for the banner + `_claim_reminded` sentinel. e.g. `_emit_triage(resolve_main_repo_root(project_root) or project_root, rel_paths)`.

## Affected
- shared/scripts/hooks/plugin_sync_reminder_on_stop.py (_emit_triage target)
- reuse shared/scripts/lib/events_log.resolve_main_repo_root (existing main-root resolver)
- new test under shared/tests/ (worktree fixture: assert the item is appended to the main-repo log, not the worktree log)

## Notes
- Monorepo-dev only (is_monorepo gate) -> end-user projects unaffected.
- The mis-filed item from this session (trg-b860a99e) was dismissed in the worktree log; it vanishes with the worktree.
- Filed at user request (Sven), 2026-05-30, from the iterate-2026-05-30-gitignore-canon-propagation session.

REMAINING: C3 (FR-gate finalize bypass + D3 same-event), C4 (sub-iterate A = backfill events for the 4 ci/docs drift commits + G2 board + reopen FR link, webui repo). The monorepo Group E + webui B7/A5.0 symptoms should auto-dismiss on next producer run. Two detective checks assumed the old model and the audit's uv-run invocation assumed a Python project env, producing recurring FALSE-POSITIVE compliance findings in BOTH repos that the #132 per-project disabled_checks band-aid only MASKED.

VERIFIED EVIDENCE (this session):

title: Campaign lifecycle status (draft -> active -> complete) — make a campaign identifiable as running vs not
detail: Add a campaign-level status field so consumers (WebUI Campaigns lane + CLI campaign_progress summary) can tell whether a campaign is started or just planned. Today only per-step status exists; done/total is derived, so a freshly-created/hand-authored campaign (all steps pending) is indistinguishable from one that is actively running, and it shows up everywhere immediately. Changes: (1) campaign_init.py init_campaign writes top-level status:'draft' into status.json AND status: draft into the campaign.md frontmatter. (2) campaign_progress.py: add a 'start' (or set-status) subcommand that sets the top-level status to 'active'; when update-status makes all sub_iterates complete, set status:'complete'; the 'summary' command prints the top-level status. (3) The autonomous campaign loop sets status='active' at run start and 'complete' at finalize. (4) Backward-compat: a missing status field means legacy — consumers fall back to the current done<total behavior so nothing existing breaks. Lifecycle: draft (planned, lives only in triage) -> active (started, shown on the board) -> complete (hidden). Counterpart already being built in shipwright-webui: the Campaigns lane filters the board on status==='active' (draft/complete hidden), with the legacy no-status fallback. Decision recorded in webui design session 2026-06-03 (Option B, draft hidden = triage-only).

title: Harden compliance A5: verify the security critical-gate actually BLOCKS, not just that the step exists
detail: Group A5 audits the deployed .github/workflows/security.yml by grepping for the shipwright-critical-gate step id (CRITICAL_GATE_STEP_ID) — it confirms the step is PRESENT but never that it WORKS. The 2026-06-04 false-green was a gate whose step existed yet could never block (read SARIF security-severity at result-level instead of rule-level). Harden A5 to execute the gate shell against fixture SARIF (rule-level >=9.0 -> blocks; empty/invalid -> fail-closed; clean -> passes) so a structurally-broken DEPLOYED gate is caught. Root-cause fix shipped PR #144; shared/tests/test_security_critical_gate.py already covers the TEMPLATE, A5 should cover the deployed file.

title: security.yml fetch-depth:0 comment is vestigial — no scanner is diff/history-aware
detail: shared/templates/github-actions/security.yml.template (and the deployed shipwright-webui copy) checkout with 'fetch-depth: 0  # full history for diff-aware secret scans', but NO scanner uses git history/diff: gitleaks runs --no-git (filesystem), semgrep 'scan --config auto .' and trivy 'fs .' scan the working tree. The full-history fetch is unnecessary AND correlated with a transient merge-ref gitleaks false positive on shipwright-webui PR #103 (cafebabe:deadbeef surfaced from a stale merge ref, now allowlisted via .gitleaks.toml). Either drop to fetch-depth:1 (current tree only) or fix the misleading comment. Low priority.

title: Gitleaks smoke test silently SKIPS in CI: same-version gitleaks finds the synthetic PEM locally but 0 in CI
detail: plugins/shipwright-security/tests/test_oss_backend_smoke.py::test_gitleaks_detect_scans_committed_shipwright_dir uses a positive-control gate: if gitleaks does not find src/main_key.pem it pytest.skip()s (allow-silent-skip). It SKIPS in every CI run (e.g. 26941507522, 'Got paths: []') while semgrep+trivy smoke tests pass -- so gitleaks' real detection + node_modules-exclusion contract is NEVER exercised in CI. Investigated 2026-06-04: reproduced the synthetic fixture (BEGIN/END RSA PRIVATE KEY + short body) committed in a git repo and ran the EXACT _run_gitleaks invocation (gitleaks detect -s <repo> --config <generated allowlist with [extend] useDefault=true>). LOCAL gitleaks 8.21.2 (Windows) detects it (1 finding, rule=private-key, entropy 4.64) WITH and WITHOUT the allowlist config; CI gitleaks 8.21.2 (Linux) finds 0. Ruled out: fixture content, allowlist config. NOT reproducible on this Windows host -> needs a Linux repro / a temporary CI diagnostic step. Candidate causes: win-vs-linux binary default-ruleset divergence; gitleaks git-mode behavior on a root commit in the CI env; or _run_tool error handling swallowing a gitleaks failure. Possible direction: if the positive control cannot be made reliable, the silent skip should become a CI-fail per the ADR-044 silent-skip discipline so the coverage hole is visible rather than hidden. Same win/linux gitleaks divergence was also seen with the sidekiq-secret rule on shipwright-webui PR #103 (cafebabe:deadbeef).

title: Durable producer-maintained campaign status (tracked SSoT)
detail: Campaign per-sub status is read by the WebUI from an untracked, never-committed status.json; the tracked campaign.md table is write-once 'pending' (campaign_progress updates status.json only) -> board shows stale/wrong status on a fresh clone / deployed WebUI. title: Bloat session-marker not worktree-aware: false Stop-block after ADR-documented baseline bump in a worktree iterate
detail: bloat_gate_on_stop.py + the PostToolUse bloat recorder store MAIN-root-relative paths (.worktrees/<slug>/...) in the session marker .shipwright/locks/bloat_pending.<sid>.json, then look them up in shipwright_bloat_baseline.json (which keys repo-relative paths, no .worktrees/ prefix). For a worktree iterate that grows an ALREADY-baselined file, this (a) mis-classifies the anti-ratchet as delta=crossing at write and (b) false-blocks Stop as a not-in-baseline crossing at read -- even when the committed baseline + the CI anti-ratchet gate (which read the worktree baseline) correctly PASS. Repro: iterate-2026-06-05-fr-linkage-lifecycle (campaign 2026-06-02 C3) bumped test_finalize_iterate.py 306->464 + test_audit_groups_a_d.py 748->789 under ADR-096; CI 'Anti-ratchet + allowlist diff' passed but the Stop gate blocked on '.worktrees/.../test_finalize_iterate.py'. Workaround used: rm the stale 1h-TTL session marker. Fix: strip the '.worktrees/<slug>/' prefix (or resolve the worktree baseline + worktree-relative path) before the baseline lookup in BOTH the recorder and bloat_gate_on_stop (_re_measure_oversize/_baseline_map).

title: triage.jsonl main-tree drift blocks git pull/FF — reconcile-and-commit at integrate/sync
detail: C2 (#156) of the track-triage campaign chose a leak-guard EXEMPTION over the per-tree producer reroute (old C3). The exemption silences the leak-guard but is NOT a commit-path: per-session background producers (plugin-sync Stop-hook, compliance audit, triage_add) append to the tracked, main-repo-root-durable triage.jsonl, leaving UNCOMMITTED main-tree drift with no commit path (worktrees snapshot origin/main, never the dirty main tree -> orphans). The churn resolver only covers committed-vs-committed merges, so 'git merge --ff-only / git pull' against the dirty main tree is BLOCKED (hit 2026-06-07 during post-merge plugin-cache-sync; had to reconcile by hand). events.jsonl avoids this (per-tree pipeline producers). FIX (single iterate, not a campaign): a guarded reconcile_main_triage(project_root) that validates+union-dedups+commits the drift as ONE chore(triage) (B7-exempt) BEFORE any FF/pull, wired into integrate_main.py + the sync path (+ optionally setup_iterate_worktree to close the orphan). Commit lives in TOOLING, not hooks (avoids history-noise/hook-commit/race). Full design + ACs + rejected-alternatives: .shipwright/planning/iterate/proposed-triage-main-tree-drift-reconcile.md

title: external-review-state hygiene: transient review-gate state inconsistently tracked (ADR-089 leak class)
detail: The external-review gate (mark-review-state.py) writes external_review_state.json + external_code_review_state.json (Branch A/B/C state) into the run's planning dir. RESOLVED DESIGN (investigated 2026-06-09): these markers are TRANSIENT run-scoped state, NOT durable audit evidence. KEY FINDING: rtm.py::collect_external_review_states (lines 234-237) EXPLICITLY SKIPS .shipwright/planning/iterate/ ('iterate runs produce run-scoped markers audited separately via EVENTS, not per-split RTM rows'); the RTM only treats .shipwright/planning/<plan-split>/external_review_state.json as durable evidence. All 6 currently git-tracked copies live under .shipwright/planning/iterate/ (2 top-level + 4 in campaign sub-iterates) => transient, accidentally committed. Handoff + W5 verifiers read only the CURRENT run's marker (live), never historical copies. CORRECT FIX (iterate-scoped, NOT blanket): a blanket **/external_*review_state.json ignore would be a NEAR-MISS — it would also catch the durable plan-split RTM evidence and erase it on fresh clones. Instead add to the gitignore canon (template + framework managed block, congruent): /.shipwright/planning/iterate/**/external_review_state.json and /.shipwright/planning/iterate/**/external_code_review_state.json (the **/ matches the direct top-level copy AND the deeper campaign/sub-iterate copies; it does NOT touch planning/<split>/external_*). Then git rm --cached the 6 tracked copies (gitignore alone does not untrack committed files). Plan-split markers stay tracked = RTM evidence preserved. Propagates to adopted repos via the canon template. Same producer-leak class as ADR-089 / iterate-2026-06-09-idle-main-artifact-hygiene / -audit-report-hygiene.

title: artifact-path-canon: exempt generated triage_inbox.md cache from legacy-path lint
detail: The artifact-path-canon Layer-1 lint (test_no_legacy_artifact_paths) scans tracked .md/.py for bare legacy artifact-dir references. .shipwright/agent_docs/triage_inbox.md is a GENERATED cache (regenerated each iterate by aggregate_triage.py from .shipwright/triage.jsonl) that renders arbitrary producer finding detail + launchPayload, which can quote any path verbatim. A finding whose text mentions a bare legacy artifact dir therefore trips the lint on the generated cache, which cannot be fixed in place because it regenerates. title: Triage live-view: union the gitignored outbox so new items are visible/startable before sweep
detail: UX gap: a freshly-created triage item (manual triage_add or an idle-main background producer) routes to the gitignored per-tree buffer .shipwright/triage.outbox.jsonl and is INVISIBLE in the WebUI until the next iterate-setup sweep folds it into the tracked .shipwright/triage.jsonl. So you cannot see or one-click-start an iterate for the very item that should BE the next iterate (chicken-and-egg). Root cause: the monorepo canonical reader shared/scripts/triage.py::read_all_items ALREADY unions tracked + outbox (two-pass union, D1) and triage_cli.py list shows outbox items; but the WebUI reads only the tracked log (or the derived triage_inbox.md). FIX (two parts): (1) MONOREPO enabler - add a JSON contract triage_cli.py list --json that emits the unioned, reduced item list (single source of truth for union + reduction) so the WebUI consumes it instead of re-parsing JSONL. (2) WEBUI (shipwright-webui repo) - live-union read: render tracked + outbox, badge outbox-only items as Pending-delivery/ships-with-next-iterate, and let the existing Start/Fix CTA act on them (the iterate setup sweep delivers the item into that iterate PR automatically). Do NOT route user/manual items straight to the tracked log to fix visibility - that reintroduces main-tree drift the outbox exists to prevent. Interim: triage_cli.py list already shows the item; an iterate can be started manually and the setup sweep delivers it. NOTE: this is the real D4 (WebUI live-view union); the id trg-55516654 referenced in older notes is a DIFFERENT item (idle-main artifact hygiene).

title: classify_complexity Stage-1 systematically under-classifies: app-domain keywords + hard-coded trivial fall-through
detail: Empirical (45 Stage-1 outputs from sessions 2026-05-10..2026-06-10 vs 50 finalized runs in agent_docs/iterates): Stage 1 returns trivial 64% of the time (scope_keyword_estimate trivial in 33/45), but only 14% of runs finalize trivial (small 44%, medium 42%). The agent's Stage-2 Repo Scout bumps nearly every run upward, so Stage 1 carries near-zero signal in this repo. Root causes: (1) estimate_scope() keyword vocabulary is hard-coded for end-user web apps (spinner/tooltip/dashboard/new page) and never matches monorepo vocabulary (hook, triage, producer, gate, worktree, classifier) -> falls through to 'trivial'; (2) the fall-through default is the lowest rung instead of the project's observed median; (3) no feedback loop although F5c entries record final complexity per run; (4) the few medium/large hits are lexical accidents ('dashboard' in 'compliance dashboard', 'session' in SessionStart -> touches_auth, 'schema' -> touches_migrations). Side effect: a trivial estimate selects the Quick repo scout, so the stage meant to correct the estimate is itself shallowed. PROPOSED FIX (Option 1 + signals transparency): classify() reads the last N=20 finalized complexities from .shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/*.json and uses their median (clamped small..medium) as the fall-through prior when no scope keyword matched; expose signals.prior_source = history|keyword|default and print it in the Run Summary; keep risk-floor logic unchanged; cold start (no entries) keeps today's trivial default. Secondary (separate, optional): per-project scope vocabulary generated at adopt/project time to also fix risk-flag false positives. Estimated scope: small-medium iterate, touches classify_complexity.py + tests + SKILL.md Step E prose.

title: Bloat Stop-gate reads MAIN baseline while re-measuring the WORKTREE file — false-block on a worktree iterate that bumps a baseline (trg-305e2aab gap)
detail: Reproduced 2026-06-10 in PR #184. trg-305e2aab was dismissed as FIXED in #150, but #150 fixed only the PATH-prefix half. bloat_gate_on_stop.main(): current=_re_measure_oversize(root,entry) measures main_root/.worktrees/<slug>/.../file (the WORKTREE file, e.g. 326), but ceiling=_baseline_map(root) loads the MAIN-repo shipwright_bloat_baseline.json (old current, e.g. 318) — my ADR-documented bump to 326 lives in the worktree, committed in the PR, not yet on main. So 326<=318 is false -> anti-ratchet offender -> Stop-block, even though pre-commit + CI anti-ratchet (which read the worktree baseline) PASS. Same baseline-source mismatch in the recorder check_file_size.py at write time (records delta=anti-ratchet against main's baseline). Fix: when the marker path is a .worktrees/<slug>/ path, resolve the ceiling from THAT worktree's baseline (main_root/.worktrees/<slug>/shipwright_bloat_baseline.json), so the re-measured file and its ceiling come from the same tree. Add a regression test reproducing worktree-bump-then-Stop (missing from #150). Workaround today: rm the stale 1h-TTL session marker.

title: Align bloat marker WRITER (check_file_size) to worktree baseline — delta label still main-keyed (harmless after the trg-28e83840 reader fix)
detail: Follow-up to trg-28e83840 (Stop-gate reader fix). The recorder check_file_size.py computes the marker delta (anti-ratchet vs crossing) + was_in_allowlist against the MAIN baseline at write time, even for a .worktrees/<slug>/ path. After the reader fix (bloat_gate_on_stop resolves the ceiling + in_baseline from the worktree's own baseline) this is HARMLESS — the reader re-derives the correct decision regardless of the stored delta label (proven by test_worktree_newly_baselined_file_not_treated_as_crossing). So this is a clarity/consistency cleanup, NOT a safety gap: align the writer to read the worktree baseline (or drop the now-advisory delta/was_in_allowlist from the marker, since the reader recomputes). Found by adversarial review of the trg-28e83840 PR.

title: Intelligent bloat gate: falsifiable reducibility reviewer (LOC becomes a router, not the verdict)
detail: Replace the raw >300-LOC verdict with an LLM reducibility reviewer. Cheap LOC signal becomes the ROUTER that escalates to the reviewer; the reviewer blocks only on a concrete, falsifiable reduction from a closed catalog (D duplication / A needless-abstraction / X dead-code / C control-flow / S data-shape / M comment-restating-code / P dependency-footprint / T test-repetition), each citing what-to-remove + est-LOC-saved + keeps-tests-green; no concrete finding -> PASS. Guardrails G1-G6: long-but-coherent is never a finding, clarity>cleverness, never weaken coverage/validation/types, no churn that breaks merge stability, justified duplication (G5) exempt, generated/vendored exempt. Two goals: (A) prevent over-production = blocking on the diff; (B) boy-scout improve-on-touch = advisory, bounded to the touched unit. Lands: catalog as shared reference + per-language idiom-map in shared/profiles/; reviewer dimension in plugins/shipwright-build/agents/code-reviewer.md + shared/prompts/iterate_reviewer; enforcement via review cascade (bounce-back) + optional CI tiered-review (B4.5). Dogfood (this iterate): catalog applied to 8 H1 files -> 7/8 correctly long-coherent (no forced churn), 1/8 a real D2 (see resolver-consolidation item).

title: Consolidate 3 repo-root resolvers into lib/repo_root.py (events_log.resolve_main_repo_root is in the wrong module)
detail: Three functions resolve the MAIN repo root via git rev-parse --git-common-dir: lib/worktree_isolation.main_repo_root (raises), lib/repo_root.main_repo_root_or (fail-soft fallback), lib/events_log.resolve_main_repo_root (returns None + warnings). The third is a repo-root primitive squatting in the event-log module -- its own docstring states it is 'no longer used to locate the event log'; its real consumers are the decision-drop resolvers (write_decision_drop, aggregate_decisions), the F11 verifier (iterate_checks), plugin_sync_reminder_on_stop, and compliance group_f. Proposed fix: move the implementation into lib/repo_root.py (its thematic home) and re-export from events_log for back-compat, then migrate call sites + tests. Constraints to respect: reverses the documented 2026-05-29 keep-in-place decision (rewrite the events_log docstring sections); ~10 consumer/test files; test_decision_drop_ssot.py greps the literal string 'resolve_main_repo_root' in consumer sources; dedicated tests in test_events_log.py / test_git_tools_utf8.py import it from events_log. Out of scope for a bloat cleanup; needs its own iterate. Surfaced by the H1 bloat dogfood on events_log.py (323 LOC).

title: RTM collector crashes on explicit-null affected_frs (no None guard)
detail: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/collectors/_types.py builds WorkEvent.affected_frs via d.get('affected_frs', []), whose default only applies when the key is ABSENT. A work_completed event carrying an explicit 'affected_frs': null (e.g. when finalize_iterate is given --event-extras-json with affected_frs:null, instead of the normal omit) yields None, and rtm.map_requirements_to_events then does 'for fr_id in we.affected_frs' -> TypeError: NoneType is not iterable, crashing the whole compliance markdown regen (dashboard/RTM/sbom/test-evidence/change-history). Latent: the normal finalize flow omits the key, so 5/6 recent events are fine; surfaced when this iterate passed explicit null. Fix: coerce null+missing alike, e.g. d.get('affected_frs') or [] (same for new_frs and any sibling list fields), with a regression test feeding an explicit-null event. Generalizes so any producer that emits null can't brick compliance.

title: update_step: pre-lock standalone read triggers an unlocked legacy migration

title: Hook fan-out — redundant cross-cutting work ran N× per event; deduped via once-per-event guard + session-state phase resolver
detail: Claude Code fires every enabled plugin's hooks with no active-plugin filter, so each shared cross-cutting hook did its real work N× per event (SessionStart/Stop/PostToolUse ×11–12), and audit_phase_quality_on_stop keyed the audited phase off CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT → one Stop audited 11 phases, 10 of which never ran. RESOLVED in iterate-2026-06-14-hook-fanout-dedup (symmetric, no single controlling plugin): genuinely-redundant work is wrapped in a fail-open once-per-(event,session) guard (event_once.claim_once_for_event) on audit_phase_quality_on_stop + generate_handoff_on_stop + check_artifact_drift; the audit resolves which phase(s) ran from SESSION STATE (phase_quality.resolve_engaged_phases over events.jsonl + run_config) instead of plugin root. register-everywhere kept (test_hook_registry_bloat invariant + robustness across pipeline AND iterate). mark_plugin_edit/check_file_size were left unchanged (already convergent set-idempotent/upsert markers). Comprehensive integration-tests/test_hook_fanout_consolidation.py (exactly-once, phase-from-session-state, fail-open, robust-when-first-plugin-disabled, parallel-fan-out atomicity, marker convergence). Earlier SessionStart injection spam was already fixed via capture_session_id's claim_once. Supersedes the abandoned 2026-06-02-hook-consolidation campaign framing (single-owner-in-iterate).

reason: Implemented: symmetric once-per-event guard + session-state phase resolver; see iterate spec + integration-tests/test_hook_fanout_consolidation.py.

title: triage_gc: make under-lock GC recompute union-residence-aware (audit-1 a1-6 follow-up)
detail: a1-6/F19 closed the tracked-route TOCTOU (recompute droppable set under the lock), but the recompute reads the tracked store only. On idle-main-with-origin a concurrent re-open routes to the gitignored outbox and stays invisible to the recompute, so the item is still dropped and the outbox status orphans. Make the recompute consider union residence (still rewriting only the tracked file) and add an outbox-route survival test. Documented as an operator constraint in triage_gc.py until fixed. Also (low): make the reverse-drift meta-test source-derived rather than a hand-copied token set, and resolve the legacy auditResolved orphan token; extract the duplicated _strip_control_chars into shared/ and cover the GC dry-run report render surface.

title: Campaign independent-branch decision-drop bleed false-fails arch-md test locally
detail: In an autonomous campaign with independent branches run sequentially on one shared working tree, gitignored decision-drops accumulate across branches while each branch's architecture.md is committed per-branch. Consider scoping the test to the current run_id, or having campaign sub-iterates run in isolated worktrees so gitignored artifacts don't bleed.

title: Auto-merge churn fix (Option A): serial integrate_main merge for campaign/parallel iterates
detail: GitHub auto-merge (PR #197) does a server-side merge and never runs integrate_main / resolve_churn_conflicts (the regenerate-at-merge resolver). For a single sequential iterate (branch current with main) auto-merge is fine, but for PARALLEL iterate branches (--autonomous campaign, or concurrent iterates) each branch commits its own regenerated derived snapshots (.shipwright/compliance/*.md, .shipwright/agent_docs/*.md, shipwright_test_results.json). As branches merge serially, every still-open branch goes DIRTY (auto-merge stalls) or merges stale (Group E staleness noise) because the regen step never runs server-side. events.jsonl + triage.jsonl are fine (merge=union); only the regenerate-on-conflict snapshots break. Seen live in campaign 2026-06-10-audit-1-auto: #199/#204/#205 merged, #200-#203 cascaded DIRTY/behind and needed manual integrate_main merges; an UNRELATED PR #206 (agent-doc compaction) re-conflicted them on conventions.md mid-drain. DECISION = Option A: do the merge through integrate_main, SERIALIZED, for campaigns/concurrency; keep auto-merge only for single iterates whose branch is current; add an F11 guard that runs integrate_main first if the branch is behind. Host-agnostic, reuses existing machinery, softens no gate. REJECTED: GitHub Action post-merge (host-specific); untracking snapshots (breaks audit_staleness); Option C derived-cache restructure (disproportionate, would have to extend to agent docs too). FOLLOW-UP (Option B, later): automate the serial drain as the gh-pr-ci watcher producer on the B4.5 roadmap. Full plan + acceptance criteria + reuse pointers: Spec/automerge-churn-serial-integrate-plan.md. DO BEFORE the next autonomous campaign.

title: update-marketplace.sh F37 python probe picks the broken Windows python3 Store-stub (regression from #205)
detail: a1-7/F37 (#205) changed update-marketplace.sh to probe 'python3 -> python -> py' via 'command -v'. On Windows, python3 is usually the Microsoft Store App-Execution-Alias STUB: command -v finds it, but running it prints 'Python was not found; install from the Microsoft Store' and exits 49. Under set -euo pipefail the first cache_target=$(python3 -c ...) then aborts the whole script right after 'Full sync:' with exit 49 -> the plugin-cache sync silently does nothing on Windows (plugin fixes never reach the runtime cache; the campaign's own merged plugin changes did not propagate until worked around). F37 fixed the POSIX case (bare python absent) but introduced a Windows regression. FIX: probe by TEST-RUNNING each candidate, not just command -v: 'if command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && "$c" --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then PYTHON_BIN=$c; break; fi'. The stub fails --version (49) and the probe falls through to the real 'python'. Validated: with the test-run probe the full sync completes (13 synced, 0 errors) on this Windows box. File: scripts/update-marketplace.sh (probe lines ~40-45). Same test-run pattern likely wanted wherever else the python3-first command-v probe was copied (e.g. verify-setup.sh). Add a shell test that simulates a python3 that exits non-zero on --version and asserts the probe picks the next candidate.

title: Decompose coarse one-FR-per-plugin requirements into sub-FRs (esp. FR-01.10 compliance)
detail: The 14 FRs are one-per-plugin/command (FR-01.10 = the whole /shipwright-compliance plugin), so coverage is trivially 14/14 and never moves, and real capabilities added inside a plugin (Control Grade, honesty gate, CI-security ingestion, SBOM quality, RTM reconciliation) have no specific FR to map to -> they get filed no-FR, depressing strict FR-traceability. Decompose the fat plugin-FRs into sub-FRs (e.g. FR-01.10.x: Control Grade / RTM / SBOM / CI-security ingestion / honesty gate; similarly FR-01.13 adopt, FR-01.11 iterate, FR-01.07 security). Product-modeling task: needs owner input on granularity. Makes coverage meaningful + the grade reflect the real feature surface. Paired with the re-tag follow-up (fr-model-followup).

title: Re-tag mis-filed compliance/security FEATURE events to their parent FRs (clears the traceability decline)
detail: Recent /shipwright-compliance + /shipwright-security FEATURE work was filed change_type=compliance/no-FR though it delivers FR-01.10 (and FR-01.07) functionality, depressing strict FR-tagging to ~10% (vs 18% all-time) -> honesty-gate caps the grade at B. Fix: append event_amended overlays (record_event.py --type event_amended --amends <id>) setting affected_frs + spec_impact=modify on the genuine features. RE-TAG -> FR-01.10 (security ones +FR-01.07): Goodhart Control Grade/honesty gate; AR-10 CI-security ingestion; AR-10 SARIF fallback; AR-04 SBOM quality; AR-05 RTM Reconciled column; Control-Grade anchors/maintainability anchor. STAY no-FR (real infra): scorecard add/fix/remove (CI), mtime drift-detector removal, bloat-baseline tighten, events_log lazy-import doc, ci-security.json data refresh. CAVEAT: spec_impact=modify makes FR-01.10/FR-01.07 behavior-touched -> VERIFY the reconciliation dimension stays green (each touched FR needs a test run at/after its last touch; link a later test event or don't tag the very latest as modify). Expected: recent 3/30 -> ~9/30, decline clears, grade -> A honestly. Pairs with the sub-FR decomposition (fr-model-followup); ideally do the decomposition first so features map to specific sub-FRs.

title: Measure patch/diff coverage (were the CHANGED lines tested?), not just pass-rate
detail: Reviewer comment B: '3618/3618 green' is pass-rate, not coverage — it says nothing about whether AI-added code is even executed. Killer case for AI-first: AI writes code + a trivial test that misses the risky branch; pass-rate stays green, new code untested. The Test Completeness Ledger is an author-CLAIMED checklist, not instrumented. Today CI runs plain pytest (no --cov). BUILD: pytest --cov -> coverage.xml -> diff-cover against the PR merge-base = % of CHANGED lines covered; surface as (a) a CI gate (warn/fail under threshold) AND (b) an input to the Control Grade Test-health dimension (note: the W4 verifier already reads shipwright_test_results.json coverage.total but the field is never populated -> SKIP). SCOPE/caveats: touches CI across ALL plugins (each has its own pytest step) + a coverage-combine step + a schema field + grade wiring -> its own iterate (biggest of the A/B/C/D set, why it wasn't bundled into #296). Generic repo-grader story (arbitrary languages) is harder -> do monorepo dogfood first, defer the generic case. Central to the 'control over AI code' thesis.

title: github_triage artifact-ingest counts inline-suppressed Semgrep findings as live, inflating gh-security triage and blocking auto-resolve
detail: shared/scripts/github_triage/producer.py security_artifact_action_unit() sets artifact_total = len(findings) with no suppression filter. On the artifact-ingest path (GHAS Code Scanning unavailable, cs_alerts is None) this counts inline-suppressed Semgrep findings (SARIF results carrying suppressions:[{kind:inSource}]) as live, inflating the gh-security:<owner>/<repo> action-unit count. Since the count never reaches 0, resolve_stale never auto-dismisses the item and it re-appears after every manual dismiss. Fix: count only results where (.suppressions // []) | length == 0 before len(), so a fully-suppressed scan yields 0 findings -> producer returns None -> auto-resolve gate fires. Add a regression test with a SARIF fixture containing suppressed results. Found during a shipwright-webui security review of CI run 28407935303 (12 inline-suppressed FPs surfaced as 12 low).

title: pr_review Tier-3 truncates on medium+ iterates: exclude generated artifacts from the review diff (82% of tokens are derived)
detail: pr_review.py Tier-3 review truncates + fails-closed on medium+ iterates because it sends the FULL gh-pr-diff (no path filter) and generated artifacts dominate the token budget. Measured on PR #310: total diff 295,497 chars (~74k tok) vs MAX_DIFF_CHARS=200,000 -> truncated. Breakdown: DERIVED artifacts 241,286 chars (82%) — test-evidence.md alone 119,670, uv.lock 77,758 — vs real SOURCE only 54,211 chars (~13.6k tok, well under cap). So every medium+ iterate (regenerates compliance MDs + bumps uv.lock) trips truncation, and the skip-pr-review workaround then DISABLES review entirely on exactly the large PRs that need it. The fail-closed-on-truncation itself is correct design (#263); the fixable part is the INPUT bloat. FIX (own iterate, --type change): in pr_review.py filter the unified diff to DROP file-sections for generated paths (.shipwright/compliance/, .shipwright/agent_docs/, *.lock, shipwright_test_results.json, shipwright_events.jsonl, CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/) and record the excluded list in the PR meta (transparent, not silent). Effect: -82% tokens -> review runs + the model sees only real code (better quality). REJECTED: bumping MAX_DIFF_CHARS (symptom-only, wastes tokens on lockfiles). CAVEATS: pr_review.py is in plugins/shipwright-security (sensitive Tier-3a path -> own PR); WebUI has a VENDORED copy that needs a separate webui iterate to stay in parity; keep the exclusion list conservative + logged. expands_triage this id; dismiss after fix.

title: Cross-repo contract: the WebUI now renders grade's ReportModel + adopt's snapshot.json - say so in the SKILLs
detail:
The WebUI Command Center now RENDERS these two artifacts natively (WOW campaign
webui-wow-usability-2026-07-10, sub-iterate A08 "intent-wizard", triage trg-3edbc478). That turns
them from "our own output format" into a CROSS-REPO CONTRACT — and nothing in this repo says so.

WHAT THE WEBUI CONSUMES
  1. shipwright-grade: the `ReportModel` / `DimensionView` dataclasses
     (plugins/shipwright-grade/scripts/lib/report_model.py, rendered by html_report.py).
     The WebUI's "Grade your repo" screen renders THIS model field-for-field, deliberately, so
     the screen and the downloadable HTML report cannot tell different stories.
     Load-bearing fields it depends on:
       - dimensions[].status (ok|gap|n/a) -- drives the VISUAL. An n/a is drawn as absent
         evidence, never as a zero-score bar. The WebUI must never synthesize a score.
       - dimensions[].provenance + .detail -- the per-row "how this was measured" disclosure.
       - network_enabled / network_note / network_enrichments -- "exactly what left the
         machine". This is the receipt for the product's "read-only, no account" promise and
         is shown verbatim. If this field disappears, the WebUI loses its trust surface.
       - honest_ceiling_note, measurable_count, na_count, controls_shipwright_would_light[].
  2. shipwright-adopt: `.shipwright/adopt/snapshot.json` (stack, profile, conventions,
     test_frameworks, ci_pipeline, folders, nested_projects, features, git, commands) -- the
     WebUI's adopt screen shows "what's already here" from it before anything is written.

THE RISK
A field renamed or dropped here does not fail loudly in the WebUI -- it renders a half-empty
card or, worse, a plausible-but-wrong one. Nobody in this repo currently has a reason to know
the WebUI is watching.

TASK
  - State the contract in the SKILL.md of shipwright-grade and shipwright-adopt: these output
    shapes have an external consumer (the Command Center); a change to them requires a
    corresponding WebUI change. Point at the consumer.
  - Consider a versioned//stable marker on ReportModel (e.g. a schema version) so the WebUI can
    detect an unknown shape and say so honestly instead of rendering nonsense.
  - Also worth noting: grade.py accepts a local path OR a remote (shallow-cloned into a
    throwaway tempdir, purged after; --no-clone opts out). The WebUI surfaces the clone step
    and the network cost explicitly -- keep that behaviour stable or tell the WebUI.

WebUI side is already guarded: A08's spec requires payload-shape validation + an honest
"report shape not recognised" state rather than a half-empty render.

title: phase_timings rides along with the next iterate (verify it fires); phase_started needs a pipeline run, not an iterate
detail:
Producer gap found by the WebUI backend-completeness audit (2026-07-13): the event log has ZERO
live rows for phase_started / phase_timings.

=== CORRECTION (supersedes trg-eb989815, which conflated two mechanisms) ===
The old item said "fire ONE real iterate run ... verify the event log contains phase_started +
phase_timings". That is WRONG: an iterate will NEVER emit phase_started. Verified in the source --
these are two DIFFERENT producers:

  phase_timings  <- shared/scripts/tools/finalize_iterate.py + iterate_phase_timing.py
                    THE ITERATE FLOW. The 5 boundary marks (scope|build|review|test|finalize) are
                    emitted as the skill crosses each group boundary, and F5b folds the durations
                    into `work_completed.phase_timings`.
                    => ANY real iterate in this repo produces it. It is FREE.

  phase_started  <- plugins/shipwright-run/scripts/lib/orchestrator_pkg/{events,single_session_cli}.py
                    THE PIPELINE ORCHESTRATOR ONLY. Paired phase_started/phase_completed.
                    => needs a real /shipwright-run pipeline. An iterate cannot produce it.

(Reference: plugins/shipwright-iterate/skills/iterate/references/phase-timing.md, which states it
explicitly: the pipeline rail uses paired phase_started/phase_completed; the ITERATE flow instead
emits lightweight marks folded into work_completed.phase_timings.)

=== WHAT TO ACTUALLY DO ===
1. phase_timings — DO NOT schedule a dedicated run for this. Ride along with the next real iterate
   in this repo (e.g. the cross-repo-contract item trg-46a8de1f). Its own F5b emits the rows.
   The only work is to VERIFY afterwards that `work_completed.phase_timings` is present and
   populated in the event log. If it is NOT, then the emitter is genuinely broken (the marks are
   "additive and best-effort", so a skipped mark silently omits a bar) -- and THAT is the bug to
   fix. Confirming the emitter actually fires is the whole point.
2. phase_started — needs no dedicated task at all. It appears on the next real /shipwright-run
   pipeline. Do not run a full pipeline just to produce telemetry.
3. Optional (unchanged): an explicit gate-verdict object -- today the verdict is inferred rather
   than stated.

=== WHY IT MATTERS ===
The WebUI WOW campaign (webui-wow-usability-2026-07-10, A01/A02 = event-log reader) renders
per-phase durations from these rows. Until they exist the reader degrades to an honest `n/a`
(specified) -- it must NEVER fabricate or interpolate a duration.

title: Retarget the 8 phase-skill Step-0 blocks off the deleted SHIPWRIGHT-PIPELINE-CONTEXT block
detail:
The 8 phase skills still gate their Step-0 context recovery on the presence of a SHIPWRIGHT-PIPELINE-CONTEXT block ("if the PIPELINE-CONTEXT block is present, parse phaseTaskId and run get_phase_context.py; otherwise standalone"). The sole producer of that block was the phase_session_start SessionStart hook, deleted with the multi-session engine in iterate-2026-07-14-remove-multi-session. The trigger can therefore never fire, and every phase skill silently takes its standalone branch.

Not a regression from that iterate: single_session has been the default since SS8, and the phase runner is a SUBAGENT of the master, so it never had a bound Claude session whose id could match a phase_tasks[].sessionUuid — the block already never reached it. The removal only made the dead consumer visible.

Already closed the loop on the tool itself: the master now passes dispatch.phaseTaskId to the phase-runner, whose brief (agents/phase-runner.md Step 0) calls get_phase_context.py --phase-task-id directly. So prior-phase artifacts DO get loaded in the surviving mode.

Remaining work: retarget the 8 phase-skill Step-0 blocks (project, design, plan, build, test, security, changelog, deploy + their references/step-0-*.md) off the deleted context block and onto "the orchestrator handed you a phaseTaskId", so a phase skill invoked as a phase-runner subagent takes the pipeline branch rather than the standalone one. Also decide whether the Step-0 blocks are still needed at all now that the phase-runner brief does it.

title: Phase skills detect invocation mode from the unmaintained v1 current_step, so a driven phase can wrongly conclude standalone
detail:
The 8 phase skills classify "pipeline vs standalone" in their First-Actions step C ("Detect Invocation Mode") by reading shipwright_run_config.json status + current_step. Under the v2 pipeline those two fields are never advanced, so the check is blind for every driven run.

Empirically reproduced: drive project + design through the real single-session loop, then read the config. The phase_tasks frontier is correctly at "plan", but current_step is still "project" and completed_steps is []. grep confirms phase_task_lifecycle never writes current_step.

NOT a regression from iterate-2026-07-14-remove-multi-session, and this is the load-bearing point: the deleted phase_session_stop hook never wrote current_step either (verified against origin/main), so the check was equally blind under multi_session. It is the long-standing v1-compat vs v2 divergence — current_step/completed_steps are the v1 fields, phase_tasks is the v2 authority — surfaced by a reviewer looking at the phase skills with fresh eyes.

Consequence today: a phase skill dispatched by the orchestrator can conclude "standalone" from step C, skip its pipeline-state updates, and mark its own artifacts with mode: standalone, even though it is part of a driven run. Step 0 (context recovery) is unaffected — that was retargeted onto the phaseTaskId the orchestrator hands the phase-runner, and is guarded in both directions.

Fix direction: make step C key on the same thing Step 0 now does — the orchestrator handed you a phaseTaskId — or derive the invocation mode from phase_tasks rather than the unmaintained v1 fields. Touches all 8 phase skills plus their first-actions references, so it wants its own iterate rather than being bolted onto the removal PR.

Found by the Codex review of PR #369 (delta round).

title: Sweep quarantines a dismiss forever when the append lives only in main's tracked working tree (silent data loss + resurrection loop)
detail:
Reproduced live in shipwright-webui on 2026-07-14: triage item trg-6db81c59 kept
resurfacing on the board after every dismiss. Two defects compound into a loop that
SILENTLY EATS operator dismisses. The quarantine mechanism (#303) converted a loud
hard-block into quiet data loss.

== Evidence (shipwright-webui, 2026-07-14) ==
The `append` for trg-6db81c59 (and trg-6e048260) existed in NO git object:
  origin/main:.shipwright/triage.jsonl  -> 0 hits
  HEAD:.shipwright/triage.jsonl         -> 0 hits
  .shipwright/triage.outbox.jsonl       -> 0 hits
It existed ONLY as an uncommitted modification of main's TRACKED triage.jsonl
(`git status` showed `M .shipwright/triage.jsonl`, +2 lines).

triage.outbox.quarantine.jsonl recorded the same dismiss eaten repeatedly:
  2026-07-14T14:55:07  trg-6db81c59  dismissed  by=operatorReview
  2026-07-14T15:43:52  trg-6db81c59  dismissed  by=webui
  (trg-6e048260: 4x, from 2026-07-14T06:50:55 onward)
reason: "orphan-status: no append anywhere in the combined triage log"

== Defect A: a tracked-on-main append is delivered by NOTHING ==
`sweep_outbox_to_branch()` folds ONLY the gitignored outbox into the iterate branch.
An append that lands in main's TRACKED triage.jsonl (uncommitted) is picked up by no
producer, no sweep and no reconcile -- it sits in the working tree forever, invisible
to origin and to every worktree. The known rule "a tracked write on main = undelivered
drift" has no enforcement and no repair path. Whatever wrote those two appends bypassed
`should_route_to_outbox()`; the sweep should at minimum not let the drift rot silently.

== Defect B: the orphan check's universe is too small ==
`sweep_quarantine.decide(worktree_lines, outbox_lines, eol)` classifies over
`worktree-tracked (branched from origin/main) INTERSECT/UNION outbox` only. It never sees
MAIN's tracked log -- even though `sweep_outbox_to_branch()` already holds `main_root`.
So any status event for a drift-only append MUST look like an orphan. It is then
quarantined AND deleted from the outbox (sweep_outbox.py, the `if gc_dropped or
quarantined:` rewrite), and the sweep reports success. The operator's dismiss is gone.

Resurrection loop: the WebUI reader unions local-tracked (WITH the drift append) u origin
u outbox. Append present, dismiss quarantined away -> status falls back to `triage` ->
the item reappears -> operator dismisses again -> next sweep eats it again. Forever.

== Proposed fix ==
1. Widen the orphan universe: pass main_root's tracked log into `decide()` as a
   third read-only "known appends" source, so a status is only an orphan when its
   append exists in NEITHER worktree-tracked NOR outbox NOR main-tracked.
2. Do not silently drop a quarantined STATUS. Either keep it in the outbox until its
   append is origin-delivered, or surface the quarantine count loudly at setup (today
   `SweepResult.quarantined` is returned but the operator never sees it).
3. Detect + repair Defect A: if main's tracked log carries append lines absent from
   HEAD, the sweep should route them into the outbox (the real delivery channel)
   instead of leaving undelivered drift -- that is exactly the manual repair that
   fixed webui.

== Manual repair applied to shipwright-webui (reference implementation) ==
Moved both drift appends OUT of main's tracked log INTO the outbox, replayed the newest
quarantined dismiss behind them, reset the tracked log to HEAD. `sweep_quarantine.decide()`
then returns `clean` against origin/main, and the webui reader resolves both items to
`dismissed`. Regression tests should cover exactly this shape.

== Regression tests to add ==
- decide(): a status whose append exists ONLY in main-tracked is NOT an orphan.
- sweep: a drift append in main-tracked is routed to the outbox, not left behind.
- sweep: quarantining a status never silently removes the operator's only dismiss.

Move the 11 pipeline plugins (project, design, plan, build, test, deploy, changelog, compliance, security, iterate, preview) to PROJECT scope; adopt + greenfield run WRITE that enablement block into the target repo's .claude/settings.json. DECISIONS RESOLVED (owner, 2026-07-16): (D1) greenfield is run-only, shipwright-project stays project-scoped, global set = adopt/grade/run; (D2) solo use -> monorepo uses .claude/settings.local.json, tracked settings.json stays git-ignored (B4 moot). Plus JSONC-aware merge, secret-leak guard, marketplace-source conflict guard, min-version UX, prescriptive activation-lag messaging. title: FR taxonomy: capability-altitude FR minting (adopt) + Mint-vs-Fold gate (iterate) + FR-hygiene lint (compliance)
detail:
Root cause of badly-scoped, wrongly-numbered FRs in adopted specs: two FR-minting engines with incompatible philosophy. Fix across three plugins (full analysis + before/after mapping in the webui repo: Spec/design/2026-07-17-fr-taxonomy-regrouping.md).

(1) shipwright-adopt (feature_inferrer.py / artifact_writer.py): stop minting one FR per route. Group routes under the page/capability they serve (one FR per capability; routes become Interface bullets in the Description). Add an Area column + section-grouping (area from top route segment; fallback GEN). Keep the stable FR-01.NN ID scheme (IDs are referenced in append-only shipwright_events.jsonl the Mission view reads — never renumber). Strip HTTP verbs from the Name; dedup UI-page-FR vs backing-route-FR at the existing crawl-vs-AST url/route join.

(2) shipwright-iterate (path-a-feature.md / path-b-change.md / F5b): add an explicit MINT-vs-FOLD gate. FOLD (append AC to the existing FR) when the change completes/polishes/fixes/is Phase-N-of/extends an existing capability; MINT a new FR only for a genuinely new user/system-observable capability. Pin the number rule (new FR = next free FR-01.NN, deterministic max+1, filed into its Area section) to end guessed numbers + parallel-iterate collisions. Name fence: no GET/POST, snake_case symbols, ADR numbers or iterate slugs in the FR Name.

(3) shipwright-compliance: add an advisory FR-hygiene lint (new group), anti-ratchet/baseline style. Flag: altitude (Name carries a verb/symbol/ADR/slug), orphan-delta (Description says completes/modifies/replaces FR-x / Phase N of but is its own row -> fold candidate), missing Area, and UI-API duplicate FRs. Freeze existing violations; only new crossings block.

Cross-repo context: the webui spec.md is being sanitised in a parallel dedicated iterate (IDs kept stable, regroup+rename+fold, two tables: clean Requirements + a Fold/Alias map). These plugin fixes prevent the drift from recurring.

title: Fold-aware traceability: resolve @covers folded FR IDs via FR-Fold-Map before orphan-flagging
detail: The test_links collector, D-orphan (_group_d_traceability) and backfill_scan read only survivor FR-table rows and do NOT resolve the spec FR-Fold-Map. A @covers tag on a FOLDED FR id is therefore classified fr_absent -> confirmed_orphan -> D-orphan MEDIUM (FAIL). Evidence: webui #287 (fr-taxonomy-regroup) folded 66 FRs into 29 capabilities; when the webui traceability retrofit #289 merged that spec, 22 tagged FRs were folded -> 419 orphans and D-orphan failed. Worked around by deterministically remapping folded->survivor via the fold-map. FIX: collector + D-orphan should resolve a tagged id through FR-Fold-Map to its survivor (identity for a survivor) before deciding orphanhood, so granular @covers tags survive a later taxonomy fold instead of hard-breaking. Until then tags must reference survivor ids only. Ref: webui .shipwright/compliance/test-traceability-coverage-delta.md follow-on #5.

detail: The traceability manifest can now file a test link against a surviving FR while the source tag names the folded id, recording it as resolved_from. A reader comparing the WebUI to the source will otherwise see a test linked to FR-01.28 whose code says covers(FR-01.44) with no explanation. When the WebUI surfaces per-FR test links it should render 'mapped from <folded id>' wherever resolved_from is set. Separate repo (shipwright-webui), so a separate iterate. Also worth confirming there: the manifest schema_version deliberately stays 2 (the new keys are optional and omitted when unused), so any vendored validator with additionalProperties:false should be checked before a fold-map repo is onboarded.
