title: Adopt + project: capability-level FR minting (route grouping + Area) and a decision on the greenfield/brownfield spec-table shape
detail:
Deferred remainder of trg-8e840ca0 / trg-44d23d63, split out of iterate-2026-07-18-fr-authoring-rules (which delivered the authoring RULES + the advisory Group I lint). This item is the STRUCTURAL half: it changes generated output and table schema, so it was kept out of a prompt-rules PR that had to stay reviewable and independently revertable.

(1) ADOPT MINTS ONE FR PER ROUTE - the root cause of endpoint-altitude FRs.
The real minting is NOT in feature_inferrer.py (that is the AST fallback only); it is generate_adoption_artifacts.py:312-365, which unions crawl+AST routes and assigns FR-01.{i} positionally. Required change: group routes under the page/capability they serve (the crawl's page URLs are the natural capability anchors); one FR per capability, with the routes becoming interface detail in architecture.md rather than sibling FRs. Add UI-vs-API dedup at the existing crawl-vs-AST url/route join, and strip HTTP verbs from the generated label. Keep the FR-01.NN id scheme - ids are referenced from the append-only shipwright_events.jsonl the Mission view reads, so they are never renumbered.
Files: plugins/shipwright-adopt/scripts/tools/generate_adoption_artifacts.py (716 LOC, grandfathered), scripts/lib/artifact_writer.py (695 LOC, grandfathered). Blast radius: test_features_additive_merge.py, test_artifact_writer.py, test_adopt_pipeline_subprocess.py, test_e2e_baseline_generator.py, test_traceability_layers.py, test_seed_traceability_baseline.py.

(2) AREA COLUMN - brownfield only, by design.
Adopt puts everything into one split (01-adopted), so the FR id can no longer express grouping and it must be restored as an Area column + section headers. Greenfield does NOT need this and must not get it: /shipwright-project already decomposes into splits and the split is encoded in the id (FR-04.02 = split 04). This is written up in shared/fr-authoring.md section 4 - keep it that way.

(3) DECIDE THE SPEC-TABLE SHAPE - AFFECTS shipwright-project, NOT ONLY ADOPT. This is a required DECISION with a deliverable either way; it is the only reason this item touches project at all, and it is easy to miss because points 1/2/4 are adopt-only.
Already done, do NOT redo: project's language + altitude work shipped in iterate-2026-07-18-fr-authoring-rules (spec-generation.md carries the plain-business rule, the no-implementation-how fence, and "one requirement, one capability"). What is open for project is ONLY the table shape.
The two generators disagree today:
  - /shipwright-project (greenfield): | ID | Requirement | Priority | Layers |   - one IREB "The system SHALL ..." sentence.
  - /shipwright-adopt  (brownfield):  | ID | Name | Priority | Description | Source | Layers |
Both are rendered by the WebUI and read by the compliance collectors; drift_parsers.parse_fr_table / rtm.collect_requirements tolerate the difference via an optional-group regex (ADR-031). traceability_layers._layers_index resolves its column BY HEADER NAME, so ADDING a column is safe - REMOVING or renaming one is not.
Pick one and record it:
  (a) CONVERGE - move greenfield to Name+Description so both generators emit one shape. This is a schema migration: it ripples into the two FR parsers, the RTM, traceability_layers and seed_traceability_baseline, and needs its own test re-baseline. Do it WITH point 1, not separately, so the parsers change once.
  (b) KEEP BOTH - a legitimate answer (the Rupp sentence is an IREB choice, not an accident), but then it must be written down as intentional in shared/fr-authoring.md, otherwise the divergence silently rots and the next person re-opens this same question.
Choosing (b) means project is never touched again by this item - that is fine, but it must be a decision, not a default. Group I reads both shapes header-driven, so it does not constrain the choice.

(4) STALE DOC (found while scouting, unrelated to the above).
plugins/shipwright-adopt/skills/adopt/references/feature-inference.md:109-110 states "AST-inferred features are used only when no crawl data exists". That contradicts shipped behaviour - generate_adoption_artifacts.py:342-360 unions AST-only routes into the crawl set (the fix pinned by test_features_additive_merge.py). Correct the doc.

(5) GROUP I ROBUSTNESS FOLLOW-UPS (from the review round; all low severity).
  - A spec that parses to zero rows is indistinguishable from an absent spec: both SKIP with "no FR rows found". A blind scanner therefore reads as "nothing to audit". Distinguish "no spec.md on disk" from "spec.md present but no FR table header recognised", and normalise header cells (strip bold/backticks) before the "id" test.
  - _column_map returns a bare None for both "not a header row" and "header I do not understand", so a second unrecognised table inside one section keeps the previous table's column mapping and can misread cells.
  - A raw unescaped pipe inside a Description cell shifts later columns (escaped pipes are handled). Cheap guard: skip a data row whose cell count exceeds the header's.

(6) PROMOTE I1/I2 FROM ADVISORY TO ANTI-RATCHET.
This iterate ships the advisory half deliberately: the requirement was that existing violations must not redden CI while a spec cleans up gradually, so I1-I3 never emit status=fail (that would feed AuditReport.any_fail and flip run_audit's exit code and the dashboard verdict). The ratchet half - freeze existing violations in a baseline, block only NEW crossings, mirroring shipwright_bloat_baseline.json - still needs a baseline file plus its own drift protection.

title: Requirements Catalog campaign: one catalog, one table shape, one discovery path
detail:
Umbrella anchor for the Requirements-Catalog campaign (S0-S8). Full spec + evidence + risk register: Spec/design/2026-07-18-requirements-catalog-campaign-SPEC.md (gitignored; read it before starting any sub-iterate).

PROBLEM. Requirements are scattered across planning documents and the folder determines the grouping. Five table shapes exist for the same table, five parsers read them, and nine independent discovery loops look for them with no shared helper. The divergence has already produced two wrong verdicts (ADR-031 predicted two stable formats; ADR-048 records a brownfield RTM reporting zero percent coverage). The FR gate validates only that a declared requirement id is non-empty, never that it exists. Requirement text has absorbed the changelog (417 lines for 15 requirements; one requirement carries about 145 lines of history).

OUTCOME. One catalog grouped by area in plain business language; planning documents keep the work detail and are linked from it. Each requirement records how it was established, including an honest assumed marker. Change history moves to a derived query over the append-only event log.

SHAPE. Target table is derived from the already-cleaned webui reference state (PR 287) plus a Layers column: ID | Area | Name | Priority | Description | Basis | Layers.

SEQUENCE. S0 existence gate, S1 test harness, S2 one discovery function, S3 namespace from the requirement id, S4 one header-driven parser, S5 converge the shape, S6 merge the catalog, S7 derived traceability view, S8 glossary plus targeted elicitation. S0-S4 change nothing observable and exist so S5-S6 become safe.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT. The catalog must stay inside a split directory. A markdown file placed directly under planning/ matches none of the nine discovery walks, yielding zero requirements, which reads as pass or skip nearly everywhere while the spec-impact check simultaneously hard-fails every feature or change iterate. See section 6.1 of the spec before revisiting.

CROSS-REPO. The webui Mission campaign may start; it reads what this reshapes and PR 287 already built the target shape. After S3 merges, webui regenerates its manifest and RTM.

title: FR gate accepts requirement ids that do not exist (false green)
detail:
The finalization FR gate validates only that the declared requirement list is non-empty. is_non_empty_fr_list checks the strings and nothing else; whether a declared requirement actually exists is verified ONLY by detective check D2, which is medium severity, non-blocking, post-merge, and gated behind a spec-updated watermark.

Consequence: an iterate can declare an affected requirement that does not exist anywhere and the gate passes. This is why dangling references to non-existent requirement ids are present in the repo today.

This is a false green in the most load-bearing gate of the finalization chain, and it is independent of any table or catalog restructuring.

FIX. Validate declared requirement ids against the collected requirement set at write time in the event recorder and the finalizer, and hard-reject unknown ids with a message naming the offending id. The no-requirement change-type branch stays unchanged. Existing dangling references are reported, not auto-corrected.

Pulled forward as S0 of the Requirements-Catalog campaign (anchor trg-16d79da2) but independently shippable and worth doing first. Spec: Spec/design/2026-07-18-requirements-catalog-campaign-SPEC.md section 4 (S0).

title: Triage outbox: missing trailing newline concatenates two records, silently dropping one
detail:
A record in the triage outbox was written without a trailing newline, so the next writer appended onto the same physical line. The reader then fails to parse that line and SKIPS it with a warning, discarding BOTH records on it.

Observed today: one line held an append followed by a status record written by the WebUI. The status marked an item as dismissed with the note that it had been implemented. That dismissal never propagated, so the item still reads as open in the main log while the person who closed it believes it is done.

IMPACT. Silent loss on an append-only log. The warning goes to stderr and is easy to miss, and the reader treats a corrupt line as absent rather than as an error, so the loss is invisible in normal use. This is the same failure family as the earlier orphaned-status incident.

FIX DIRECTIONS. (1) Writers must guarantee the file ends with a newline before appending, rather than assuming the previous writer left one. (2) The reader should quarantine a corrupt line loudly instead of skipping it quietly, and should attempt to recover concatenated records by splitting on a record boundary. (3) A repair pass for lines already corrupted.

NOTE. The outbox file is untracked, so a corrupted line has no git history to recover from. Repair must preserve both records.

title: REQ-1 - Iterate: requirements test harness (golden corpus) - run AFTER REQ-0, BEFORE REQ-2
detail:
SECOND of three. Order: REQ-0 (FR existence gate) -> REQ-1 (this) -> REQ-2 (campaign trg-1b764b2c). This is the safety net the whole catalog rebuild rests on; REQ-2 must not start before it is merged.

Autonomous start:
  /shipwright-iterate --type change "requirements test harness: golden corpus that freezes todays discovery and parser behaviour, including its known false verdicts"

WHY. Nine independent implementations walk .shipwright/planning/ looking for spec.md, with no shared helper, and five parsers read the resulting table. Steps S2-S4 of REQ-2 rewrite exactly that machinery and claim to be behaviour-preserving. Without a harness that claim cannot be checked, only asserted.

WHAT TO BUILD. A fixture corpus - greenfield multi-split, brownfield single-split, empty, malformed, mixed-shape - plus assertions pinning the CURRENT output of every discovery path and every parser for each fixture.

THE POINT MOST LIKELY TO BE GOT WRONG. The harness must freeze todays behaviour INCLUDING its bugs. Two known false verdicts must be recorded as current behaviour, each with a comment naming the later step that flips them: (1) a spec parsing to zero rows makes the traceability check SKIP rather than FAIL; (2) an empty manifest reads as green because "no requirements" is treated as "nothing to audit" nearly everywhere. title: CI supply-chain guardrails + make an accepted risk actually stick (from webui #285 revert)
detail:
webui iterate-2026-07-18-unpin-actions-no-dependabot reverted PR #285
(SHA-pinned all first-party GitHub Actions + added Dependabot) and recorded the
posture as an ADR. Four FRAMEWORK gaps surfaced that let a reviewed change
contradict a recorded decision unnoticed. Ordered by leverage, not by cost:

1. PROPAGATE THE PRINCIPLE. Owner decision (2026-07-18): GitHub is repo host +
   Actions runner ONLY; no other GitHub-hosted proprietary service. Rationale is
   PORTABILITY, not cost - shipped CI templates
   (shared/templates/github-actions/*) and adopt scaffolding must not make
   adopters inherit Dependabot or any hosted service. NOTE: a parallel monorepo
   session (2026-07-18) independently reached the same conclusion via a
   cost/GHAS-availability argument; prefer the portability framing, which still
   holds where the service is free (webui is public, Dependabot is free there).

2. GAP 2 - ROOT CAUSE OF #285. An acceptance silences the TRIAGE item but NOT the
   code-scanning alerts. The repo keeps showing red for a consciously accepted
   risk, which trains the next person to "fix" it - exactly how #285 started.
   Accepting a risk must converge BOTH surfaces.

3. GAP 4 - CHEAPEST, HIGHEST LEVERAGE. classify_complexity.RISK_TAXONOMY has NO
   pattern for .github/workflows/** or .github/dependabot.yml. Changing the files
   that decide which third-party code runs with repository credentials fires zero
   risk flags. Verified TWICE: #285 recorded risk_flags: [] while running a full
   medium iterate (external plan review + code review + confidence calibration),
   and the revert reproduced risk_flags: [] on the same 7 files. Proposal: a
   touches_ci_supplychain flag, min_complexity small, enforcing mandatory review.

4. GAP 5. Nothing reads ADR Re-Review-Date - verified by grep across the
   compliance plugin and shared scripts. The ONLY expiry surface that reaches a
   human is the .trivyignore.yaml accepted-risk register rendered by the
   dashboard as "EXPIRED - re-review" (ci_security.py:163-201, :246-255). webui
   had to register a Semgrep/CI POSTURE decision in a TRIVY ignore file to get a
   due date - an acknowledged semantic stretch. Generalize it into a
   scanner-agnostic accepted-risk register.

5. GAP 3 - STRETCH, NOT COMMITTED. No audit check detects a change contradicting
   a recorded decision. Most expensive and least certain; listed so it is not
   lost, deliberately NOT promised - a triage item mixing four solvable things
   with one vague one tends to get dropped whole.

Evidence trail: webui .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-18-unpin-actions-no-dependabot.md,
webui CLAUDE.md DO-NOT #25, webui server/src/test/ci-action-pinning-posture.test.ts.
launchPayload:
Framework follow-up to webui iterate-2026-07-18-unpin-actions-no-dependabot.
Start with item 3 (touches_ci_supplychain in classify_complexity.RISK_TAXONOMY) -
smallest diff, and it is the guard that would have caught #285. Then item 2
(acceptance must converge triage AND code-scanning), then item 1 (strip hosted
services from the shipped CI template), then item 4 (scanner-agnostic accepted-risk
register). Leave item 5 unless the others land cheaply. Read the webui ADR first so
this does not re-decide the posture - it is already decided and recorded.

title: REQ-0 - Iterate: FR gate accepts requirement ids that do not exist (false green) - IN FLIGHT
detail:
FIRST of three. Order: REQ-0 (this) -> REQ-1 (test harness, trg-94337862) -> REQ-2 (campaign, trg-1b764b2c).

STATUS: code complete in worktree iterate/fr-existence-gate, NOT committed and NOT pushed. Remaining: bloat-baseline decision (record_event.py 820 -> 723), F0-F11, PR, watch to merged and green.

THE DEFECT. The finalization FR gate validates only that the declared requirement list is non-empty. Whether a declared requirement actually exists is verified ONLY by detective check D2, which is medium severity, non-blocking, post-merge, and gated behind a spec-updated watermark. An iterate can therefore declare a requirement id that exists nowhere and the gate passes - a false green in the most load-bearing gate of the finalization chain.

WHAT WAS BUILT. A new module lib/fr_gates.py holds BOTH FR gates behind one entry point run_fr_gates(), so a write path can no longer wire one gate and forget the other - the same bypass ADR-059 had to close. The pure predicate unknown_fr_ids lives in fr_classification (stdlib-only by contract). Both write paths - the CLI and the worktree finalize path - are wired.

GRADUATED ON PURPOSE. No planning directory means unverifiable, so it allows. Specs present but parsing to zero requirements allows too, but warns loudly - that is the blind-scanner case where silence reads as nothing to audit. Only an id outside a non-empty known set is a hard failure. Fail-open on unavailable is deliberately not fail-open on unknown, so a customer repo is never bricked by a gate it cannot satisfy.

VERIFIED. 4310 shared tests and 234 integration tests pass, lint clean, all touched files under their bloat baseline (record_event.py ratcheted DOWN from 820 to 723). A scan of 326 historical iterate events found ZERO ids the new gate would reject, so this is a pure tightening with no false-positive surface here.

Renumbered and promoted to a real campaign. Superseded by REQ-2 (trg-1b764b2c), which is scaffolded at .shipwright/planning/iterate/campaigns/2026-07-18-requirements-catalog with seven sub-iterates and can be started autonomously once REQ-1 (trg-94337862) is merged.

title: Three requirements-parser defects frozen by S1, fixed by campaign step S4
detail:
Three defects in the requirements table parsers, found while building the S1 golden corpus (campaign Requirements Catalog). All three are frozen as current behaviour in integration-tests/test_requirements_corpus_found_defects.py and are fixed by the SAME change - S4's single header-driven reader. Filed so they survive if S4 is descoped or resequenced.

FV-3: a requirements row carrying more columns than its header declares has a later column read as the requirement text, so the generated traceability matrix can display the wrong description for a requirement. Live in a shipped audit artifact.

FV-4: the requirements hygiene audit maps no columns at all when a table header names its first column FR instead of ID, dropping every row in that file. The four hygiene checks then report against zero rows, which reads as green.

FV-5: the same audit resets its column mapping at every heading, so a requirement row appearing under a later heading without a repeated header row is silently dropped.

Rationale and flip-step for each: integration-tests/requirements_corpus/frozen_bugs.py

title: Flaky idempotency test: dashboard render compared across a minute boundary
detail:
shared/tests/test_finalize_iterate.py::test_run_is_idempotent compares two generated dashboard renders for byte equality. Each render stamps a minute-resolution UTC timestamp into its banner, so when the two calls straddle a minute boundary the renders differ and the idempotency assertion fails.

Observed live on an unrelated PR: the two banners read 20:39 and 20:40 UTC, everything else identical. Nothing about the change under test was involved.

Effect: a time-dependent failure that reddens whichever pull request happens to run across the boundary, costing a re-run and eroding trust in a required check. The test also does not currently prove what it claims - a genuine idempotency regression would be indistinguishable from this flake.

Suggested direction: freeze the clock for the comparison, or compare with the banner line excluded, so the assertion measures idempotency rather than wall-clock alignment. A related banner-drift fix already exists in the events log helper but does not cover this path.

title: CI-Security 1/2: scanner-agnostic accepted-risk register that converges triage AND code-scanning
detail:
CI-Security 1 of 2. Splits items 4 + 2 out of anchor trg-9509c2e8 (webui
iterate-2026-07-18-unpin-actions-no-dependabot). Item 3 is DELIVERED as PR #401.

MERGED ON PURPOSE: item 4 builds the register, item 2 rewires acceptance onto it.
Done apart, item 2 would be built against the Trivy-shaped register and migrated
days later. One iterate.

GAP 4 - the only expiry surface that reaches a human is parse_accepted_risks over
.trivyignore.yaml, rendered by the dashboard as "EXPIRED - re-review"
(ci_security.py:163-201, rendered :246-255). Nothing reads an ADR Re-Review-Date
(verified by grep across the compliance plugin + shared scripts). webui therefore
had to register a SEMGREP / CI-POSTURE decision inside a TRIVY ignore file to get
a due date at all - an acknowledged semantic stretch. Generalize it into a
scanner-agnostic accepted-risk register.

GAP 2 - ROOT CAUSE OF #285. An acceptance silences the TRIAGE item but NOT the
code-scanning alerts. The repo keeps showing red for a consciously accepted risk,
which trains the next person to "fix" it - exactly how #285 started. Accepting a
risk must converge BOTH surfaces.

Do NOT re-decide the posture: GitHub-owned actions on mutable tags, third-party
SHA-pinned, no hosted updater. Portability, not cost. See webui ADR +
CLAUDE.md DO-NOT #25.

Suggested shape: register entry carries scanner + rule id + expiry + rationale ref;
one producer resolves it into (a) triage auto-dismiss and (b) a code-scanning
dismissal, so one acceptance quiets both. Expiry stays human-visible.

NOT IN SCOPE: item 5 (audit-level contradiction detection) stays deliberately
unpromised - a card mixing four solvable things with one vague one gets dropped
whole.

title: CI-Security 2/2: ship the action-pinning posture RULE to adopters (templates already correct)
detail:
CI-Security 2 of 2. This is what is LEFT of item 1 in anchor trg-9509c2e8 after
verification - most of it turned out to be already done.

VERIFIED ALREADY CORRECT (do not redo):
- shared/templates/github-actions/*.template already ship the decided asymmetry:
  GitHub-owned actions on mutable tags (actions/checkout@v4,
  github/codeql-action/...@v4, actions/upload-artifact@v4) and the one
  third-party action SHA-pinned (peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@71345be...).
- No dependabot config anywhere in shared/templates/ or the adopt plugin, so
  adopters already inherit no hosted updater.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING: the RULE is not shipped, only the current state. An
adopted repo gets correct workflows but nothing tells the next author why, so the
first well-meant "let us pin everything for supply-chain safety" silently reverses
the posture - which is precisely how webui #285 happened, in a repo that DID have
the state right.

Scope:
1. Carry the posture rule into shared/templates/claude-md-template.md so adopters
   inherit it the way webui carries CLAUDE.md DO-NOT #25.
2. A guard pinning the templates' asymmetry in BOTH directions (re-pinning a
   GitHub-owned action fails; unpinning the third-party action fails), mirroring
   webui server/src/test/ci-action-pinning-posture.test.ts. Without it the
   templates can drift back silently.

Do NOT re-decide the posture (portability, not cost - it holds even where the
hosted service is free). Independent of CI-Security 1/2 (trg-15a8e267): different
files, no shared machinery. Small.

reason: Superseded by the split. Item 3 DELIVERED as PR #401 (touches_ci_supplychain flag + non-dodgeable acknowledgement gate). Items 4+2 continue as trg-15a8e267 (CI-Security 1/2 - merged on purpose: 4 builds the register, 2 rewires acceptance onto it). Item 1 continues as trg-0ce59c05 (CI-Security 2/2 - reduced after verification: shipped templates already correct, only the RULE is missing). Item 5 left unpromised. Dismissed so the anchor stops double-counting its own children.

title: CI-Security 1b/2: converge an acceptance onto code-scanning + triage (GAP 2, root cause of #285)
detail:
CI-Security 1b of 2. Phase 2 of the split out of trg-15a8e267 (CI-Security 1/2,
which delivers the scanner-agnostic accepted-risk register itself). Numbering note:
2/2 is already taken by trg-0ce59c05 (adopter posture rule) - this is 1b, not 2.

WHY SPLIT, given the parent card said "MERGED ON PURPOSE": both external reviewers
(GPT-5.4 + Gemini 3.1 Pro) independently called the merged scope too large, and the
parent's stated reason for merging is satisfied by the split. Its worry was that
item 2 would be built against a Trivy-shaped register and migrated days later.
Phase 1 fixes the register shape first, so this card is built against the
generalized register from the start. The letter of the card is broken; its
rationale is not.

SCOPE - converge the second surface. Phase 1 makes an acceptance a recorded,
validated, time-bounded object with a both-directions drift gate and an expiry that
fails a required test. It does NOT quiet the code-scanning alerts, so the repo can
still show red for a consciously accepted risk. That is GAP 2, the root cause of
webui #285.

Build a single CLI (subcommands, one domain module) that resolves a register entry
into both surfaces: (a) dismiss the matching open triage items, (b) dismiss the
matching code-scanning alerts, with the dismissal comment derived from the register
entry. Read-only check mode first; mutation is a deliberate command, never an
automated CI sweeper - no scheduled job should hold the authority to mass-dismiss
security alerts.

VERIFIED PREMISE (do not re-litigate): code-scanning dismissals persist across
re-scans. 22 alerts dismissed 2026-06-27 carry most_recent_instance.commit_sha
7c303a8b (merged 2026-07-18) and are still dismissed. Note updated_at does NOT
advance on re-observation, so the naive probe reads as "never seen again" and
inverts the design - use most_recent_instance, not updated_at. This also corrects
the rationale recorded at decision_log.md:3319 and :3332 ("reappear each scan"),
which is factually wrong for dismissed alerts. What those ADRs actually rejected -
dismissal as a substitute for fixing - stays rejected.

CARRY THE UNRESOLVED REVIEW FINDINGS (from the Phase 1 review, all still open here):
- Define canonical per-target match keys before implementation. Rule id alone is not
  enough; loose matching dismisses unrelated alerts, strict matching creates
  permanent false drift. Reject ambiguous mappings rather than guessing.
- Verify the token can actually PATCH a code-scanning alert. Scope check says yes
  (public repo, repo scope, admin) but it was deliberately NOT proven by a test
  mutation, because the only honest test overwrites a real alert comment.
- Paginate the alert listing and verify repository identity against the checked-out
  repo before any mutation; an incomplete listing reads as "converged".
- Never dismiss an alert with no backing register entry.
- On expiry, decide explicitly how visibility is restored. Reopening only alerts
  this tool dismissed (identifiable by machine provenance in the comment) is the
  strong option; never reopen a human-dismissed alert.
- Register the new status tokens in triage_gc MACHINE_DISMISSERS / MACHINE_REASONS
  in the same diff - that pair is a decoupled SSoT and a new reason otherwise
  escapes the dismissed-pile GC.

NOT IN SCOPE: shipping the register and this convergence to adopted repos via
shared/templates. That is a third step, worth doing only once this is proven here,
and it is distinct from trg-0ce59c05 (which ships the action-pinning posture rule,
not the register).

reason: Delivered in PR #406 (iterate-2026-07-18-accepted-risk-alert-convergence): converge resolves github-dismissal entries onto live code-scanning, keyed (tool, rule, path), provenance-marked, expiry/removal reopens only its own dismissals. Triage half built against the local-scanner per-finding surface; the repo-wide gh-security aggregate is deliberately untouched.

title: Remaining shipwright_events.jsonl readers still drop concatenated records
detail:
iterate-2026-07-18-events-jsonl-record-boundary (PR #405) fixed the WRITERS (record_event.append_event/_idempotent, adopt event_seeder) and the canonical reader (lib/config.read_events). SIX read sites still use the pre-fix bare json.loads + skip-whole-line, so a concatenated line still discards BOTH records there.

Reachable in normal operation: shipwright_events.jsonl carries merge=union, and union merge is line-based, so an ordinary merge of two worktrees joins an unterminated blob last line to the next side first line. No write-time lock can guard that.

TWO TIERS, deliberately not fixed together with #405 to keep that scope honest:
  A) NO import barrier - trivially fixable, same one-line delegation as config.read_events:
     - shared/scripts/lib/events_log.py:172-174 (latest_event_dt)
     - shared/scripts/lib/events_log.py:219-221 (finalized_run_ids)
     - shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/common.py:156-158
  B) ADR-045 sys.modules[lib] barrier - the plugin ships its own scripts/lib, so "from lib import jsonl_records" resolves THERE and raises ImportError (verified empirically in PR #405 for the adopt plugin). Needs the same documented-duplicate treatment, or a real fix to the shared-import story:
     - plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/collectors/change_history.py:126-128
     - plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/audit/group_b.py:83-85 (silent continue, no warning)
     - plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/audit/group_d.py:74-76

Why it matters: these feed the compliance change-history, the audit groups and the F11 verifiers - a dropped work_completed makes a step that happened read as one that never did.

Reference implementation: lib/config.read_events in PR #405, and the regression home shared/tests/test_events_newline_integrity.py.

title: phase_timings sidecar append has no newline guard (lower risk: no union merge)
detail:
shared/scripts/lib/iterate_phase_groups.py:115 appends to .shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/<run_id>.phase_timings.jsonl with a bare open(path,"a") and no ends_without_newline probe - the same unguarded-append shape fixed for triage.jsonl (#399) and shipwright_events.jsonl (#405).

DELIBERATELY FILED SEPARATELY AND AT LOW SEVERITY: this sidecar is GITIGNORED, so unlike the other two logs it carries NO merge=union driver. The dominant vector - an ordinary git merge concatenating across an unterminated blob - does not apply. What remains is only a genuinely interrupted write, which is far rarer. Bundling it with the events-reader work would have implied a shared urgency that the evidence does not support.

Fix is a two-line change (probe + conditional separator) reusing lib/jsonl_records.ends_without_newline; the module is in shared/scripts/lib, so there is no ADR-045 import barrier. Also worth checking whether its reader recovers or skips.

title: CI-Security 3: ship the accepted-risk register + converge to adopted repos
detail: The third step named as out-of-scope in iterate-2026-07-18-accepted-risk-alert-convergence, whose precondition ('worth doing only once this is proven here') is now MET: the register ships with a both-directions offline gate (PR #404) and converge resolves it onto live code-scanning (PR #406), both green on this repo. Probe P1 of PR #404 measured the real gap: shared/templates/github-actions/security.yml.template runs raw 'semgrep scan --config auto --sarif' and uploads that SARIF untouched, so an adopted repo applies acceptance at INGEST (security_findings._findings_from_sarif, ADR-260) - triage goes quiet while code-scanning keeps the alert. The monorepo converges only because its SARIF is generated --input-from-cache findings.json AFTER normalizer tailoring, an accident of ordering rather than a designed property. So shipping this means deciding how an adopted repo gets the same ordering, or accepting that adopters converge only via the operator-invoked converge command. title: sub-iterate-runner finalizes without F3 decision-drop / F5c iterate record, and F11 does not catch it
detail: Evidence from webui campaign 2026-07-18-mission-artifacts (4 sub-iterates, all run by the sub-iterate-runner subagent under campaign mode, all reporting a clean F11 verifier): decision-drop present for 2 of 4; iterates/<run_id>.json record present for only 1 of 4; and one sub-iterate wrote its ADR DIRECTLY into decision_log.md, taking a sequential ADR number in its worktree -- exactly the collision F3 forbids (two parallel iterates each compute max(ADR)+1). No collision occurred this time, by luck. Impact: the per-run ADR and the FR record are silently lost, so release-time aggregation cannot emit an ADR for that run, and the D3 compliance check (FRs introduced via new_frs but never reaffirmed) is fed incomplete data. Wanted: (a) the sub-iterate-runner contract executes F3 + F5c as reliably as it executes F5b, (b) the F11 verifier accepts run-id ADR identity ONLY when the drop actually exists or a matching Run-ID line is present in decision_log.md, and (c) an iterate never writes decision_log.md directly. Secondary finding: append_iterate_entry.py enforces a 50-entry retention, so on a full directory each append silently evicts an older tracked record; consumers that read iterates/<run_id>.json (the webui Mission Requirement artifact does) therefore lose older runs by design -- worth confirming that is intended and documented.

title: REQ-3: make the Layers column authoritative - establish the missing test links first
detail:
The substantive half of the requirements work, deliberately left open by the catalog campaign (REQ-2).

After REQ-2 the structure is done: one catalog, one parser, one discovery helper, one table shape, traceability as a query. What is NOT done is the content question - which test levels does each requirement actually need, and how do we know.

Today 10 of the 15 requirements have no test links at all. Because of that, the campaign's converged table marks every Layers cell as inferred rather than asserting real values: an unmarked value would claim knowledge nobody has verified, and would also hard-fail the coverage gate against those missing links. That was the right call for the campaign, but it defers the real work rather than doing it.

This item is that work: establish the missing test links, then promote the Layers column from inferred to authoritative per requirement, as evidence appears. Promotion is one-way in practice - walking back a recorded coverage claim is far harder than making one - so it should happen requirement by requirement, not in a sweep.

Prerequisite: REQ-2 merged. Reference: Spec/design/2026-07-18-requirements-catalog-campaign-SPEC.md (open question 2) and the S5 sub-iterate spec, which carries the exact marker rule.

title: S2b: converge the requirement-discovery filter semantics (~10 call-site decisions)
detail:
The tail of campaign step S2, not a new campaign - file it now so it is not lost between "S2 merged" and "somebody notices the divergence is still there".

S2 extracts one shared helper for finding requirement documents and makes all 15 call sites delegate to it. The helper is deliberately PARAMETERIZED, not opinionated: each call site keeps the behaviour it has today. That preserves behaviour byte-for-byte, which is what makes S2 verifiable against the frozen corpus - but it consolidates the divergence rather than resolving it.

The divergence, measured from the corpus: at least 10 of the 15 walks include hidden directories, at least 7 include the iterate directory, 2 descend into nested subdirectories, 4 crash when the planning path is a file, and 2 do not sort at all - so which document they act on depends on filesystem order. Those are lower bounds; five walks return ids or text rather than paths, so their filter behaviour cannot be read off the return value.

This item is the convergence: decide, per call site, whether a hidden directory or an iterate document SHOULD count for that consumer. Roughly ten decisions. The corpus surfaces each as a golden diff, which is the point - but ten deliberate behaviour changes must be reviewed as ten decisions, not waved through as one refactor.

Note the only correct walk in the repo today is plan_checks._find_planning_split_dirs (filters non-directories, dot-directories and the iterate directory) - and it targets a different file, so it is not in the fifteen.

Prerequisite: S2 merged. An earlier draft folded this into S2; that was withdrawn on 2026-07-19 because it contradicts S2's behaviour-preserving criterion.

title: S5 must surface specs whose rows all fail the canonical FR-id form (zero-row parse, third state)
detail: S4 converged the FR-id tier onto the canonical FR-XX.YY form. That creates a state the traceability T1 guard still cannot distinguish: a spec present on disk, with a header it recognises, where NO row id matches - so it parses to zero rows and T1 SKIPs instead of FAILing (the FV-1 mechanism, reached by a new route). S5's acceptance criterion has been amended to name this third state explicitly; it previously covered only 'no spec on disk' vs 'spec present, no recognised header', neither of which is this. S4 shipped the raw material: the traceability manifest now carries an invalid_ids array recording every declined row with a reason (non_canonical_id, no_governing_header, row_narrower_than_header), so S5 reads an existing field rather than re-deriving it. Concrete in-tree trigger: generate_adoption_artifacts emits FR-01.{i:02d} with no cap on i, so an adopted repo with more than 99 detected routes emits FR-01.100.

title: Adopt FR-id generation has no cap: more than 99 detected routes emits a non-canonical FR-01.100
detail: generate_adoption_artifacts and feature_inferrer both emit f"FR-01.{i:02d}" with no upper bound on i. Past 99 the format widens to three digits (FR-01.100), which is not the canonical FR-XX.YY machine token. Before S4 the loose parser tier accepted it; the canonical tier now declines it, so on a large adopted repo those requirements would leave the RTM. Not silent since S4 - the row is recorded in the manifest invalid_ids array with reason non_canonical_id - but the generator should either cap the count, roll to the next group digit, or fail loudly at emit time rather than producing ids its own readers reject. Filed rather than fixed in S4 to keep that step to one concern.

title: test: bind test results to the code version they describe
detail: The test phase gate checks that a results record exists and was not produced outside the pipeline, but not that it describes the code now being checked. A record left over from an earlier commit satisfies the gate, so a change can pass on evidence that predates it. Finishes a provenance guard that is already half-built. Surfaced by the FR-01.06 negative-space pass; kept out of the requirements catalog because the catalog describes what the product does. Mint the acceptance criterion when this ships.

title: test: check journey coverage per journey, not all-or-nothing
detail: Browser-test generation from the plan's user journeys is skipped entirely as soon as any one test file exists, so a journey added to the plan later can end up with no test and nothing reports it. Replace the all-or-nothing check with a per-journey one, and report journeys with no test. Greenfield should block; brownfield gaps belong in triage instead (see the adopt cross-cutting rows). Surfaced by the FR-01.06 negative-space pass; kept out of the requirements catalog because the catalog describes what the product does. Mint the acceptance criterion when this ships.

title: test: warning-only layers should leave a follow-up, as the budget check does
detail: Three of the four layers that report a failure without stopping the run leave nothing behind once the session ends: browser tests, cross-page consistency and screen-versus-mockup fidelity. Only the performance budget files a follow-up that outlives the run. Extend that same pattern to the other three so a suite that has been failing for weeks is distinguishable from one that just started. Surfaced by the FR-01.06 negative-space pass; kept out of the requirements catalog because the catalog describes what the product does. Mint the acceptance criterion when this ships.

title: shipwright-test work unit: three decided gaps from the REQ-3 requirement walk
detail: Per-plugin work unit (the evidence ledger's convention; supersedes trg-737d0449, trg-30fc1fc6, trg-3a4466e5). Three changes the operator decided during the FR-01.06 walk, each removed from the requirements catalog because the catalog describes what the product does. Mint the acceptance criterion for each when it ships. (1) Bind results to the code version: the phase gate checks a results record exists and was not produced outside the pipeline, but not that it describes the code being checked, so a leftover record from an earlier commit passes. (2) Journey coverage per journey: browser-test generation is skipped wholesale once any test file exists, so a journey added to the plan later goes uncovered and unreported; greenfield should block, brownfield gaps route to adopt. (3) Warning-only layers leave a follow-up: three of the four non-blocking layers leave nothing behind once the session ends; only the performance budget files one. Extend that pattern. Full per-criterion enforcement status is in the ledger, not here.

title: shipwright-security work unit: two decided gaps from the REQ-3 requirement walk
detail: Per-plugin work unit (evidence-ledger convention; full per-criterion enforcement status lives in the ledger, not here). Two changes decided during the FR-01.07 walk, both kept out of the requirements catalog because the catalog describes what the product does. Mint the acceptance criterion for each when it ships. (1) Name what was not checked: the phase runs whichever of its three tools are installed and records nothing about the absent ones, so a machine with one tool produces a report that reads clean for all three classes. A tool that crashes is already surfaced as degraded and fails the run; a tool that was never there is invisible. Extend the same honesty to absence. (2) One accepted-findings answer per repository: the secret scanner run locally substitutes a generated config and ignores the project's own accepted-findings file, while the host workflow reads it, so the same repo yields different results by path. Adopt scaffolds that file for every onboarded repo. Local should extend the project file rather than replace it.

title: host-side review work unit: shipped review workflow skips the changes that most need it
detail: Per-requirement work unit for FR-01.17 (minted 2026-07-24). Two gaps in the review workflow the framework scaffolds into every onboarded repo, both decided by the operator as gaps to close rather than limitations to accept. (1) Oversized changes are skipped, not failed: the shipped template has a step that skips the review when the change exceeds a size threshold, so the largest changes pass by not being reviewed. The monorepo's own reviewer fails closed in the same situation. Make the shipped one fail closed too. (2) Changes proposed from a contributor's own copy of the repository get no review at all, because the host withholds credentials from such runs and the reviewer needs one. Every other check still runs and still blocks. The documented safe pattern is two-stage: a first run without credentials saves the change as an artifact, a second run triggered on its completion reads that artifact with credentials and never executes the contributor's code. Applies to the monorepo and the companion app as well as scaffolded repos.

title: returning to a previous version does not use the version you ask for, and reports success anyway
detail: Found by reading the code during the FR-01.08 requirement walk. The version-revert path takes the target version as a required argument, then calls the hosting API without passing it — the same call the normal release path makes, which fetches whatever is currently at the top of the branch. After a bad release that is still the bad code. It then returns success with a message naming the version it never used. The command line insists on the argument the implementation discards. Consequences: the safety net is absent exactly when it is needed, and the false success means nobody looks further during an incident. Contributing factors, all worth fixing together: the shipped target profile records this mechanic as implemented and verified; the discipline document states a target without a working way back is not a supported target; and the test file covers argument validation only — it asserts the argument is required, never that it is used. The second path (stopping the broken environment and switching to a backup copy) stops the environment but leaves the switch to a person, while also reporting success. Needs a real hosting environment to verify against, so it cannot be closed from a local session alone. The catalog was corrected to describe what the product actually does; this card carries the repair.

title: hosting-phase work unit: three gaps found by walking concrete failure scenarios
detail: Per-plugin work unit. Three decided changes, each surfaced by putting a concrete failure scenario to the operator during the FR-01.08 walk rather than by reading code. All three are unimplemented today, so they stay out of the requirements catalog; mint the acceptance criterion for each when it ships. (1) Warn before returning the code when stored data has already moved. If a data change was applied earlier in the same release and the liveness check then fails, returning the code alone leaves the older version facing a data shape it does not know. The product must say so explicitly and ask whether to proceed, instead of silently restoring into a mismatch. (2) The liveness check asks once with a ten second limit and never retries. An application that takes fifteen seconds to start is reported as a failed release, which triggers the way back unnecessarily. It should ask repeatedly until the application answers or a deadline passes, with the deadline belonging to the hosting target since a small site and a large application start at different speeds. (3) When the way back itself fails, name the state. Today the failure surfaces as a non-zero result; what is missing is stating plainly that neither the new nor the old version is running, what was last attempted and what it found, and then stopping rather than continuing to act unattended. The worst case is not that the way back fails, it is that nobody notices it failed.

title: security work unit: three decided gaps from the REQ-3 walk (supersedes trg-33b22f43)
detail: Per-plugin work unit; supersedes trg-33b22f43, which carried the first two. Third item added after a concrete scenario was put to the operator. All three stay out of the requirements catalog because the catalog describes what the product does; mint the criterion for each when it ships. (1) Name what was not checked. The phase runs whichever of its tools are installed and records nothing about the absent ones, so a machine with one tool produces a report that reads clean for every class. A tool that crashes is already surfaced and fails the run; a tool that was never there is invisible. (2) One accepted-findings answer per repository. The secret scan run locally substitutes a generated configuration and ignores the project's own accepted-findings file, while the host workflow reads it, so the same repository yields different results depending on which path asked. Local should extend the project's file rather than replace it. (3) Only compare two runs when they covered the same ground. A finding present on Monday and absent on Tuesday means fixed only if Tuesday checked the same classes; if it checked fewer, the finding is unchecked, not fixed. This is what makes item 1 worth building: it is also the reasoning that let us drop the stored per-finding outcome, since absence from the next run is only evidence when coverage is equal.

reason: superseded by trg-b4b320ce — same work unit plus a third decided item (compare two runs only when they covered the same ground). Scope unchanged, nothing dropped.

title: release-note writer destroys an existing history file it does not recognise
detail: Found by reading the code during the FR-01.09 walk and reproduced empirically. The writer has three branches. Two preserve the existing file. The third — file exists but has no section marker for unreleased work — builds the new content from a fresh header plus the new entry and never appends what was read, so the file is overwritten. A hand-written history with entries up to 1.0.0 came back containing only the new entry; everything before it was gone. Who this hits: any project whose history file does not use that marker, which is the normal case for a brownfield project onboarded with its own history. It also contradicts an existing acceptance criterion, which promises the title and older entries are left intact. Same shape as the earlier rollback defect: the two branches that work are covered by tests, the one that destroys data is the untested one. Decided fix (operator): when the file does not have the expected shape, insert at the top and leave everything else untouched, or stop and ask when safe insertion is not possible — never overwrite what was not understood. Second decided item on the same unit: a second run must not duplicate. Because setting the version marker is instruction rather than code, an interrupted run leaves the note written and unmarked; running again regenerates the same entry and appends it, leaving the same version twice. Re-running should extend or replace that version's section, and the check is cheap — one version appears once.

title: compliance work unit: evidence documents should say what they describe and when they were last checked
detail: Per-plugin work unit from the FR-01.10 walk. Two decided changes, both kept out of the requirements catalog because the catalog describes what the product does. (1) Name the state, not just the time. Each evidence document carries a generated timestamp, which says when it was written but not which state of the project it describes. The staleness check already identifies the reference snapshot by its run identifier in the commit trail, so the document could carry the same identifier and a reader could tell at a glance what it reflects. A timestamp alone cannot distinguish a document regenerated from an old state from one regenerated from the current one. (2) Disclose when the cross-check last ran. The cross-check is on demand and wired to no trigger, so in a project where nobody thinks of it for three months the divergence accumulates while the documents look unchanged and trustworthy the whole time. On demand stays right, but the documents should show when that check last happened, so a reader can weigh it. Operator decision: make the absence visible rather than close it silently with a schedule.

title: build work unit: two rules decided by scenario, neither built
detail: Per-plugin work unit from the FR-01.05 scenario pass. Both rules were decided by the operator and neither exists today, in code or in instruction. (1) When the approved mockup and the section description contradict each other, stop and put it to a person. Today the phase carries two criteria that cannot both be satisfied in that case — implement exactly what the section said, and never ignore the mockup — so whichever the builder happens to follow wins silently. The operator's position: the mockup is closer to real life because a human looked at it and judged it against real use, so the expected resolution is that the requirement is corrected to match the mockup. That makes stopping essential rather than merely careful, because a silent choice either way discards the reason mockups exist. Detecting the contradiction itself needs reading comprehension between prose and rendered markup, so it has no deterministic check; the honest ceiling is the instruction plus a record that the decision was put to someone. (2) A section that cannot be built without touching something shared may make the smallest change it needs, recorded as belonging to that section. Taken literally the existing wording makes such a section unbuildable, which is not the intent — the rule is aimed at unrequested extra work. A check is possible once sections declare their files: verify every changed file is either declared by the section or recorded as an attributed extra.

title: design work unit: what the feedback rounds change never reaches the requirements
detail: Found by the operator asking whether the design phase has a criterion for correcting the requirements from what the mockup rounds change — not only for the contradiction case. It does not. The feedback round does write back into the requirements file, but only POINTERS: which screen stands for which requirement, and cross-reference tags. Nothing writes back what changed in SUBSTANCE. So when a feedback round adds an option, removes a step or reorders a path through the product, that stays in the mockup and the requirement keeps describing the older intent. This is a source of exactly the drift this campaign exists to remove, sitting in the phase where flows are rightly rethought. Decided fix: when a round of feedback changes what a screen or flow does rather than how it looks, the requirement it belongs to is corrected before the design is approved. Deciding whether a given change is behaviour or appearance needs a human read, so that half has no deterministic check. The mechanisable half already exists elsewhere and can be copied: the change workflow declares a requirement impact per change and refuses to finish unless a requirements file was touched or a one-line reason was given for touching none. The design feedback round could carry the same declaration, which turns an unenforceable intention into a checkable one.

title: requirement write-back loop: design and build both need the same missing mechanism (supersedes trg-35785118, trg-ed419fd7)
detail: One work unit because it is ONE mechanism with two call sites, not two plugin problems. Bundling supersedes trg-35785118 (design) and trg-ed419fd7 (build); scope unchanged, nothing dropped. The loop: design is where flows are rightly rethought, and build is where a contradiction surfaces — in both places what is learned must reach the requirements instead of staying in the mockup or being resolved silently. Three parts. (1) Design: when a round of feedback changes what a screen or flow does rather than how it looks, the requirement it belongs to is corrected before approval. Today the round writes back pointers only — which screen stands for which requirement — never substance. (2) Build: when the approved mockup and the section description contradict each other, stop and let a person decide; the expected resolution is that the requirement is corrected to match the mockup, because the mockup is the thing a human judged against real use. Today two criteria make that case unsatisfiable either way, so whichever the builder follows wins silently. (3) Build: a section that cannot proceed without touching something shared may make the smallest change it needs, recorded as belonging to that section. The shared mechanism, and the reason to build these together: the change workflow already declares a requirement impact per change and refuses to finish unless a requirements file was touched or a one-line reason given for touching none. Give the design feedback round and the build section the same declaration and all three become checkable at one cost. Judging behaviour-versus-appearance and detecting a prose-versus-markup contradiction stay human reads; the declaration and the touch check do not.

title: hosting phase: the way back is broken, plus three rules found by scenario (supersedes trg-7c6de478, trg-84db1841)
detail: One work unit because all four need the same file and the same live hosting environment to verify against. Supersedes trg-7c6de478 (the critical defect) and trg-84db1841 (the scenario findings); scope unchanged, nothing dropped, severity stays critical for the first item. (1) CRITICAL. Returning to a previous version takes the target version as a required argument, then calls the hosting interface without passing it — the same call the normal release path makes, which fetches whatever is currently at the top of the branch. After a bad release that is still the bad code. It then reports success with a message naming the version it never used. The command line insists on the argument the implementation discards, and the test file covers argument validation only, so it asserts the argument is required and never that it is used. (2) Warn before returning the code when stored data has already moved forward: the older version would meet a shape it does not know, so say so and ask rather than restoring into a mismatch. (3) The liveness check asks once with a ten second limit and never retries, so an application taking fifteen seconds to start is reported as a failed release and triggers the way back unnecessarily. Ask repeatedly until it answers or a deadline passes, with the deadline belonging to the target. (4) When the way back itself fails, name the state: say plainly that neither the new nor the old version is running, what was last attempted and what it found, then stop rather than continuing unattended. title: project phase: no notion of how big a requirement should be, and the templates contradict the basis rule
detail: Per-plugin work unit from the FR-01.02 scenario pass. (1) Requirement granularity has no guidance and no check. There is guidance for how big a planning unit should be — not too broad, not too small, find natural boundaries — but nothing for a single requirement, while the phase promises requirements each scoped to be delivered on its own. This campaign is the evidence: one requirement in this very catalog carried a single acceptance criterion for an entire phase and nobody noticed for a long time. Decided rule: a capability that cannot be given acceptance criteria a single delivery would satisfy is too broad and gets divided; being unable to enumerate what would settle it is the signal that it names several capabilities at once. The judgement stays human, but the signal is observable, and a warning when a requirement has no criteria at all is buildable. (2) The templates contradict the basis rule. A criterion forbids marking a requirement as an unconfirmed assumption for a new project, because with the person in the conversation unconfirmed means unasked. The phase's own generation templates seed rows with exactly that marking and define it as nobody confirmed this, needs checking. Resolution: the marking stays available but only together with what would settle it — who to ask or what to try. The ban targets silent assuming while someone is available to answer, not honest not-knowing. The templates and the reference wording need to say the same thing; today a reader following the template violates the criterion.

title: plan phase: disagreement between reviewers is averaged away, and section order cannot be checked
detail: Per-plugin work unit from the FR-01.03 scenario pass, plus the gaps the earlier walk had already recorded. (1) Two independent reviewers can contradict each other and nothing records it. Their full texts are preserved in the review output, but the marker later checks read reduces both to one status and one finding count. So one reviewer approving while the other calls the approach fundamentally wrong looks, downstream, like an ordinary finding count. Two independent reviewers exist precisely so that disagreement is noticed; averaging it away makes the second reviewer worthless. Decided: a contradiction is recorded as its own outcome and put to the person. The comparison is deterministic once both verdicts are read. (2) Section order cannot be checked because dependencies are not expressible. The plan promises the numbering is the build order, but the manifest is a flat list of names, so nothing could establish it and a section can be scheduled before what it needs. Decided: a section names which others it presupposes, which turns an unverifiable promise into a checkable one — a numbering that places a prerequisite after its user then fails. The criterion has been rewritten accordingly; the declaration format is the work. (3) Carried from the earlier walk, same plugin: no check that every requirement lands in at least one section, no check that a section traces back to a requirement, no section-quality check, and the in-session review gate exists only as instruction.

title: CRITICAL - release-note writer destroys an existing history file it does not recognise
detail: OWNS: the changelog plugin. Independently executable. Supersedes trg-7ad0849b (title only, so the severity is visible wherever only a title is shown). Found by reading the code during the FR-01.09 walk and reproduced empirically. The writer has three branches. Two preserve the existing file. The third - file exists but has no section marker for unreleased work - builds the new content from a fresh header plus the new entry and never appends what was read, so the file is overwritten. A hand-written history with entries up to 1.0.0 came back containing only the new entry; everything before it was gone. Who this hits: any project whose history file does not use that marker, which is the normal case for a project onboarded with its own history. It also contradicts an existing acceptance criterion, which promises the title and older entries are left intact. Same shape as the other critical defect: the two branches that work are covered by tests, the one that destroys data is the untested one. Decided fix: when the file does not have the expected shape, insert at the top and leave everything else untouched, or stop and ask when safe insertion is not possible - never overwrite what was not understood. Second item: a second run must not duplicate. Because setting the version marker is instruction rather than code, an interrupted run leaves the note written and unmarked; running again regenerates the same entry and appends it, leaving the same version twice. Re-running should extend or replace that version's section - one version appears once.

title: CRITICAL - going back to a previous version does not use the version you ask for, and reports success

(1) CRITICAL. Returning to a previous version takes the target version as a required argument, then calls the hosting interface without passing it - the same call the normal release path makes, which fetches whatever is currently at the top of the branch. After a bad release that is still the bad code. It then reports success with a message naming the version it never used. The command line insists on the argument the implementation discards, and the test file covers argument validation only, so it asserts the argument is required and never that it is used. (2) Warn before returning the code when stored data has already moved forward: the older version would meet a shape it does not know, so say so and ask rather than restoring into a mismatch. (3) The liveness check asks once with a ten second limit and never retries, so an application taking fifteen seconds to start is reported as a failed release and triggers the way back unnecessarily. Ask repeatedly until it answers or a deadline passes, with the deadline belonging to the target. (4) When the way back itself fails, name the state: say plainly that neither the new nor the old version is running, what was last attempted and what it found, then stop rather than continuing unattended. The worst case is not that it fails, it is that nobody notices.

title: orchestrator: a waved-through phase leaves no trace, and resume says nothing about where it stands
detail: OWNS: the orchestrator plugin's step-advance and resume paths. Independently executable; touches no workflow file and no other plugin. Two items. (1) Overriding a phase gate leaves no trace, and skips the check entirely. When a phase fails its own validation the run pauses, which is right. If the person then says go ahead, the step is completed with the override flag set — and with that flag the validation DOES NOT RUN AT ALL. So nothing knows what the check would have said, and nothing records that an override happened. Afterwards the evidence reports only that the phase completed, which makes passed-its-checks and waved-through indistinguishable three months later. Fix: run the check regardless, record its findings, and record the override with the reason given. The rule requiring a person to be asked already exists; what is missing is that the answer lands anywhere. (2) Resume does not state where it stands. Recovery from an interrupted run exists, but nothing requires it to say which phases are finished and which one was interrupted, nor that a phase which merely started does not count as finished. Without that the person guesses, and guessing costs either duplicated work or a silently skipped phase.

title: change workflow: a concurrency warning must outlive the session, and loudly
detail: OWNS: the change workflow's parallel test-gate runner. Independently executable; touches no other plugin and no workflow file. One item. A test unit that fails when units run side by side but passes repeatedly when run alone is either a race between processes or an unreliable test. The gate deliberately does not stop - the alone-run verdict is authoritative, which is right, because the point of the re-run was to avoid false blocking. It warns instead, and the instruction says the unit must be tracked. No code creates that entry, so once the session ends the warning is gone. The operator's requirement: the entry must be created by the runner itself, must not get lost, and must be loud enough that it is not skimmed past - a race nobody wrote down returns precisely when it is expensive. Same shape as the other non-blocking checks this round has been closing: what warns and does not stop leaves a tracked follow-up that outlives the run. Note the runner already knows everything needed to write it: which unit, that it was red in parallel and green alone, and that it could not distinguish a race from a flaky test.

title: onboarding: a derived catalogue must announce itself as derived, and ask to be questioned
detail: OWNS: the onboarding plugin's artifact writers and its handover step. Independently executable; touches no other plugin. Three items, all about the same honesty problem. (1) Requirements derived from reading code are not visibly marked as derived and unconfirmed, and the handover does not say how many there are. Everything downstream then measures against a catalogue that looks confirmed and is not: traceability, coverage, drift. (2) Onboarding must leave a tracked follow-up to take those derived requirements through the shared questioning method with a person. Reading the code is a start and is not enough. This repository is the proof: its own catalogue came from onboarding, and an entire campaign now exists to repair it years later. Note the scope carefully - the campaign phase that grills requirements covers OUR two repositories, not what the product does for a customer project, so nothing today would give an onboarded project the same treatment. (3) A codebase that arrives with failing tests, or with capabilities no test covers, must have those recorded as inherited rather than counted as the project's own failures. Two halves of this were decided during earlier walks and belong here: gaps in journey coverage route to onboarding rather than blocking, and the accepted-baseline-failures list is the mechanism the test phase should also read.

title: Eight adopt scaffolders share an unguarded shared/ loader (dies FileNotFoundError, not ImportError)
detail:
Found by sweeping for the pattern rather than fixing the one reported instance during S5 review round 7 - which is what took the count from three to eleven.

Eight adopt scaffolders load shared/scripts/lib/*.py via importlib.util.spec_from_file_location with the guard 'if spec is None or spec.loader is None'. That guard can never fire: spec_from_file_location returns a non-None spec with a non-None loader even for a missing path, so exec_module raises a bare FileNotFoundError instead of a named ImportError.

Affected: automerge_setup_scaffolder, baseline_generator, ci_workflow_scaffolder, claude_review_workflow_scaffolder, codeql_workflow_scaffolder, gitattributes_scaffolder, gitleaks_config_scaffolder, security_workflow_scaffolder.

Impact is confined to the documented plugins-without-shared/ install (healed by a fail-open SessionStart hook): the user gets an unnamed FileNotFoundError rather than a message telling them which dependency is missing.

Three instances were fixed in PR #413 (adopt_brief_intake, traceability_layers, spec_table) - copy that shape: an existence check raising a named ImportError before spec_from_file_location. All eight remaining files are untouched by #413, verified per-file against origin/main.

title: Design verifier C1 demands a design-manifest from projects that never ran the design phase
detail: check_design_fr_coverage (shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/design_checks.py, surfaced as detective-audit C1) fails HIGH when .shipwright/designs/design-manifest.md is absent. That file is produced by /shipwright-design. An ADOPTED project never runs that phase - shipwright-webui has completed_steps [project, plan, build, test] and only visual-guidelines.md under .shipwright/designs/ - so the check demands an artifact from a phase that by construction never happened. The verifier already has the right shape of escape hatch for a different case: _is_no_ui_scope() skips when scope=library. It needs the equivalent for 'no design phase ran'. This stayed hidden because the check returned 'no planning FRs - coverage trivially satisfied' for months on a WRONG basis: the FR table existed the whole time and the older spec parser simply did not recognise the adopted table shape. Measured by running today's collect_requirements_from_planning against the historical specs: 2026-05-20 spec -> 32 FRs, 2026-05-22 -> 32, 2026-06-30 -> 42, while each audit of that date reported 'no planning FRs'. A parser upgrade then flipped C1 to HIGH-fail with no change to the project. Suggested fix: skip when the design phase is absent from run_config completed_steps (or when no design manifest has ever existed), mirroring the scope=library skip. Consumer note: shipwright-webui is leaving C1 open and documented rather than adding it to audit_config disabled_checks, so the producer fix is not masked.

title: Event tests block cannot record skipped tests: no --tests-skipped producer, no consumer
detail: record_event.py builds a work_completed tests block from --tests-passed / --tests-total / --tests-new / --tests-modified / --e2e-run only; there is no --tests-skipped. Nothing under shared/scripts or the compliance plugin reads tests.skipped either. Consequence: a host-gated skipped test (for example a symlink guard that degrades to it.skip on Windows without Developer Mode) has to be folded into the collected total, which makes passed < total on a green run, and the detective audit's D4 then reports every FR whose latest covering event looks like it landed in a failing build. Recording executed totals instead is correct but currently loses information in the other direction: test_evidence.py renders the shortfall as 'PASS (N skipped)', so once passed == total that disclosure disappears while the skip count lands in a field no consumer reads. Requested: (1) a --tests-skipped flag on record_event.py, (2) test_evidence.py and update_build_dashboard.py to read tests.skipped and render it, (3) D4 to key on failures rather than on the passed/total gap. Also worth noting for the same area: apply_amendments merges shallowly, so an event_amended carrying fields.tests REPLACES the whole block and silently drops sibling keys such as e2e_run - which test_evidence.py uses to classify a work event's layer. A deep-merge option, or a documented warning at the write surface, would remove a sharp edge that is easy to hit and invisible afterwards.

title: REQ3.06 [CAMPAIGN AUTONOM] Enforcement-Liste abarbeiten: Checks bauen fuer prompt-only (mechanisable) - Monorepo
detail: AUTONOME Kampagne. Der Anker, der die Enforcement-Liste des AC-Nachweis-Registers abarbeitet - das Register IST die Arbeitsliste, eine Zeile pro Kriterium, bounded pro Kriterium. GENAU ZWEI Sorten Arbeit gehoeren hierher. (1) 44 Zeilen 'prompt-only (mechanisable)': die Zusage existiert heute NUR als Anweisung in einem Prompt, ein deterministischer Check waere aber moeglich. Erst den CHECK bauen, DANN den Test - es gibt heute nichts zu testen. 39 davon tragen keine Zuordnung. (2) 15 Zeilen 'prompt-only (judgement)': hier ist KEIN Gate erlaubt (Kampagnen-Entscheidung D7 - naiv 98% Flag-Rate, zweckgebaut 0.52-0.66 Praezision, innerhalb von Wochen ignoriert). Die ehrliche Obergrenze ist ein Drift-Test, der prueft, dass die Anweisung noch dasteht. Wer hier ein LLM urteilen laesst, baut genau das, was die Kampagne abgelehnt hat. NICHT hierher: die 10 Zeilen 'enforced, untested' - Mechanismus existiert, nur der Test fehlt, das ist REQ3.05 (trg-137f48b5). Ebenso NICHT die AC-Identitaet, das Manifest, die Bindung und das Keystone-Gate - das ist REQ3.04 (trg-7085d783). Und NICHT die 25 Zeilen 'unimplemented': die bauen die Bereichskarten; sobald eine ausgeliefert ist, wird ihre Zeile 'enforced, untested' und erst dann schuldet REQ3.05 einen Test. ERSTE SUB-ITERATE, Buchhaltung: sieben 'unimplemented'-Zeilen nennen auf der Zeile selbst keine Karte (FR-01.02 #3 und #7, FR-01.03 #3b, FR-01.04 #1 und #4, FR-01.08 #6b, FR-01.15 #6). Einige sind nur in der Prosa zugeordnet - fuer einen Lauf, der Zeilen liest, unsichtbar. Zuordnung pro Zeile explizit machen, bevor irgendetwas gebaut wird, sonst faellt genau das durch, was niemand liest. REIHENFOLGE: laeuft nach den Bereichskarten (deren 'unimplemented' wird sonst waehrend des Laufs zu neuer Arbeit) und ist sauberer nach REQ3.04s AC-Identitaet, weil ein neuer Check dann benennen kann, welches Kriterium er durchsetzt. ABBRUCHBEDINGUNG pro Kriterium: wenn sich beim Bauen zeigt, dass kein deterministisches Orakel existiert, wird die Zeile auf 'judgement' umgestuft und bekommt einen Drift-Test - NICHT ein schwaecheres Gate, das so tut als ob.
