title: Three finalization/delivery checks report a weaker signal than they can compute
detail:
Three checks in the finalization / delivery path each already hold the information needed to name a cause, but report a weaker signal instead. Same defect class, adjacent code, so one iterate - not three.

Observed during iterate-2026-07-27-f0-race-triage (PR #439).

(1) watch_pr_delivery.py - says "timed out" where it could say "blocked".
    PR #439 sat green for ~25 minutes with all 10 check-runs successful and the
    PR Review status successful, while auto-merge was armed. The watcher returned
    {"status":"pending","timed_out":true} three times. The actual cause was one
    UNRESOLVED review thread, which blocks auto-merge on its own; neither the
    check rollup nor the watcher mentions threads. The data is one GraphQL
    reviewThreads query away. Suggested: report the named blocker (unresolved
    threads, and a required check that never reported at all) instead of a bare
    timeout. Lowest risk of the three.

(2) The session_handoff.md freshness check keys on mtime.
    It fires on any run that waits longer than ~10 minutes on CI, i.e.
    structurally rather than on a real defect - it warned on this run purely
    because of time spent waiting for checks. It also contradicts a decision
    this repo already recorded (2026-06-28, iterate-2026-06-28-drop-timestamp-drift):
    filesystem mtime is NOT a content-staleness signal in a git repo, because
    checkout, branch-switch and worktree creation all reset it. Suggested: key it
    on content - does the handoff name the current run_id - and delete the mtime
    path. A warning operators learn to ignore is worse than no warning.

(3) cross-layer coverage reports "could-not-determine" for the ENCOURAGED
    authoring pattern.
    shared/fr-authoring.md section 3 says the common case is to FOLD: append an
    (E) acceptance criterion to an existing requirement rather than mint a new
    row. The gate resolves behaviour change from FR-ROW diffs, so a correctly
    folded change leaves the row untouched and always lands in
    "no FR-row-level behaviour change was determinable". Suggested: compare the
    (E) lines inside the requirement's own section, not just its table row.
    Do NOT weaken it to a silent pass - "visibly undecidable" is the right
    posture and is the reason it was built that way.
    HIGHEST RISK of the three: it touches traceability gate semantics, where the
    manifest/schema contracts are deliberately frozen. Scope this one on evidence
    after reading the contracts; if it turns out to be its own piece of work,
    split it off THEN rather than guessing now.

Deliberately NOT included, so they are not silently swept in:
  - The classify_complexity touches_auth prose false positive (the literal
    "session" matching an auth pattern). Over-flagging is the fail-safe
    direction, the diff-driven risk_detectors predicates are authoritative
    anyway, and an override plus a degraded[] line is the whole cost.
  - Whether the code / doubt subagent review passes should run in autonomous
    iterates. That is an operator policy decision, not a defect.

Related, fold in only if cheap: external_review.py should mark a leg degraded
when the reply is not actually a review. On this run the Gemini leg returned an
unfinished internal monologue while the transport reported success; only the
downstream parse_status exposed it as partial. Same class - success reported,
nothing delivered.

title: Phase-canon C3 handoff freshness still keys on mtime
detail: The F11 iterate freshness check moved off filesystem mtime to a content key in iterate-2026-07-27-name-the-blocker (it now asks whether the handoff names the current run). Its twin, check_c3_session_handoff_fresh_after_phase in shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/common.py, still compares mtime against a 600s budget and is called by six phase verifiers (build, plan, design, test, changelog, deploy). It fires on schedule rather than on staleness for the same structural reason. It was deliberately left out of that iterate rather than guessed at: it is phase-scoped and has no run_id to key on, and its own docstring records that session_handoff carries no per-phase marker, so a content key has to be designed. Two leads for whoever picks it up: the canon frontmatter already carries a phase field alongside run_id, and docs/guide.md line ~2023 already DESCRIBES C3 as checking the canon-marker frontmatter, so the documentation states the intended contract the code does not yet meet. The guide was left as-is deliberately - it describes the intended invariant, and editing it to match the current behaviour would paper over the gap.

title: shared/tests and integration-tests fail 21 tests when run in one pytest session
detail: Running 'uv run pytest shared/tests integration-tests -m "not slow and not cross_plugin"' as a SINGLE invocation fails ~21 tests in integration-tests/test_shared_contracts_consumers_behavior.py and neighbours. Each root is fully green on its own (4991 and 418 as of 2026-07-27). Confirmed PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to any current change: reproduced on a clean origin/main with the in-flight branch stashed, identical 21 failures. CI and CLAUDE.md both invoke the two roots as separate pytest runs, so the combined session is an unsupported configuration - the same structural cross-root import/state collision class as the cross_plugin marker (ADR-044). Why it matters: the combined run is an attractive convenience (one junit.xml for iterate F5 evidence staging), and the failures name files the current change never touched, so they read as a regression the author just caused. Two options: make the roots compose (fix the pollution, or isolate via a conftest), or make the unsupported combination fail loudly with an actionable message instead of 21 misleading assertion errors. Found while producing junit evidence for iterate-2026-07-27-triage-defer-ci-cap.

title: [f0] shipwright-run failed in parallel and passed alone - race or flaky test
detail:
shipwright-run: red in parallel (rc 1), GREEN alone (rc 0). It is NOT xdist-allowlisted, so this is inter-unit pollution or an unreliable test.

The F0 suite runner ran this unit twice. With every unit running side by side it reported a pytest test failure (exit 1). Re-run ALONE - after the pool drained, without xdist, in a clean temp dir - it PASSED (exit 0). That alone-run verdict is authoritative, so the gate was NOT stopped.

The runner cannot tell which of these it is:
  - a race between concurrently running units (shared state, ports, temp files, the shared working tree), or
  - a test that fails intermittently on its own.
Both are real defects; only measurement separates them.

Reproduce the unit exactly as the runner re-ran it (expect GREEN):
  cd plugins/shipwright-run && uv run --with pytest --with pytest-mock pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
Reproduce the whole suite in parallel (expect the intermittent red):
  uv run shared/scripts/tools/run_test_suite.py --project-root 'C:\01_Development\shipwright\.worktrees\adopt-derived-catalogue'

The failing output stayed in that run's F0 console and is deliberately not copied here.

This entry is never closed automatically: one clean parallel run is not evidence the race is gone. Close it when the unit is fixed, or dismiss it deliberately.

title: Iterate PRs touching regenerated artifacts livelock against auto-merge on a busy default branch
detail: An iterate PR that touches regenerated artifacts cannot reliably auto-merge while the default branch is busy. Observed on PR #455: all 11 Required Checks green (PR Review included), yet the PR went CONFLICTING four times in a row. Every conflict was in a regenerated file only -- the compliance MDs, build_dashboard, session_handoff, triage_inbox -- and never in a code file. Each merge to the default branch regenerates the same set, so a PR carrying its own regenerated copies conflicts with every one of them. The check cycle takes about 7 minutes while the default branch moves faster than that, so ensure_current wins the merge only by luck. This is the limitation F11.md already documents (GitHub auto-merge does a server-side 3-way merge and never runs the regenerate-at-merge resolver); what is new is that it becomes a livelock rather than a one-off refresh when merge traffic is high. Possible directions, none evaluated: a merge driver for the regenerated set so the server-side merge resolves them the way the local resolver does; regenerating those artifacts post-merge on the default branch instead of carrying them per-PR; or a queue so only one iterate PR is mergeable at a time. Worth deciding deliberately rather than absorbing per-PR.

title: Release aggregator can write the same version twice on a re-run
detail:
aggregate_changelog.py is the writer the release path actually invokes (changelog SKILL.md Step 4). _insert_section always inserts above the first versioned heading and never checks whether a section for that version already exists. Its only idempotency comes from consuming the drop files, and the atomic write happens BEFORE the unlink loop -- so a release interrupted in that window leaves the drops on disk and a re-run inserts a second '## [x.y.z]'. It also has no stop-and-say-why arm.

Found during the FR-01.09 walk while fixing the plugin-side writer (PR #452, merged 97392eea). Deliberately scoped out of that iterate: the plugin fix cannot be imported here (wrong direction across the ADR-045 lib-collision boundary), so it is a genuine separate change.

Suggested shape: extract the section predicates to a TOP-LEVEL shared module (shared/scripts/changelog_sections.py) so both the plugin and the aggregator import one implementation without a lib collision -- the same pattern conventions.md records for tests_block.py. Then give the aggregator the same-version replace and the refusal arm. Note aggregate_changelog.py is 458 lines and carries a grandfathered bloat-baseline entry, so plan the extraction before editing it.

The FR-01.09 acceptance criterion added in PR #452 was deliberately worded to cover only what the plugin writer guarantees, so it does NOT currently overclaim -- but it will need widening once this lands.

detail:
Running the F0 suite leaves an untracked directory in the working tree: plugins/shipwright-security/.shipwright/ containing triage.jsonl and triage.jsonl.lock. It is written by that unit's own tests into the repo tree rather than into a tmp_path, and it is NOT gitignored (checked: git check-ignore returns 1; .gitignore line 136 is blank), so it shows up as untracked in every contributor's git status after any test run and is a candidate for accidental staging.

Found while investigating F0 race card f0-race:shipwright-run. That card asked whether the shipwright-run failure was inter-unit pollution or an unreliable test; it turned out to be neither (a genuine Windows os.replace bug in shared/scripts/lib/atomic_write.py, fixed in iterate-2026-07-27-run-unit-parallel-race). This pollution is a SEPARATE, real instance of the shared-working-tree class that card named, and is still open.

Two candidate fixes: point the tests at tmp_path so nothing is written into the repo at all (preferred - a test that writes into the source tree can collide with a concurrently running unit), or, if some test genuinely needs a repo-rooted path, add the directory to .gitignore. The first is the real fix; the second only hides it.

title: host checks part 2 follow-up: require the checks that currently gate nothing
detail: FOLLOW-UP to trg-c7e5835b, do this AFTER the part-2 PR (items 3-5) is merged. The new check_required_checks producer found two checks on this repo that run on every pull request, report a result, and hold nothing up because they are not in the configured must-pass set: "Empirical calibration (real OSS repos)" and "Prepare review request". Adding them is a ruleset change at GitHub (Settings -> Rules), not a code change. LANDMINE: making a check required that does NOT run on every pull request blocks EVERY pull request forever - it waits on a result that never arrives. "Prepare review request" is verified to always run. "Empirical calibration" is NOT - read grade-empirical.yml first and check its triggers before requiring it. If it does not run on every PR, leave it out and record that decision instead. Then run the same producer against the webui repo and do the same there - that part is tracked separately as trg-9e6c0b66, which also covers porting the two-stage review from shipwright#437.

title: A successful atomic-write retry is silent, so degrading contention is unobservable
detail:
shared/scripts/lib/atomic_write.py retries a Windows sharing violation on both the write and the read side. A retry that SUCCEEDS is completely silent: no counter, no log line, no event. That is deliberate for now, but it means the module swallows the one observable that would show the "unlocked readers are safe" design assumption degrading in practice.

Concrete consequence: plugins/shipwright-run/tests/test_runconfig_concurrency.py can no longer detect an internally-introduced handle held across a write for less than the budget. It goes green while the latent contention ships, and then fails hard on a slower host.

The module docstring states this limit explicitly and points here. Raised by the Stage-3 doubt reviewer during iterate-2026-07-27-run-unit-parallel-race and deliberately not built in that run: wiring a telemetry channel out of a primitive with 30 call sites is a design decision with no consumer today (YAGNI), not a bug fix.

Suggested shape when someone picks this up: expose a retry counter (or emit one note on first retry) and assert ZERO retries in test_runconfig_concurrency, since internally-coordinated writers should never need one. Decide first whether the consumer is a test assertion, an event, or an operator-facing warning - each implies a different surface.

title: No CI job runs on Windows, so platform-specific defects and fixes are unverified
detail:
Every workflow in .github/workflows runs on ubuntu-latest, so no CI job ever executes on Windows. Two consequences observed during iterate-2026-07-27-run-unit-parallel-race:

1. A Windows-only defect shipped on main and stayed green in CI. shipwright-changelog was deterministically red on Windows at commit 97392eea (a child process encoded its stderr with the locale codec while every reader decodes utf-8), and nothing in CI could see it. It was found only because a developer ran the suite locally on Windows.

2. Windows-specific fixes are verified by platform-gated tests that CI always skips. test_real_windows_reader_does_not_lose_the_write is skipped on every PR; the cross-platform coverage comes from injected-failure tests that force the branch via a mockable predicate, which is sound but is not the real OS.

Raised by the Stage-2 code reviewer and deliberately declined inside that bug fix: adding a matrix leg changes .github/workflows/**, which trips the touches_ci_supplychain risk flag and its posture-acknowledgement gate. That is a deliberate CI-posture decision of its own, not a rider on a bug-fix PR.

Suggested shape: a windows-latest leg limited to the suites where platform semantics actually differ (shared/tests plus the shipwright-run and shipwright-changelog units) rather than the whole matrix, with the supply-chain acknowledgement recorded as the gate requires. Weigh the runner-minute cost against the two failures above.

title: deferring a triage finding does not yet defer it - make the third decision mean what it says
detail: Post-merge review of PR #444 found the CLI defer subcommand records the decision correctly but almost nothing downstream honours it. Five parts, one coherent piece of work, operator decisions already taken (2026-07-27). (1) RE-IMPORT: a parked finding raised by a background check re-appears as a NEW open item on the next import, because the idempotent-append dedup only suppresses when the existing match is still open - so parking a machine-raised finding yields a duplicate open item plus a permanent parked row. DECIDED: parking takes a REQUIRED revisit date; the finding stays suppressed until that date, then returns to the open list by itself. (2) SELF-CLOSE: the auto-resolver skips anything not open, so a parked entry outlives the problem it describes even after the check goes green. DECIDED: yes, a parked entry closes automatically when its underlying finding disappears, exactly like an open one. (3) VISIBILITY: the machine-readable listing contract cannot express the parked state at all, and the rendered agent-facing document shows only a count, so both still treat a parked item as gone - while the glossary now promises the opposite. DECIDED: parked items appear on every surface in their own section; this needs a version bump on the shared output contract plus the matching consumer change in the Command Center repo. (4) UN-PARK: no surface can reverse a park, though the store permits it - so a mistaken park pushes an operator toward hand-editing the log. DECIDED: add an un-park command. (5) UNBOUNDED VIEW: the parked section prints every entry uncapped, in tension with the crowding cap the same change added elsewhere; a cap plus an elided-count line is the shape the rendered view already uses. Evidence: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-27-triage-defer-ci-cap.md and the Stage-2/Stage-3 review notes in that run folder.

title: a triage decision can be silently lost and the command still reports success
detail: Found by adversarial review of PR #444; pre-existing, shared by all three decisions (promote, dismiss, defer), not introduced by that change. The decision helpers read an item's current state OUTSIDE the store lock and then write, while the write path re-checks only that the id EXISTS under the lock - never that the state is still what the caller validated against. A background auto-resolver does the same read-then-write across a whole loop. So an operator decision landing inside that window is overwritten by the automatic one, and the command still prints its success line and exits zero. It gets worse downstream: the automatic writer's actor and reason are both on the machine-churn allowlist, so the compaction tool may then legitimately drop those lines - taking the operator's decision and its stated reason with them. Preconditions are narrow (the racing writer only ever writes an auto-resolve, and the compaction step needs an explicit apply flag and keeps a backup), but the lost update and the false success message stand on their own without either. Two parts: make the state guard hold under the same lock as the write (an expected-current-state argument is the obvious shape), and stop reporting success when the write did not land. Evidence: the Stage-3 review notes in .shipwright/planning/iterate/iterate-2026-07-27-triage-defer-ci-cap/.

title: PR review: a fail-closed verdict outlives its cause and blocks the PR forever
detail: When the Tier-3 reviewer fails closed (diff truncation, unparsable model reply), it posts a CHANGES_REQUESTED review. When a later run on the same PR succeeds it posts only COMMENTED — which does NOT clear a CHANGES_REQUESTED in GitHub. reviewDecision stays CHANGES_REQUESTED with zero unresolved threads, so mergeStateStatus is BLOCKED even though every required check is green and the branch is up to date. Observed on PR #446: five stale CHANGES_REQUESTED from superseded commits (bdd788a1, 720f0de8, 75e538c1, 2ea75602, 1086cf4e) survived the fix in #461 and six subsequent clean reviews; the PR only merged after all five were dismissed by hand. The symptom is silence — no red check, no unresolved thread, nothing naming the blocker — which cost several diagnostic rounds. Fix direction: when a review run concludes success, dismiss this bot's own prior CHANGES_REQUESTED on the same PR (or post APPROVED rather than COMMENTED). A verdict must not outlive the condition that produced it — the same honesty rule FR-01.06 just applied to the test phase.

title: update-marketplace reports up-to-date for a plugin the sync checker calls drifted
detail: Discovered while syncing the runtime cache after iterate-2026-07-27-requirement-writeback-loop; unrelated to that change. scripts/update-marketplace.sh writes into the version directory named by ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json, while scripts/check_plugin_cache_sync.py compares the cache against repo HEAD. When the repo's plugin.json version has moved past the installed one, the two disagree: the sync prints up to date and the strict checker reports drift with files present in the repo and absent from the cache. Observed for shipwright-test (installed pin well behind the repo manifest); the plugins touched by that iterate were clean. Either the sync should reconcile the installed pin with the repo manifest, or the checker should compare against the installed version so the two answers cannot contradict each other. As it stands a real un-synced plugin is indistinguishable from a version-pin mismatch, which is the case the strict flag exists to catch.

title: Cross-layer gate cannot see a behaviour change that adds criteria under an unchanged FR row
detail: The cross-layer coverage check keys 'did behaviour change?' on a changed FR TABLE ROW. The standing campaign rule is the opposite shape: 'mint the acceptance criterion when it ships' ADDS (E) criteria UNDER an unchanged row. So every delivery that follows that rule reports 'no FR-row-level behaviour change was determinable — could-not-determine' and asks a human to adjudicate. Observed on iterate-2026-07-27-test-phase-record-honesty (PR #446), which minted four criteria into FR-01.06 and shipped 95 new tests: the gate could not connect the two. The failure is benign (it says 'I do not know' rather than 'this is fine'), but it fires on EVERY criterion-minting iterate, so it becomes routine noise a human learns to wave through — the exact 'operator learns to ignore red' failure FR-01.06 was just hardened against. Fix direction: treat added/changed (E) criteria under an FR heading as a behaviour change for the same FR, not only a changed table row. Care needed: getting this wrong makes the net report too little rather than too much.

title: An unreadable run config silently demotes a driven run to standalone, disabling the override guarantee
detail:
Deferred from iterate-2026-07-27-handoff-tally-and-gate-honesty (PR #468); found by its Stage-3 doubt review and recorded under ADR-114 'Rejected'. NOT fixed there on purpose: it predates PR #438, its blast radius is every v1 caller rather than the override path, and fixing it means deciding what a corrupt config should do to a run.

What happens: _read_standalone_flag treats an unparseable config the same as an absent one and answers 'standalone'. On a run that is NOT standalone, three guarantees then switch themselves off at once: the phase gate is skipped, --force stops requiring a recorded reason, and no validation_overrides[] entry is written - i.e. the FR-01.01 evidence rule silently stops applying in exactly the degraded state where evidence matters most. Worse, the follow-on bootstrap can then atomically replace the file, discarding phase_tasks, completed_steps and any existing override log with no trace.

Note the same read already has a recorded history: an earlier finding about it (unlocked legacy migration) was fixed and dismissed, so this is a second, distinct defect on the same predicate.

Direction to consider (not a decision): distinguish 'no config' (bootstrap standalone is right) from 'config present but unparseable' (refuse to complete; do not overwrite). Whether a corrupt config should hard-stop a run is the open question.

title: grade_snapshot has no branch/commit attribution: the Grade-Trend timeline mixes divergent trees
detail: grade_snapshot events carry grade + score but nothing that identifies WHICH tree they were measured in. The emitter omits commit deliberately (the finalize-time regen runs before the F6 commit, so HEAD would still be the previous commit) and there is no branch field. Snapshots produced inside different iterate worktrees therefore union-merge into one timeline on main with nothing to tell them apart. Observed on main: A 92.5 -> F 49.0 -> A 91.5 -> B 87.4 -> C 79.9 -> F 49.0 within five days, plus 35 identical F 49.0 points on 2026-07-27 alone from 15 distinct sessions. The Ships-Log Grade-Trend sparkline this emitter was built for (M-Pre-3) therefore plots a mixture of divergent trees, not a control-posture trend for main. Needs a decision, not just a field: either attribute each snapshot (branch / merge-base / is-main flag) so consumers can filter to the main lineage, or restrict emission to main-lineage regens. Consumer side lives in the shipwright-webui repo. Found 2026-07-27 while investigating the events.jsonl main-tree append defect; the volume half of that finding is being fixed separately.

title: Adopted repos inherit derived-snapshots-off-branch without a refresh producer
detail: shared/ syncs into the plugin-cache root that every adopted repo resolves, and the change lives in the iterate skill, so every managed repo stops committing its derived compliance views as soon as this merges. Those repos have no post-merge refresh, so their views freeze at whatever main last computed. Not worse than today (a branch-local derivation is wrong there for the same structural reason) but a repo that never runs parallel iterates takes the downside without the upside. Resolve by scaffolding the refresh producer via /shipwright-adopt, or by making the behaviour opt-out for single-iterate projects. Decide before the refresh-producer iterate ships.

title: Complexity calibration: the history fall-through manufactures medium (79% of runs)
detail: MEASURED 2026-07-28 over 67 recorded runs: 79% classify medium, 16% small, 3% trivial, 1% large. The ladder therefore modulates almost nothing. Reproduced cause: the fall-through default is the median final complexity of recent runs, so with a medium-dominated history any change without a scope-keyword match becomes medium - and then becomes history itself, holding the median at medium. Self-reinforcing. Probe: 'add a missing docstring' returns medium with prior_source=history, history_prior=medium, no risk flags; keyword-matched phrasings like 'fix a typo in the guide' return small. Consequence: a docstring addition draws an iterate spec, mini-plan, approval gate, external LLM plan review, full review cascade and confidence calibration. Ceremony share per merged iterate was 54% median before the derived-snapshot change and is ~34% after it; the largest remaining item is the iterate spec at ~15%, which shrinks on its own if fewer changes are medium. PROPOSAL: do not thin the finalization - the event log, review record, changelog drop and agent-doc bullets are ~10% combined and are the evidence chain that makes Grade and compliance mean anything. Instead (1) break the ratchet: cap the fall-through at small, or compute the median only from keyword-classified runs so history cannot feed itself; (2) decide whether trivial is reachable at all - 2 of 67 is a dead tier, either widen it or remove it. Measurement method: git diff line counts per merged iterate bucketed by path; a proxy for effort, not a token or wall-clock cost.

title: Review record cannot evidence Stage 1 (spec-reviewer) — add a spec review type
detail: REVIEW_TYPES has no 'spec' entry, so the spec-compliance HARD-GATE has no row. After iterate-2026-07-28-cascade-delegated-to-nobody the Stage-1 pass RUNS in standalone mode, but the record cannot PROVE it ran: a code row sourced code-reviewer is byte-identical whether Stage 1 passed first or was never spawned. That is the not-run-versus-not-recorded distinction reviews.json exists to abolish, at the one stage the constitution calls first and blocking. This is a CORRECTNESS gap, not a visibility one. Carrying the verdict in the code row instead was built and then WITHDRAWN on that run after three independent reviewers disproved it: status=completed let a Stage-1-only row satisfy the medium+ code-quality floor although Stage 2 provably had not run; status=not_run discards the findings; the write ordering was unknowable at write time because a REJECT you intend to fix is not terminal; and the verdict was never validated so {verdict: ERROR} recorded as non-blocking. Do not re-attempt that shape. The real fix is a sixth REVIEW_TYPES entry plus a schema_version bump, which invalidates every existing reviews.json under validate_record and is read by the webui Mission contract — so it needs a cross-repo decision. Analysis: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-cascade-delegated-to-nobody.md sections 4d and 5.

title: Campaign sub-iterates get no internal reviewer cascade — before-merge step at 3f-bis
detail: The sub-iterate-runner has no Agent tool and delegates the internal cascade to the campaign orchestrator, but the autonomous loop (campaign-mode.md steps 3a-3i) has NO step that spawns it, and the window the old prose described is impossible: the orchestrator blocks at 3d on the runner's terminal DONE marker, emitted only after F6 commit and Step 5 push. So for sub-iterates built under --autonomous, spec-reviewer (HARD-GATE) and doubt-reviewer never run and have no external substitute. campaign-mode.md now states this instead of claiming otherwise. Closing it means a before-merge cascade at a new 3f-bis, and BOTH external plan reviewers plus the doubt pass said its state machine must be specified before it is built: bounded retry/abort (no unbounded runner re-spawn), row-targeted record updates via record_review_pass rather than overwriting reviews.json, a durable Stage-1 verdict the merge gate can inspect, branch/ref provenance derived from tracked campaign state with reviewer text treated as data not shell input, and revalidation on the exact SHA merged at 3g. FIRST STEP: measure whether a subagent may spawn a subagent at runtime — if yes, giving the runner the Agent tool (ADR-029 rejected option (a), rejected on token cost alone) is simpler than any orchestrator step. Analysis: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-cascade-delegated-to-nobody.md sections 4a and 5.

title: F11 review floor accepts an evidence-free row, and skips entirely when the iterate entry is missing
detail: Two pre-existing fail-open paths in check_review_record, demonstrated by the Stage-3 doubt pass on iterate-2026-07-28-cascade-delegated-to-nobody and NOT introduced by it. (1) _code_review_floor accepts external_code=completed as proof a review happened, but nothing on that row must be evidence: with --from omitted it defaults to none, build_findings returns an empty list, and the row records findings_count 0 / provider null / raw_excerpt null — indistinguishable from a fabricated one. A medium+ run can therefore ship with no review of any kind at a green gate. The prescribed campaign command no longer makes the payload optional, but the gate still does not require it. Candidate fix: require the floor-satisfying row to carry non-null provider or raw_excerpt, or a recorded_by naming an adapter other than none. (2) check_review_record returns skipped when find_entry_by_run_id finds nothing (complexity reads unknown), so a missing or not-yet-written iterate entry is a silent pass — reproducible today by running the verifier before F5c. Decide whether a missing entry should skip or fail. Both need a deliberate change to the floor's contract, which is why they were not folded into a bug-fix iterate.

title: [f0] shipwright-run failed in parallel and passed alone - race or flaky test
detail:
shipwright-run: red in parallel (rc 1), GREEN alone (rc 0). It is NOT xdist-allowlisted, so this is inter-unit pollution or an unreliable test.

The F0 suite runner ran this unit twice. With every unit running side by side it reported a pytest test failure (exit 1). Re-run ALONE - after the pool drained, without xdist, in a clean temp dir - it PASSED (exit 0). That alone-run verdict is authoritative, so the gate was NOT stopped.

The runner cannot tell which of these it is:
  - a race between concurrently running units (shared state, ports, temp files, the shared working tree), or
  - a test that fails intermittently on its own.
Both are real defects; only measurement separates them.

Reproduce the unit exactly as the runner re-ran it (expect GREEN):
  cd plugins/shipwright-run && uv run --with pytest --with pytest-mock pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
Reproduce the whole suite in parallel (expect the intermittent red):
  uv run shared/scripts/tools/run_test_suite.py --project-root 'C:\01_Development\shipwright\.worktrees\security-pyasn1-bump-brace-accept' --run-id iterate-2026-07-28-security-pyasn1-bump-brace-accept

The failing output stayed in that run's F0 console and is deliberately not copied here.

This entry is never closed automatically: one clean parallel run is not evidence the race is gone. Close it when the unit is fixed, or dismiss it deliberately.

title: F11 ledger gate validates the previous run's data after the derived-snapshot restore
detail: check_test_completeness_ledger reads shipwright_test_results.json.iterate_latest.test_completeness but never compares iterate_latest.run_id to the run being verified. Since that file is in DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS, the verifier's own mandated fix (git restore --source=HEAD~1 -- <derived paths>, then amend) reverts it to the PRIOR run's content. Observed on this run: the gate reported 'complete: 30 tested, 1 untestable' while this run's ledger had 6 behaviours; the numbers belonged to iterate-2026-07-27-checks-that-gate-nothing. The gate passes on another run's evidence. The sibling session_handoff check has the same root cause but DOES compare run ids, so it degrades to a WARN instead of a false pass. Suggested fix: make the ledger check assert iterate_latest.run_id == run_id and fail closed on mismatch, and decide where a per-run ledger should live given the file may not ship.

title: uv.lock raises no touches_build risk flag (TOUCHES_BUILD_FILE_PATTERNS is JS-only)
detail: risk_detectors.TOUCHES_BUILD_FILE_PATTERNS lists package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lockb, npm-shrinkwrap.json and the JS build configs, matched by basename. A Python lockfile (uv.lock, poetry.lock, requirements*.txt, Pipfile.lock) therefore raises no touches_build flag, even though it is just as much a build input and this is a Python monorepo. Noticed while changing plugins/shipwright-plan/uv.lock: the change was correctly classified small, but purely because the detector cannot see Python lockfiles at all. Not fixed in that iterate on purpose - widening the pattern list changes risk classification, and therefore the enforced phase set, for every future iterate that touches a Python lockfile, which deserves its own run rather than riding along with a security remediation.

title: WebUI Grade-Trend must group grade_snapshot by tree attribution, not plot every point
detail: Producer side landed: every grade_snapshot now carries lineage (main|branch|unknown), branch and base (merge-base with the default branch). Consumer side is unchanged and still folds EVERY snapshot into one chronological series ordered by ts - shipwright-webui server/src/core/run-data-join.ts projectGradeTrend, whose only filter is 'has a grade'. So the sparkline still plots a mixture of trees. Required change: group by base, keep the latest snapshot per base, and order the bases by general ancestry / topological position in the default branch history. NOT by first-parent index: base is only guaranteed to be a common ancestor reachable from the default branch. Also: an ABSENT lineage means the event predates attribution (183 legacy events, not backfillable) and must be excluded from a lineage series - it is not the same as an explicit lineage=unknown. Contract documented in docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md under 'grade_snapshot attribution'.

title: Nothing measures the default branch itself, so a main-lineage grade series is empty by construction
detail: Empirical: 18 of 18 sampled grade_snapshot events (of 183) were introduced onto the default branch by an iterate PR squash commit, and the default branch working tree has no uncommitted event lines. Every snapshot ever emitted was measured inside a worktree on a branch. Cause: the three regen sites all run in the worktree - finalize_iterate F5b, ensure_current, resolve_churn_conflicts - and no producer runs after a merge. Consequence now that attribution shipped: filtering lineage==main yields zero points. That empty is honest but it means the Control-Grade trend can never describe the default branch until something measures it. Options to decide, not assume: regen after a merge; or regen at worktree setup, where HEAD is the freshly fetched default tip with zero delta and the measurement is genuinely main-lineage. Both put a full compliance regen on a critical path, which is the cost that needs the decision. Deliberately NOT bundled into iterate-2026-07-28-grade-snapshot-lineage, which only made each snapshot say which tree it measured.

title: grade_snapshot emits on every regen: unchanged repeats bloat the event log and a main-root append has no delivery path
detail: The volume half of the 2026-07-27 grade_snapshot observation. The attribution half is owned by iterate-2026-07-28-grade-snapshot-lineage (closes trg-72a9d195), whose spec explicitly hands this half over as being fixed separately - it is not. Nothing is in flight for it. EVIDENCE: shipwright_events.jsonl holds 587 lines, 172 of them grade_snapshot (29 percent), across 16 distinct grade/score values with only 29 value transitions in 16 days - roughly 83 percent of those lines carry no new information. On 2026-07-27 alone: 35 snapshots from 15 distinct sessions, every one identical, one of them with an empty session field. The emitter documents the no-dedup choice deliberately and delegates dedup to the WebUI, on the premise that a regen is an explicit act (a run finished); 15 sessions in one day falsifies that premise. SECOND HALF - the loss path: a regen whose project root is the main tree leaves a tracked-dirty event log. Unlike the triage log, the event log has no outbox and no sweep (deliberately - it was designed for exactly one producer running inside a worktree). The sync tooling then aborts with exit 6 (merge_failed) and the eingeuebte operator response is to discard the file, which destroyed a real event on 2026-07-27 at 19:26:47Z. This is a return of the class fixed in 2026-05 after 9 events were wiped; the seal built then (commit_event_followup) was scoped to the iterate flow and never runs for an idle-main append. PROPOSED SCOPE: (1) skip the append when the grade and score are unchanged - LANDMINE: the log is union-merged and therefore NOT ordered by ts, so the comparison must target the chronologically newest snapshot, never the last line of the file; (2) make the sync step seal a stranded event append via the existing commit_event_followup helper instead of aborting - this is producer-agnostic and closes the class, not just this producer, and it belongs at sync time rather than in the regen path because the 2026-06-07 design explicitly rules out git commit in a background hook hot path; (3) make the exit-6 message stop pointing implicitly at a destructive discard. DELIBERATELY OUT: removing the leak-guard exemption for the event log (the fail-closed follow-up noted in the 2026-05-29 spec) - with about 30 parallel worktrees it would turn an unrelated session red, and item 2 makes it redundant.

reason: Fixed and delivered in PR #472 (squash 23329f57). The aggregator now replaces a same-version section instead of appending a duplicate, but only when replacing cannot lose anything; otherwise it refuses, leaving CHANGELOG.md and every drop untouched. Section predicates extracted to top-level shared/scripts/changelog_sections.py + changelog_splice.py per ADR-045, so both writers share one implementation. Verified end-to-end against the synced runtime plugin cache: 1 section, no duplicate.

title: Changelog aggregator does not preserve BOM / line endings the plugin writer preserves
detail:
shared/scripts/changelog_splice.py records this at the top of the module, and the iterate spec under 'Out of scope' -- neither of which anything sweeps, so it would otherwise be forgotten.

The two changelog writers now share the section PREDICATES (shared/scripts/changelog_sections.py) but NOT the splice. plugins/shipwright-changelog/scripts/lib/changelog.py::update_changelog carries its own because it additionally preserves a UTF-8 BOM and the file's own line endings (PR #452 AC12). changelog_splice.apply_section does not: it splices an LF-rendered section between whatever head/tail the file already had.

Consequence, observed and accepted in PR #472: on a CRLF checkout a converging re-run compares equal (normalize_body folds CRLF->LF), then produces new_text != changelog_text, reports 'replaced' rather than 'unchanged', rewrites, and leaves that one section LF inside a CRLF file. It converges after a single write, so there is no loop and no content loss -- but AC11's 'a converging re-run writes nothing' is false there, and the aggregator silently changes the line endings of the section it touches. A BOM would be dropped the same way.

Shape: give changelog_splice the _read_preserving / _to_eol behaviour update_changelog already has (detect BOM + dominant EOL, re-express the rendered body, carry the BOM through), then fold the two splices into one so there is a single implementation rather than two that agree only by review. Pin it with a CRLF and a BOM fixture driven through aggregate() end-to-end, not just apply_section -- the aggregator reads with read_text, whose universal-newline translation currently hides the CRLF case from any library-level test.

title: A commit-blocking gate is named for security but counts review findings
detail: The PreToolUse hook check_security_scan (shipwright-compliance) blocks every Bash git-commit while the RTM's 'Unresolved findings' row exceeds enforcement.allowed_critical_findings, which defaults to 0 and is unset in this repo. Two separate problems. (1) NAMING: the row it reads sits in the RTM's review-findings block (Total review findings 66 / Unresolved findings 24) and is unrelated to the security scan, which reports critical_gate=pass with 3 open high/critical. An operator reading the block message concludes a vulnerability is in the way. The docstring says compliance findings, so the subject is intended; the NAME is the defect. (2) EFFECT: with 24 unresolved and a threshold of 0, no commit can be made in this repo at all. compliance_overrides.log holds exactly one override (2026-06-27) for the same count, so the gate has been passing or being bypassed unlogged since. Worth deciding deliberately: resolve the 24, set an explicit threshold with a recorded rationale, or rename the hook and split the two subjects. Related in kind to #475 (checks that ran, reported and gated nothing) inverted: this one gates, on a subject its name misstates.

title: Campaign sub-iterates get no internal cascade — give the runner the Agent tool (nested spawning MEASURED to work)
detail: Supersedes trg-d6cc3d3d, whose first instruction ('measure whether a subagent can spawn a subagent') is now answered. MEASURED 2026-07-28: a general-purpose subagent found the Agent tool in its own tool list, called it, and its nested child returned NESTED_OK. Config agrees — Explore and Plan are declared 'All tools except Agent' while general-purpose and claude carry 'Tools: *'; the explicit exclusion only makes sense if * includes Agent. THE PROBLEM (unchanged): the sub-iterate-runner has no Agent tool and delegates the internal cascade to the campaign orchestrator, but the autonomous loop in campaign-mode.md steps 3a-3i has NO step that spawns it, and the window the old prose described is impossible because the orchestrator blocks at 3d on the runner's terminal DONE marker, emitted only after F6 commit and Step 5 push. So spec-reviewer (HARD-GATE) and doubt-reviewer never run for runner-built sub-iterates and have no external substitute. WHAT CHANGES WITH THE MEASUREMENT: the before-merge 3f-bis state machine is probably unnecessary. The simpler fix is adding Agent to the tools: frontmatter of plugins/shipwright-iterate/agents/sub-iterate-runner.md, letting the runner spawn its own cascade BEFORE its own commit — which is where reviews belong, and which needs no bounded-retry loop, no row-targeted record updates, no branch-ref provenance and no revalidation on the merged SHA. WHAT STILL NEEDS DECIDING: ADR-029's actual objection was token cost ('the runner already has Bash/Edit/Write and Agent would double-spend tokens'), not feasibility. That trade-off is now the only open question — measure the cost of a runner that fans out three reviewer stages per sub-iterate against the cost of shipping campaign sub-iterates with no spec-compliance gate. Analysis: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-cascade-ask-before-lapse.md section 3a.

reason: Superseded by trg-71d7a4fa — NOT resolved; the campaign cascade gap is unchanged. This card's FIRST STEP ('measure whether a subagent can spawn a subagent') was answered 2026-07-28: nested spawning WORKS (a general-purpose subagent called Agent; its child returned NESTED_OK). Left open, it sends the next reader to re-run a done measurement and to build the 3f-bis state machine that result probably makes unnecessary. The successor carries it and reframes the open question as token cost.

title: grade_snapshot stamps lineage=main on a pre-commit iterate worktree, defeating the filter it was built for
detail: Shipped in PR #485. resolve_tree_lineage derives lineage from COMMITTED ancestry while grade and score are computed from the WORKING tree, and the two disagree exactly where it matters. An iterate worktree is created at the fork point and F5b emits the snapshot BEFORE the F6 commit, so HEAD is still the fork point, merge-base --is-ancestor exits 0, and the event is stamped lineage=main while the measured tree holds the entire uncommitted change set. Reproduced: a branch at the fork point with a dirty working tree resolves to TreeLineage(lineage=main, branch=iterate/simulated). The consequence is worse than the original defect, because the phantom point is now labelled authoritative rather than merely unlabelled. PR #485's own emitted event read branch only by luck: a chore(triage) sweep commit landed on the branch before F5b, so HEAD was not the fork point. Run-shape dependent, so the durable log will hold a silent mix. Candidate fix: reach the ancestry test ONLY when branch is None or branch equals the default branch - ancestry exists for detached HEAD, and a named non-default branch never needs it. Consider additionally carrying a dirty flag so a measurement taken over uncommitted changes discloses itself rather than being labelled by its commit. The test test_branch_with_no_commits_of_its_own_is_still_main_lineage asserts the buggy behaviour and must be inverted. Found by the internal code-reviewer subagent; two external models missed it across two rounds.

title: event_amended --fields can overlay grade_snapshot attribution, and the pipeline doc claims it cannot
detail: Shipped in PR #485. record_event.py validates only the tests block inside event_amended --fields, and lib/events_amend.apply_amendments folds an amendment onto its target with a blind dict merge - no field allowlist, no target-type check. So record_event.py --type event_amended --amends <snapshot-id> --fields with lineage main writes a false main-lineage attribution from the same binary into the same durable log, exit 0. Reproduced end to end: a snapshot honestly emitted as lineage=branch score=12 reads back to any amendment-folding reader as lineage=main branch=main score=99.9. Three in-repo readers fold amendments (change_history, group_d, _fr_history_events). NOT a regression introduced by #485 - the channel could always overlay arbitrary fields, including score. What #485 added is an unqualified claim to the contrary, rendered into docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md as no caller can manufacture a false main-lineage point in the log the grade trend is read from. That sentence sits in the document CLAUDE.md designates the single source of truth and is addressed at a cross-repo consumer deciding whether to trust attribution. Two mitigations already hold: the event_amended record persists so the edit is auditable, and the actual trend consumer projectGradeTrend does not fold amendments. Fix in two parts: refuse lineage, branch and base keys in --fields the same way the tests block is already validated there (verified safe - those three keys occur on no other event type and no existing amendment overlays them), and qualify the doc sentence to say no PRODUCER exposes a way to supply it. Found by the internal spec-reviewer subagent.

title: Root cause behind the grade_snapshot lineage defects: attribution reads committed state, the grade reads the working tree (supersedes trg-ca4fc0e7, re-scopes trg-1603000f)
detail: One mismatch explains three separately-found defects in PR #485. lineage and base are derived from COMMITTED ancestry; grade and score are computed from the WORKING tree. Symptom A (code-reviewer): a pre-F6 iterate worktree sits at the fork point, so ancestry says main while the measured tree holds the entire uncommitted change set - reproduced. Symptom B (doubt-reviewer): whenever lineage is main, merge-base(HEAD,default) equals HEAD by the resolver's own definition, so base is the PREVIOUS commit at any pre-commit regen - precisely the defect for which recording commit was rejected, and docs rule 4 claims base does not have it. Candidate fix has two halves: reach the ancestry test only when the branch is unnamed or equals the default branch, and carry a dirty flag so a measurement taken over uncommitted content discloses itself instead of being labelled by a commit it does not describe. shared/scripts/source_state_git.resolve_git_state already computes commit-plus-dirty and is the established precedent. ALSO CORRECTS trg-1603000f, which claimed nothing measures the default branch: verified false. Every PHASE_REPORTS entry in update_compliance includes dashboard, the branch that emits, and /shipwright-compliance SKILL.md line 87 plus the run-orchestrator per-phase regen both execute on default-branch trees in greenfield and adopted projects. What is actually true for THIS repo is narrower: a main-tree append is never committed, so it does not survive. docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md states the general claim as single source of truth and is wrong for the projects the plugins ship to.

title: The 18/18 probe that decided the grade_snapshot design cannot discriminate; the decision needs re-hanging on its other two arguments
detail: Methodology defect worth recording because the reasoning pattern will recur. PR #485 rejected the restrict-emission alternative on this probe: for 18 of 183 snapshots, git log -S <event-id> -- shipwright_events.jsonl piped to tail -1 named an iterate PR squash commit in 18 of 18 cases. The spec calls it THIS PROBE IS THE DECISION. It is non-discriminating: this repo squash-merges every PR, so every line reaching the default branch is introduced by exactly one squash commit no matter which tree produced the measurement. The hypothesis all snapshots were emitted in worktrees and the hypothesis some were emitted on a default-branch tree and later swept in produce byte-identical output. The probe measured which snapshots SURVIVED, not which were EMITTED. The decision to attribute rather than restrict is probably still correct, but it must be re-hung on the two arguments that do survive scrutiny: restricting on a fresh-base condition drops data silently, so a producer that has quietly stopped is indistinguishable from a quiet project; and branch measurements are the only data that can ever answer whether a change improved the grade. Action: correct the spec's Alternatives section and the ADR rationale so a future reader does not inherit the bad inference, and correct docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md where the same enumeration is stated as fact. No code change.

title: no-silent-revert: three deferred narrowings from the false-positive fix
detail:
Found by the review cascade during #488 and deliberately NOT fixed there, so they are recorded rather than lost. None is a false-negative in the gate's blocking direction; all three are small and independent.

(1) DERIVED-ARTIFACT DEFINITION DRIFT (Stage 3, low; pre-existing since #477). The verifier asks 'path in CHURN_ALLOWLIST', while the churn resolver's own churn_merge.classify uses 'CHURN_ALLOWLIST or is_campaign_status(rel)'. A campaign status.json is regenerated churn to the resolver and authored content to the verifier. Fix: have the verifier use the resolver's predicate so the two cannot drift on what 'derived' means.

(2) THE PRE-FLIGHT CAN SKIP A CHECKOUT THAT COULD HAVE BEEN CHECKED (Stage 1 + Stage 2, low). check_no_silent_revert resolves the default ref and then validates it, so a checkout that has origin/main but no local main returns SKIPPED even though a valid comparison was available. Fail-honest, never a false green, and it does not arise in the F11 worktree flow where the local ref always exists. Fix would be a fourth outcome in resolve_default_ref (local unresolvable + remote resolvable -> remote); that is spec-visible, so record it as an acceptance-criterion amendment rather than slipping it in.

(3) TWO NOTIONS OF 'THE SAME LINE' (self-review, low). Lines are compared after .strip(), but the hunk pairing diffs whitespace-insensitively (-w) so that a reformat cannot swell one hunk to the whole file. A line whose INTERNAL whitespace changed is therefore a finding that no hunk can pair with, i.e. it reports. That is the safe direction and arguably correct (it is a real edit), but the asymmetry is worth removing by normalising internal whitespace everywhere -- deliberately not done late in #488 because it changes what 'the same line' means for the whole detector.

title: Triage delivery surface: 29 audited findings, 3 verified high
detail: Two independent fresh audits of the triage store and its outbox delivery machinery (data-loss lens and concurrency/atomicity lens) found 33 raw / ~29 distinct findings. Full detail, per-finding file:line, fix direction and verification status: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-triage-delivery-audit-FINDINGS.md. Three are verified by hand and are small: the sweep's reader decodes strictly where its hardened sibling uses surrogateescape (crashes worktree setup after the worktree exists); the tracked store's header recovery path truncates before writing, bypassing the atomic write primitive every other writer uses; and the GC republishes the outbox from a read taken before a git commit that is budgeted at 120 seconds, destroying any append that lands in between - while the sibling module re-reads before its own write 20 lines earlier for exactly that reason. The remaining 26 are reviewer claims and are explicitly NOT verified; the document says so per finding, because this same session saw two confident mechanism claims turn out false. Roughly half are one-line hygiene (missing encoding, missing timeout, a fail-open except) and half are their own design changes (permission bits across ~30 call sites of a shared primitive, a new expected-status parameter on mark_status, bidirectional boundary recovery). Both audits also record what they attacked and could NOT break - the locking model, the atomic write on Windows, the plan-then-commit ordering - so this is not a blanket condemnation of the surface. Context: the audit was commissioned because two 2026-06-08 counters (16/4 and 20/8) make a hook block every commit in this repo, and their evidence was deleted. The document establishes from git history that the remediation did land on main, and that the counter under-reports by construction because review.fixed is written before the fixes exist on an append-only log.

title: IT-1 Triage-Store und Delivery haerten: 3 verifizierte High plus ~29 Audit-Befunde
detail: KONSOLIDIERT trg-7b6f13df + trg-93ceb2b0 + trg-51f8e2a1 + trg-0a294ef3. DREI Iterates unter EINEM Anker, interleaved-serial - bewusst KEINE Kampagne: der sub-iterate-runner hat kein Agent-Tool, also laufen spec-reviewer (HARD-GATE) und doubt-reviewer fuer Kampagnen-Sub-Iterates NICHT (siehe IT-7b); ausgerechnet die datenverlustkritischste Oberflaeche durch den einen Modus ohne Spec-Compliance-Gate zu schicken ist verkehrt herum. Ausserdem ueberspringt der Runner F5/F5c+F2, und die drei Einheiten haben verschiedene Form. S1 - die drei VERIFIZIERTEN High plus die billigen Nachbarn (Befunde 4/6/7/8, gleiche Dateien): strikter Decode im Sweep-Reader (sweep_text.py:50, kein errors=) crasht setup_iterate_worktree Schritt 5, nachdem git worktree add schon erfolgreich war -> verwaister Worktree; Truncate-then-Write auf dem getrackten SSoT (triage_header.py:48-52, einziger Ganzdatei-Rewrite der durable_atomic_write umgeht, auf einem Recovery-Pfad); der GC publiziert die Outbox aus einem Read von VOR einem git commit mit timeout=120 (sweep_outbox.py:133 -> :233) - jeder Append im Fenster ist weg und der Sweep meldet Erfolg, waehrend der Schwesterpfad commit_main_tracked_drift:256 20 Zeilen frueher genau deswegen neu liest. S2 - expected_status unter dem Lock: deckt trg-93ceb2b0 (Operator-Entscheidung wird vom Auto-Resolver ueberschrieben, Kommando meldet trotzdem Erfolg, exit 0) und Audit-Befund 19 (vier Aufrufer, identische Ursache) mit EINEM Mechanismus ab. Contract-Bump und WebUI-Konsument, Un-Park, Cap. trg-0a294ef3 (stiller erfolgreicher atomic-write-Retry) reitet auf S1 mit - gleiche Primitive. RESTLISTE BLEIBT IM ANKER, nicht als eigene Karten: Audit-Befunde 14 und 20-29 (Design-Aenderungen plus ~34 LOC Duplikation). ACHTUNG: die Evidenzdatei ist noch UNTRACKED und muss mit S1 eingecheckt werden.

title: IT-2 Grade-Snapshot-Attribution und Event-Log-Integritaet: eine Ursache, sechs Nachbeben
detail: KONSOLIDIERT trg-aea8c97e + trg-ca4fc0e7 + trg-1603000f + trg-5e945a39 + trg-465a2caf + trg-c97faa35 - alle sechs sind Nachbeben von PR #485. trg-aea8c97e benennt die EINE gemeinsame Ursache: Attribution liest committed ancestry, Grade und Score messen den Working Tree. Symptom A: ein Pre-F6-Worktree sitzt am Fork-Point, also sagt ancestry 'main', waehrend der gemessene Baum den gesamten uncommitteten Change-Set haelt - reproduziert. Symptom B: wenn lineage main ist, ist base per Definition des Resolvers der VORHERIGE Commit. trg-ca4fc0e7 ist dort explizit als superseded markiert; trg-1603000f (nichts misst den Default-Branch; 18 von 18 gesampelten Snapshots kamen per Squash auf main) wird ausdruecklich re-scoped. trg-5e945a39: 172 von 587 Event-Zeilen sind grade_snapshots, 16 distinkte Werte bei 29 Uebergaengen in 16 Tagen -> ~83 Prozent ohne neue Information; am 2026-07-27 allein 35 Snapshots aus 15 Sessions, alle identisch. Plus der Verlustpfad fuer einen Main-Root-Append. WENN DIE SPEC UEBER 5 ACs WAECHST: diese Haelfte als zweiten Iterate abspalten. trg-465a2caf: die 18/18-Probe, auf der die Design-Entscheidung hing, kann nicht diskriminieren (dieses Repo squash-merged alles, also fuehrt jede Zeile auf genau einen Squash-Commit zurueck, egal welcher Baum sie erzeugt hat) - die Entscheidung ist wahrscheinlich weiter richtig, muss aber auf ihre zwei tragfaehigen Argumente neu aufgehaengt werden; reine Record-Arbeit, gleicher PR. trg-c97faa35: event_amended --fields kann Attribution UND Score ueberschreiben (reproduziert: lineage=branch score=12 liest zurueck als lineage=main score=99.9), und docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md behauptet das Gegenteil - anderer Code, derselbe Doc-Absatz, gleicher PR. NICHT hier drin: trg-d190cc37 (WebUI-Konsument, anderes Repo, bleibt eigene Karte). Brief: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-triage-consolidation.md

title: IT-3 F11 sagt die Wahrheit ueber den Lauf, den es prueft: vier Fail-Open-Pfade im selben Gate
detail: KONSOLIDIERT trg-81fbf8ed + trg-51a57370 + trg-64372769 + trg-ffddd6b9. Ein Blast Radius: shared/scripts/verifiers/ plus record_review_pass.py plus der reviews.json-Contract. VORAUSSETZUNG: IT-0 muss record_review_pass.py (395 Zeilen, keine Baseline) zuerst baselinen, sonst blockt der Stop-Hook bei Beruehrung. (1) trg-81fbf8ed, der gefaehrlichste Einzelbefund im Backlog fuer eine autonome Kampagne: check_test_completeness_ledger vergleicht nie iterate_latest.run_id mit dem geprueften Lauf. Da die Datei in DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS liegt, setzt der vom Verifier SELBST vorgeschriebene Restore sie auf den Vorlauf zurueck - beobachtet: 'complete: 30 tested, 1 untestable', waehrend der Lauf 6 Verhalten hatte; die Zahlen gehoerten einem anderen Run. (3) trg-64372769: REVIEW_TYPES hat keinen 'spec'-Eintrag, also kann der Stage-1-HARD-GATE nicht BEWEISEN, dass er lief - eine code-Zeile ist byte-identisch, ob Stage 1 vorher bestand oder nie gespawnt wurde. Fasst dieselbe Datei und denselben Contract an wie (2); getrennt geschickt ueberschreiben sie sich. (4) trg-ffddd6b9 (low): drei Verengungen am no-silent-revert-Check - Derived-Definition driftet gegen churn_merge.classify, Pre-Flight skippt eine pruefbare Lage, dritter Punkt in der Karte. title: IT-5 Klassifikation und Risiko-Erkennung: 79 Prozent aller Laeufe sind faelschlich medium
detail: KONSOLIDIERT trg-ee7b83e5 + trg-496e63a7. Beide aendern, WELCHE PHASEN FEUERN - gleicher Blast Radius, und der Hebel wirkt auf jeden folgenden Iterate. VORAUSSETZUNG: IT-0 muss tests/test_classify_complexity.py (317 Zeilen, keine Baseline) zuerst baselinen. (1) trg-ee7b83e5, gemessen ueber 67 aufgezeichnete Laeufe: 79 Prozent medium, 16 small, 3 trivial, 1 large - die Leiter moduliert also fast nichts. Reproduzierte Ursache: der Fall-Through-Default ist der Median der juengsten Historie, also wird jede Aenderung ohne Scope-Keyword medium und dann selbst zur Historie, die den Median bei medium haelt. Selbstverstaerkend. Probe: 'add a missing docstring' liefert medium mit prior_source=history, history_prior=medium, keine Risk-Flags; keyword-gematchte Formulierungen wie 'fix a typo in the guide' liefern small. Folge: eine Docstring-Ergaenzung zieht Iterate-Spec, Mini-Plan, Approval-Gate, externes LLM-Plan-Review, volle Review-Cascade und Confidence-Kalibrierung. Zeremonie-Anteil pro gemergtem Iterate: 54 Prozent Median vor der Derived-Snapshot-Aenderung, ~34 Prozent danach. (2) trg-496e63a7: risk_detectors.TOUCHES_BUILD_FILE_PATTERNS listet nur JS-Buildinputs (package.json, lockfiles, JS-Configs), per basename gematcht. uv.lock, poetry.lock, requirements*.txt und Pipfile.lock loesen in einem Python-Monorepo also KEIN touches_build aus. RISIKO: eine Kalibrierungsaenderung mitten in einer Kampagne verschiebt Gates - klar vor REQ-3 oder klar danach, nicht mittendrin. Brief: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-triage-consolidation.md

title: IT-6 Run-Config-Integritaet: eine unlesbare Config schaltet drei Garantien gleichzeitig ab
detail: KONSOLIDIERT trg-f2d69527 + trg-d1e466aa. Gleiche Datei-Familie (config_factory plus run_config-Schema), deshalb gebuendelt. (1) trg-f2d69527: _read_standalone_flag behandelt eine unparsebare Config wie eine fehlende und antwortet 'standalone'. Auf einem Lauf, der NICHT standalone ist, schalten sich damit drei Garantien gleichzeitig ab - das Phase-Gate wird uebersprungen, --force verlangt keinen aufgezeichneten Grund mehr, und es wird kein validation_overrides[]-Eintrag geschrieben; die FR-01.01-Evidenzregel hoert also genau in dem degradierten Zustand auf zu gelten, in dem Evidenz zaehlt. title: IT-7 Die Review-Maschinerie schliesst ihren Kreis: totes Verdict blockt ewig, Sub-Iterates ohne Cascade
detail: KONSOLIDIERT trg-9e2ce202 + trg-71d7a4fa. ZWEI Iterates, ein Anker. 7a ZUERST und klein - trg-9e2ce202: wenn der Tier-3-Reviewer fail-closed geht (Diff-Truncation, unparsebare Modellantwort), postet er CHANGES_REQUESTED. Ein spaeterer erfolgreicher Lauf postet nur COMMENTED, was ein CHANGES_REQUESTED in GitHub NICHT aufhebt. reviewDecision bleibt CHANGES_REQUESTED bei null unaufgeloesten Threads, also ist mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, obwohl jeder Required Check gruen und der Branch aktuell ist. Beobachtet an PR #446: fuenf veraltete CHANGES_REQUESTED aus ueberholten Commits (bdd788a1, 720f0de8, 75e538c1, 2ea75602, 1086cf4e) ueberlebten den Fix in #461 und sechs saubere Reviews; der PR mergte erst, nachdem alle fuenf von Hand dismissed wurden. Das Symptom ist STILLE - kein roter Check, kein offener Thread, nichts benennt den Blocker - was mehrere Diagnoserunden gekostet hat. Fixrichtung: bei erfolgreichem Abschluss die EIGENEN vorherigen CHANGES_REQUESTED desselben Bots dismissen. SCHWANZ: das gevendorte pr_review im WebUI-Repo braucht denselben Fix. 7b - trg-71d7a4fa: der sub-iterate-runner hat kein Agent-Tool und delegiert die interne Cascade an den Kampagnen-Orchestrator, aber die autonome Schleife in campaign-mode.md 3a-3i hat KEINEN Schritt, der sie spawnt, und das Fenster, das die alte Prosa beschrieb, ist unmoeglich: der Orchestrator blockiert bei 3d auf dem terminalen DONE-Marker, der erst nach F6-Commit und Push kommt. spec-reviewer (HARD-GATE) und doubt-reviewer laufen also fuer runner-gebaute Sub-Iterates nie und haben keinen externen Ersatz. Verschachteltes Spawnen ist am 2026-07-28 GEMESSEN (nested child lieferte NESTED_OK), damit ist die 3f-bis-State-Machine vermutlich unnoetig - der einfache Fix ist Agent in die tools:-Frontmatter von agents/sub-iterate-runner.md, sodass der Runner seine Cascade VOR dem eigenen Commit spawnt. OFFEN bleibt nur ADR-029s eigentlicher Einwand: TOKEN-KOSTEN, nicht Machbarkeit - abzuwaegen gegen die Kosten, Kampagnen-Sub-Iterates ohne Spec-Compliance-Gate auszuliefern. VORAUSSETZUNG fuer REQ3.04/05/06 und fuer IT-1-als-Kampagne. IT-0 muss sub-iterate-runner.md (479 Zeilen) vorher baselinen.

title: IT-8 Die lokale Entwicklungsschleife berichtet die Wahrheit (2 von 3 sind Dismiss-Kandidaten)
detail: KONSOLIDIERT trg-ecddb31f + trg-410ef2a6 + trg-c6e75011. Drei Faelle, in denen das Dev-Setup dem Entwickler etwas Falsches sagt. ZWEI davon sind Dismiss-Kandidaten - ERST MESSEN, dann bauen. (1) trg-ecddb31f, der eigentliche Inhalt: update-marketplace.sh schreibt in das Versionsverzeichnis aus ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json, waehrend check_plugin_cache_sync.py den Cache gegen Repo-HEAD vergleicht. Ist die plugin.json-Version im Repo weiter als die installierte, widersprechen sich beide: der Sync meldet 'up to date', der strikte Checker meldet Drift mit Dateien im Repo und nicht im Cache. Beobachtet fuer shipwright-test. Entweder der Sync gleicht den installierten Pin mit dem Repo-Manifest ab, oder der Checker vergleicht gegen die installierte Version - so wie es ist, ist ein echt un-gesyncter Plugin nicht von einem Versions-Mismatch zu unterscheiden. (2) trg-410ef2a6 (f0-race shipwright-run): Vorpruefung 2026-07-28 - die Ursache war ein Windows-os.replace-Bug in atomic_write.py, gefixt in iterate-2026-07-27-run-unit-parallel-race; die Karte wurde am 2026-07-28 NEU gefeuert. Suite einmal parallel messen: gruen -> dismissen, rot -> echte neue Race, dann bleibt sie. Dahinter steckt die eigentliche Luecke: der F0-Runner kann Race und Flake nicht unterscheiden. (3) trg-c6e75011: Vorpruefung 2026-07-28 - plugins/shipwright-security/.shipwright/ EXISTIERT NICHT MEHR, PR #474 hat den Leak gefixt. Unit einmal laufen lassen; sauber -> dismissen. WENN BEIDE DISMISSES GREIFEN, schrumpft dieser Anker auf einen Einzeiler - dann an IT-0 anhaengen statt eigener Iterate. Brief: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-triage-consolidation.md

title: IT-9 Host-Checks: Gates die nichts gaten, das Verdict-Label, und kein CI-Job auf Windows
detail: SUPERSEDES trg-c7e5835b (das seinerseits trg-2f9865fb supersedete), KONSOLIDIERT zusaetzlich trg-9862202d + trg-80e3b3cd. OWNS weiterhin: alles unter dem workflows-Verzeichnis, die ausgelieferten Workflow-Templates und den must-pass-Ableitungshelfer. Keine andere Karte darf eine Workflow-Datei anfassen - deshalb ist die Zuordnung der beiden neuen Punkte erzwungen, nicht gewaehlt. Teil 1 ist als PR #475 gelandet. RESTPUNKTE der Ursprungskarte: (1) der in jedes onboardete Projekt gescaffoldete Review-Workflow UEBERSPRINGT eine Aenderung ab einer Groessenschwelle, also passieren die groessten Aenderungen ungeprueft, waehrend der Reviewer des Frameworks in derselben Lage fail-closed geht - den ausgelieferten ebenso fail-closed machen. (2) eine Aenderung aus einer eigenen Kopie des Projekts bekommt gar kein Modell-Review, weil der Host solchen Laeufen Credentials vorenthaelt; dokumentiert sicherer Weg ist zweistufig ueber ein Artefakt. (4) Verdict dort labeln, wo ein Mensch es zuerst sieht: das Security-Gate feuert nur auf der schwersten Klasse und meldet ein blankes 'pass', waehrend Dutzende high-Befunde offen sind; die Evidenzseite traegt die ehrliche Form bereits. (5) scripts/verify_contract_surface.py ist der einzige Check, der liest was ein Konsument TATSAECHLICH holt - und ist an nichts verdrahtet. NEU trg-9862202d (nach Teil 2): zwei Checks laufen auf jedem PR, melden ein Ergebnis und halten nichts auf - 'Empirical calibration (real OSS repos)' und 'Prepare review request'. Ruleset-Aenderung bei GitHub, kein Code. LANDMINE: ein Check, der NICHT auf jedem PR laeuft, blockiert als Required JEDEN PR fuer immer; 'Prepare review request' laeuft verifiziert immer, 'Empirical calibration' NICHT verifiziert - grade-empirical.yml erst lesen. Danach dasselbe im WebUI-Repo. NEU trg-80e3b3cd: KEIN CI-Job laeuft auf Windows, jeder Workflow ist ubuntu-latest. Ein Windows-only-Defekt ist bereits gruen auf main gelandet (97392eea, shipwright-changelog: ein Kindprozess kodiert stderr mit dem Locale-Codec, jeder Leser dekodiert utf-8) und wurde nur gefunden, weil jemand lokal auf Windows testete; und Windows-Fixes werden von plattform-gegateten Tests 'verifiziert', die CI immer skippt. Muss hierher, weil es eine Workflow-Datei ist. Brief: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-triage-consolidation.md

title: REQ3.04 [CAMPAIGN AUTONOM] Mechanik Monorepo plus der Spec-Reader (supersedes trg-7085d783)
detail: SUPERSEDES trg-7085d783, KONSOLIDIERT zusaetzlich trg-1d7d91d0 + trg-2ea0b99a + trg-8bf97fd4. Owner-Entscheidung 2026-07-28: das frueher als IT-4 vorgeschlagene Buendel wird KEIN eigener Anker, sondern Vorarbeit dieser Karte - beide fassen AC-Parsing an, parallel geht nicht. UNVERAENDERT: Phase 3, AUTONOME Kampagne. Sub-Iterates Evidenzkette (CI regeneriert das Manifest, es muss matchen), AC-Identitaet, Manifest v4, Test-Backfill, AC-Test-Bindung, Layers-Promotion, KEYSTONE-GATE (verhaltensaenderndes PR muss geaenderte ACs benennen und gebundene Tests gruen in CI haben), Zubringer-Checks, Rewritability-Link, Track R diff-scoped. VORAUSSETZUNG: IT-7b - ohne Agent-Tool laeuft fuer Sub-Iterates dieser Kampagne kein spec-reviewer. NEU ALS VORARBEIT trg-1d7d91d0: check_s5_fr_coherence meldet 19 von 19 Requirements dieses Repos als 'ohne Beschreibung und ohne Acceptance Criteria' - alle falsch. Der geteilte spec_parser kennt nur FR-Koerper mit dem Fettlabel 'Acceptance Criteria:', waehrend /shipwright-project UND /shipwright-adopt tatsaechlich '### FR-XX.YY - Titel' mit blanken Bullets ausliefern. Ein AC-Identitaets-Manifest auf einem Parser zu bauen, der die eigene Ausgabeform nicht liest, ist der falsche Boden. Der Befund ist heute eine nicht-blockierende Warnung, also war der Laerm unsichtbar statt schaedlich - aber das preventive Phase-Quality-Gate etabliert damit NICHTS ueber AC-Abdeckung. NEU trg-2ea0b99a: das Cross-Layer-Coverage-Gate keyt 'hat sich Verhalten geaendert?' auf eine geaenderte FR-TABELLENZEILE, waehrend die geltende Kampagnenregel Kriterien UNTER einer unveraenderten Zeile hinzufuegt. Beobachtet an PR #446: vier in FR-01.06 geminzte Kriterien und 95 neue Tests, und das Gate konnte beides nicht verbinden. Der Fehler ist gutartig ('ich weiss es nicht' statt 'das ist in Ordnung'), feuert aber bei JEDEM kriterien-mintenden Iterate und wird so zu Routinelaerm, den ein Mensch durchwinkt - genau das Versagen, gegen das FR-01.06 gerade gehaertet wurde. Fixrichtung: hinzugefuegte oder geaenderte (E)-Kriterien unter einer FR-Ueberschrift als Verhaltensaenderung behandeln. NEU UND ABSPALTBAR trg-8bf97fd4 (S2b, Tail von Kampagnenschritt S2, Voraussetzung S2 gemergt): ~10 Call-Site-Entscheidungen zur Requirement-Discovery. Aus dem eingefrorenen Korpus gemessen - mindestens 10 der 15 Walks laufen in versteckte Verzeichnisse, mindestens 7 in das iterate-Verzeichnis, 2 steigen rekursiv ab, 4 crashen wenn der Planning-Pfad eine Datei ist, und 2 sortieren gar nicht, sodass das getroffene Dokument von der Dateisystem-Reihenfolge abhaengt; das sind Untergrenzen. title: Stamp the C3 event anchor in the iterate ledger writer
detail: Canon C3 consults its clock only where a completion carries an event anchor. append_iterate_entry.py deliberately stamps none, so the same-phase clock check never runs for the iterate phase. The bound is safe today (the ledger is one file per run id, so a stale marker names a different run and the run-id branch catches it) and is recorded in lib/phase_history.py above COMPLETION_PRODUCER, in handoff_phase_canon.py's Known bounds, in the tool's own docstring, and asserted by test_completion_writers.py. It was left undone because the 5 lines would push a grandfathered file past its bloat baseline, needing a bloat-exception ADR on a file already slated for a split. When that split happens: stamp event_at the way append_phase_history.py does, then delete the KNOWN BOUND paragraph and flip the bound-assertion in test_completion_writers.py.

title: A grade snapshot cannot say whether the graded content matches the commit it names (dirty flag built, then withdrawn)
detail: Root cause, unfixed by design: grade and score are computed from the WORKING tree while lineage and base can only be derived from COMMITTED state, and nothing reconciles them. On the main-lineage path merge-base(HEAD,default) equals HEAD, so a pre-commit regen stamps the commit it has not made yet - the same limitation for which recording commit was rejected. A dirty flag was built for this and WITHDRAWN before shipping after two review rounds. Why the obvious implementation fails: every automatic producer writes TRACKED files before the snapshot is emitted, so measuring dirtiness at emit time reads true on a pristine tree. Measured: (1) update_compliance rewrites its own 5-7 tracked artifacts before the dashboard branch emits; (2) the run-orchestrator appends a phase_completed event to the tracked event log, then regenerates - reproduced end to end, dirty true with zero uncommitted source; (3) finalize_iterate records work_completed before calling the regen; (4) the sbom and test-evidence triage emitters write triage.jsonl before the dashboard branch. An exclusion list was attempted and rejected in review: pinning it to DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS is structurally wrong because test_derived_snapshots asserts the event log and triage.jsonl are NOT in that registry, and the two registries answer different questions. The correct design is to CAPTURE dirtiness before the producer starts writing and pass it in, not to measure after - the seam source_state.py already models with a run-id-primary stamp. Also note source_state_git.resolve_git_state already solved the sibling problem of re-expressing exclusions relative to the repo root; any retry must reuse it rather than re-copy it. Consumer impact meanwhile: docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md rule 5 tells readers to treat base as the commit a measurement was taken NEAR, not the commit the score describes.

title: [f0] shipwright-run failed in parallel and passed alone - race or flaky test
detail:
shipwright-run: red in parallel (rc 1), GREEN alone (rc 0). It is NOT xdist-allowlisted, so this is inter-unit pollution or an unreliable test.

The F0 suite runner ran this unit twice. With every unit running side by side it reported a pytest test failure (exit 1). Re-run ALONE - after the pool drained, without xdist, in a clean temp dir - it PASSED (exit 0). That alone-run verdict is authoritative, so the gate was NOT stopped.

The runner cannot tell which of these it is:
  - a race between concurrently running units (shared state, ports, temp files, the shared working tree), or
  - a test that fails intermittently on its own.
Both are real defects; only measurement separates them.

Reproduce the unit exactly as the runner re-ran it (expect GREEN):
  cd plugins/shipwright-run && uv run --with pytest --with pytest-mock pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
Reproduce the whole suite in parallel (expect the intermittent red):
  uv run shared/scripts/tools/run_test_suite.py --project-root 'C:\01_Development\shipwright\.worktrees\grade-snapshot-honest-subject' --run-id iterate-2026-07-28-grade-snapshot-honest-subject

The failing output stayed in that run's F0 console and is deliberately not copied here.

This entry is never closed automatically: one clean parallel run is not evidence the race is gone. Close it when the unit is fixed, or dismiss it deliberately.
